aberrant spectres: Fetid, vile ghosts, those. The smell alone will floor you.
Wear a nosepeg, or their stink will paralyse you where you stand.
abyssal demons: They're not really of this realm, and they move quick to trap you.
Nasty things. They'll be behind you before you've turned round.
adamant dragons: Their metal bolts sap your health. Watch for the poison bombs too.
They'll spend their own health to fire bolts at you. Mind the poison.
ankou: Powerful blows, poor defences. Kill them quick, before they hit you.
Skeletal ghosts. The quicker you finish them, the less you'll take.
aquanites: Everything they do runs through that lure. A well timed cut severs it.
Their hides shrug off a slash, but the lure doesn't.
araxxor: A very venomous spider. Bring something against the venom.
Venom, mostly. Bring something for it or you'll not last.
araxytes: Tips? For those? Try not to die.
aviansies: Icy dungeons of the north. Melee won't reach them, so magic or ranged.
Bird-like things, and out of reach of a blade. Magic or ranged.
bandits: They band together against enemies such as yourself.
Bandits stick together, you'll find. You're what they do it for.
banshees: That piercing scream will shock you senseless without earmuffs.
Got earmuffs? You'll want them before the screaming starts.
barrows brothers: Six brothers, each with his own tricks. Kill whichever you like.
Any of the brothers will do. Each has a trick, mind.
basilisks: Got a mirror shield? Their gaze paralyses, same as a cockatrice.
Don't meet their eyes without a mirror shield.
bats: Rarely on the ground, so you fight them in the air. Hard with a blade.
They don't come down to you, so melee won't be easy.
bears: Tough creatures and fierce fighters. Watch out for the claws.
Mind the claws. Fierce fighters, bears.
birds: Not the brightest, but watch the sharp stabbing beak.
Birds aren't clever, but the beak is sharp enough.
black demons: A demonbane weapon makes short work of even the big demons.
Have you a demonbane weapon? Even a black demon goes down fast to one.
black dragons: The strongest dragons, and fierce. Mind the fiery breath.
Fancy a tougher foe? The brutal sort live in the Kourend Catacombs.
black knights: All that black armour of theirs makes them easy pickings for magic.
They favour black armour, which does nothing against a spell.
bloodveld: That long rasping tongue goes straight through armour, so mind it.
Strange demonic things. The tongue's magical, it pierces plate.
blue dragons: Thick scales and fiery breath. Stab, or heavy bolts, to get through.
A stabbing weapon or heavy bolts. That's what pierces those scales.
brine rats: You'll find them in caves near the sea. Hairless and bad-tempered.
Bad-tempered, hairless and generally unfriendly. Caves by the sea.
bronze dragons: The weakest of the metal dragons, but those scales beat bronze plate.
Don't think bronze means soft. The scales are nothing like the armour.
brutal black dragons: Viler than the ordinary black sort. Melee, magic and dragonfire.
The Kourend Catacombs, and they fight with everything they have.
callisto: Roams the Wilderness. His roar knocks you flat, prayer or no prayer.
Prayer won't stop him, and the roar will have you off your feet.
catablepon: Mythical cow-like things, and magical. Beware the weakening glare.
Don't let them glare at you. It saps the strength out of your arms.
cave bugs: Like cave crawlers, only smaller and easier to squish.
Easier to squish than a crawler, but still fond of your plants.
cave crawlers: Mind the barbed tongue, or you'll be poisoned.
Small and fast, and they like to lie in ambush.
cave horrors: Under Mos Le'Harmless. You'll want a witchwood icon round your neck.
Have you a witchwood icon? You'll get nowhere with them without one.
cave kraken: They barely feel an arrow or a blade, so try magic.
Lakes under the ground, north of Eagles' Peak. Take your spellbook.
cave slimes: Lesser cousins of jellies, but often poisonous all the same.
Don't be fooled by a slime. They're often poisonous.
cerberus: Her chamber's off Taverley dungeon. All three styles, so be prepared.
She attacks every way there is. Prepare for all of them.
chaos druids: Some can harm you with spells, or teleport you back if you run.
Druids gone to evil. Run from one and it may pull you straight back.
cockatrice: Their gaze paralyses, same as a basilisk. Take a mirror shield.
Don't go looking one in the eye without a mirror shield.
commander zilyana: In the God Wars Dungeon. She leans heavily on magic.
Expect magic, and plenty of it. God Wars Dungeon.
cows: Bigger than you, aren't they? They hit hard but they're slow to react.
They're slow to react, but when they do hit, it's a cow hitting you.
crabs: They don't hit hard, but they take a while to kill.
All over Gielinor, crabs. Weak hitters, slow to die.
crawling hands: Undead severed hands. Fast, dexterous, and they claw.
Severed hands, and still clawing. Quick ones, too.
crazy archaeologists: Wilderness or Fossil Island. Dodge the exploding books.
They throw books that explode and bounce about. Step out of the way.
crocodiles: Bring a stabbing weapon to puncture those thick scaly hides.
Near water, naturally. Something that stabs, for the hide.
custodian stalkers: They've a dangerous bleed magic, so be ready to hold your ground.
Hold your ground against them. That bleed of theirs is magic.
dagannoth: Very aggressive sea creatures. Caves near sea water, usually.
Look in caves near the sea. They'll come at you, no need to look hard.
dagannoth kings: Three kings in the cave below Waterbirth. Kill whichever you like.
Any of the three kings will do. Below Waterbirth Island.
dark beasts: Big dog-like brutes. All that muscle shrugs off a crushing weapon.
Don't bring anything blunt. Their muscle just soaks it up.
dark warriors: They wear protective armour. Crush them, or try magic instead.
Armoured, so something blunt if you're fighting close, or else magic.
deranged archaeologist: Fossil Island, that one. Dodge the exploding books.
He throws books that explode and bounce about. Step out of the way.
dogs: Much like wolves. Pack creatures, so they'll hunt you in a group.
Where there's one dog there's the pack, so expect company.
drakes: Depths of the Karuulm dungeon. Boots of stone for the heat, mind.
Not quick on your feet? Take an anti-dragon shield as well.
duke sucellus: A demonic horror under Ghorrock. Weaken him before you fight him.
Don't go at him head on. Find a way to weaken him first.
dust devils: They'll blind you with dust and ash. Wear a facemask.
Facemask on, or they'll blow sand and ash straight in your eyes.
dwarves: Small but tough, and a pickaxe goes through armour nicely.
Miners, mostly, and a pickaxe pierces plate just as well as rock.
earth warriors: A kind of earth elemental. Grind them to dust with something blunt.
Something blunt, and grind them to dust.
elves: Quick, agile and vicious. They favour bows and polearms.
Expect bows and polearms, and expect them to be quick about it.
ents: Walking tree-folk. Bring a hatchet to chop the wood once they're down.
Have you a hatchet? There's good wood in an ent once it's slain.
fever spiders: Wear slayer gloves, unless you fancy catching spider fever.
Giant spiders, and they carry the fever, so keep your gloves on.
fire giants: Little magic in them, like all giants, and weak to water spells.
Water spells. Giants have no magic to speak of, and these hate water.
fleshcrawlers: Scavengers. They'll eat you, and anyone else, given the chance.
They'll eat you if you let them. Don't let them.
fossil island wyverns: Dangerous in several ways. Shield yourself from that icy breath.
Icy breath, so you'll want an elemental shield if you mean to survive.
frost dragons: Beneath the island of Grimstone. Dragonfire protection is a must.
Thick scales and icy breath. Don't go without dragonfire protection.
gargoyles: Fight them to near death, then break them apart with a rock hammer.
Winged stone, so they don't die. You smash them with a rock hammer.
general graardor: In the God Wars Dungeon. Melee and ranged, nothing clever.
He hits you, or he throws things at you. No magic in him.
ghosts: Undead, so magic's your best bet. Wind spells, even better.
Use magic on the undead. Wind spells, if you have them.
ghouls: Not undead, whatever they look like, and cowards. They run if losing.
Tougher than they look, but cowardly. Lose patience and they'll run.
goblins: Mostly just annoying, but mind the spears some of them carry.
They can be vicious, for goblins. Watch the ones with spears.
goraks: On another plane, reached by fairy ring. Their touch drains you.
Extremely aggressive, and their touch saps your skills and health.
greater demons: Demons are weak to water spells. Not the strongest, still dangerous.
Water spells, as with any demon. Don't take them lightly, though.
green dragons: Thick scales and fiery breath. Something against dragonfire, mind.
Can you stay out of reach? If not, bring something against dragonfire.
gryphons: They kill by dropping their prey, so be too heavy to lift.
Native to the Great Conch. Be too heavy for them to carry off.
harpie bug swarms: Pesky things, hard to hit. A lit bug lantern will distract them.
Is your bug lantern lit? They can't help but stare at it.
hellhounds: Half dog, half demon. A fierce bite, but a demon's weaknesses.
Treat them as demons. The bite is a dog's, but the weaknesses aren't.
hill giants: They wield big weapons. Learn to tell which kind and act accordingly.
Look at what the giant is holding before you decide how to fight it.
hobgoblins: The ones with spears are trained. Want it easier? Fight the unarmed.
A hobgoblin with a spear has been trained. Pick the unarmed ones.
hydras: Boots of stone for the heat. They spit poison and fight every way.
Depths of the Karuulm dungeon. Melee, ranged, magic and poison.
ice giants: Little magic in them, like all giants, and weak to fire spells.
Fire spells. Giants have no magic to speak of, and these melt.
ice warriors: Ice elementals. Shatter them with something blunt, or melt them.
Shatter or melt, your choice. Blunt weapons or fire.
icefiends: Ice and freezing rock, quick and agile, but weak to fire spells.
Quick little things of ice. Fire spells melt them.
infernal mages: Dangerous spell users. Beware their magic and go properly prepared.
Go properly prepared. Their spells are nothing to laugh at.
iron dragons: Among the weaker metal dragons, but those scales beat any iron plate.
Don't think iron means soft. Their scales are nothing like the armour.
jellies: Nasty gelatinous cubes. Their acid goes straight through armour.
They absorb whatever they touch, and the acid ignores your plate.
jungle horrors: All over Mos Le'Harmless. Strong and aggressive, so watch yourself.
Strong, aggressive, and all over Mos Le'Harmless. No need to look.
k'ril tsutsaroth: In the God Wars Dungeon. Poisonous, and he hits through prayer.
Prayer won't save you from him entirely. Nor will it stop the poison.
kalphites: Hives under the desert sands. Crush the chitin, and mind the poison.
Big insects. Something blunt cracks the shell. The large ones poison.
killerwatts: Touch one and all that stored energy goes through your boots.
Insulated boots, or you'll get a shock the moment you touch one.
kree'arra: Melee won't touch a flying thing, bar a halberd. Bring a grapple.
You'll need a grappling hook to get in. Then magic or ranged.
kurask: Thick hides. Leaf-bladed weapons, broad arrows or magic dart.
Nothing ordinary gets through. Leaf-bladed, broad or magic dart.
lava dragons: A volcanic bit of the Wilderness. The gods think well of their bones.
Wilderness dragons. The bones make a fine offering, if you get out.
lesser demons: Demons are weak to magic. Relatively weak, these, but still dangerous.
Magic, as with any demon. Lesser doesn't mean harmless.
lesser nagua: Well versed in magic, but reckless. Get in close with a blade.
They fight recklessly, so they're wide open to melee.
lizardmen: A poisonous bite, and don't let the shamans jump on your head.
The shamans have peculiar tricks. Jumping on your head is one of them.
lizards: The desert ones need a dousing of freezing water to finish them.
For those at Mount Karuulm, boots of stone or you'll burn your feet.
magic axes: A mind of their own. Magic or a slashing blade works a little better.
Axes with a mind of their own. Slash at them, or use magic.
mammoths: Big and not very smart. Trap them on the terrain and kill from afar.
They plod about the Wilderness. Get something between you and shoot.
metal dragons: Bronze to rune, the latter deadlier. Don't forget the dragon breath.
Metal or not, they still breathe fire. Don't forget that.
minotaurs: Large manlike creatures. Be careful of the horns.
Mind the horns. That's the whole of my advice on minotaurs.
mithril dragons: Magic or a stabbing weapon. Nothing else does much to them.
Stab or cast. Anything else just bounces off the mithril.
mogres: Ogres of the water, often taken for mudskippers. Blast them out.
They won't leave the water unless you use a fishing explosive.
molanisks: Deep caves below ground. The goblins ring some sort of bell at them.
I hear the goblins deal with theirs using a bell of some sort.
monkeys: Agile and fairly fast. Learn to anticipate their movements.
Tricky things, monkeys. Work out where they'll be, not where they are.
moss giants: Little magic in them, like all giants, and weak to fire spells.
Fire spells. Giants have no magic to speak of, and moss burns.
mutated zygomites: They regenerate fast, so finish them off with fungicide.
Hard to destroy. Fungicide at the end, or they just grow back.
nechryael: Demons of decay. Their winged minions ignore prayer, so wear plate.
The winged things they summon ignore prayer. Wear thick armour.
ogres: Brutal things with big clubs and maces. They attack without warning.
No warning with an ogre. The club just comes down.
otherworldly beings: Ethereal things, so magic is what hurts them.
Not quite of this world, so use magic on them.
pirates: Near the sea, naturally. They like collecting coins, and other things.
Look near the sea. Watch your purse while you're at it.
pyrefiends: Fire and molten rock, quick and agile, and weak to water spells.
Quick little things of fire. Water spells put them out.
rats: Everyday pests, but they get fairly big. Mind the teeth.
Some of them get very big. The teeth get bigger with them.
red dragons: Very powerful, stronger than most dragons. Mind the fiery breath.
Stronger than most of their kind, and the breath is as fiery as any.
revenants: Deepest cavern of Forinthry. A charged bracelet keeps them off you.
All three styles. A charged revenant bracelet stops the lot.
rockslugs: Fight them to near death, then finish them off with salt.
Have you salt on you? That's the only way to finish a rockslug.
rogues: Lawless places, the deep Wilderness. Very protective of their loot.
They guard their loot jealously. Find them where there's no law.
rune dragons: They drain you to heal themselves. Protective footwear for the shocks.
Shocking attacks, those. Keep clear of them, or wear the right boots.
sand crabs: Piles of sand on the Hosidius beaches. Weak hitters, slow to kill.
Want a harder one? The king sand crabs are in the Kourend Catacombs.
sarachnis: Forthos Dungeon. Mother of the temple spiders, don't get overwhelmed.
Where she is, her brood is. Don't let them pile on.
scabarites: Insectoids beyond the Kharidian desert. Don't fall in a pitfall trap.
Fall in one of their pits and you'll be overwhelmed before you're out.
scorpia: Her minions fill the cave and defend her. Expect to be poisoned.
Expect to be poisoned, and expect her brood to get in the way.
scorpions: Almost always poisonous. That carapace resists crush and stab.
Slash at them. Crushing or stabbing just bounces off the shell.
sea snakes: The venom's worse in the big ones. Keep an eye on your health.
Long and slithery, with a venomous bite. The large ones are the worst.
shades: Undead, so magic's your best bet. You'll find them at Mort'ton.
Mort'ton is where they are. Use magic, as with any undead.
shadow warriors: Spectral plate armour. Crush weapons and magic give them trouble.
Dark and mysterious, and armoured. Something blunt, or a spell.
skeletal wyverns: Arrows slip right through them. Shield yourself from the icy breath.
Extremely dangerous, and arrows are no use. Elemental shielding, mind.
skeletons: Undead, so magic. There's a spell made specially for them.
Use magic on the undead. There's even a spell just for it.
smoke devils: Slow and lumbering, but the gas is noxious. Facemask on first.
You'll not get anywhere near them without a facemask.
sourhogs: They spit acid when provoked. Reinforced goggles, for your eyes.
Acid spit, so wear your reinforced goggles.
spiders: Often poisonous, and many of them are camouflaged too.
Look carefully. Half of them you won't see until they bite.
spiritual creatures: Icy caverns near Trollheim. In a god's colours, his lot let you be.
Each serves a god. Dress in his colours and you'll avoid a fight.
steel dragons: Dangerous metal dragons. Those scales beat any steel plate.
Don't think steel means ordinary. The scales beat any steel plate.
suqahs: Only on Lunar Isle. Melee and magic, and they drop hide and teeth.
Lunar Isle, and nowhere else. Worth it for the hide and teeth.
terror dogs: Tarn Razorlor's own hounds. Find him and you've found them.
Bad-tempered and generally unfriendly, and they go wherever Tarn goes.
the abyssal sire: It can pull you to itself, and the whole place fights for it.
It'll teleport you to it, and the cave itself is on its side.
the alchemical hydra: Many forms, poisonous and heavily armoured. Weaken it first, somehow.
Find a way to weaken it before you try to kill it. I don't know how.
the cave kraken boss: A cave north of the kraken lakes. Best fought with magic.
Magic, as with the little ones. Its cave is north of the lakes.
the chaos elemental: Deepest Wilderness. It teleports you and strips your gear at random.
It'll have your armour off you, and you somewhere else entirely.
the chaos fanatic: His magic ricochets about, but you can dodge it. He strips gear too.
Watch the spell bounce, and step out of its way. Mind your gear, too.
the giant mole: Dig the molehills in Falador Park. Bring a lantern he can't put out.
Take a lantern that won't go out. He'll try to put it out.
the grotesque guardians: Top of the Slayer Tower. Ring the bell, and mind they work as a pair.
Ring the bell when you're ready. There are two, and they work as one.
the kalphite queen: Bottom of a cave in the desert. Armour won't stop her ranged or magic.
Armour's no use against what she throws at you, so pray instead.
the king black dragon: Pull the lever in the Wilderness. Take an anti-fire shield.
An anti-fire shield, and I do mean it. The lever's in the Wilderness.
the leviathan: An ancient sea thing in the Scar. The Abyss left it weak to shadow.
Shadow spells, if you have them. The Abyss did something to it.
the maggot king: In Vampyrium. Weak to fire, and the more it burns the less it resists.
Set it alight. The longer it burns, the better your spells land.
the phantom muspah: Rumour puts it deep beneath Weiss. Powerful magic, so be prepared.
Whatever it is, it has powerful magic. Deep under Weiss, they say.
the shellbane gryphon: Be light enough not to be carried off, and wear a Tortugan shield.
A Tortugan shield, and don't be so light it can pick you up.
the thermonuclear smoke devil: A cave south of Castle Wars. It hits through prayer, so wear robes.
Prayer won't stop it. Wear magical armour instead.
the whisperer: A siren's nightmare under Ice Mountain. Don't fall for her tricks.
Deep under Ice Mountain. Whatever she shows you, don't believe it.
trolls: They regenerate fast, and resist magic, but fire gets through.
Fire. They heal quick and shrug off most spells, but not fire.
turoth: Thick hides. Leaf-bladed weapons, broad arrows or magic dart.
Nothing ordinary gets through. Leaf-bladed, broad or magic dart.
tzhaar: Under the Karamja volcano. Beware, they call their fellows for aid.
Fight one and you may end up fighting several. They call for aid.
tzkal-zuk: No advice I can give for that. Stay calm and trust yourself.
Stay calm. Your skills will do the rest, or nothing will.
tztok-jad: Many waves of tough monsters before him. Stock up on supplies.
Have you enough supplies? There's a lot to get through before Jad.
undead druids: Forthos Dungeon, under the ruin in Hosidius. Melee and strong magic.
They'll hit you with a staff or a spell, whichever's nearer.
vampyres: Extremely powerful. The Myreque have tools against them, if you ask.
Have you met the Myreque? They've been looking for ways to kill those.
vardorvis: An undead vampyre in the Stranglewood. Nimble, so be quick to react.
He uses the ground itself against you, so be quick to react.
venators: Only in Vampyrium, and only a weapon made for vampyres will slay them.
Bloodthirsty things. Bring whatever you'd bring against a vampyre.
venenatis: Lives in the Wilderness. Avoid her sticky webs!
Mind the webs. Sticky, and she knows it.
vet'ion: He dies only when beaten twice, and while his dogs stand he's immune.
Kill the dogs first, or nothing you do will touch him.
vorkath: The frozen island of Ungael. Anti-fire protection or you won't last.
You'll not last long without anti-fire protection, I promise you.
wall beasts: You'll only see the arms. Something sharp on your head stops the grab.
Wear something spiked on your head, or they'll grab you by it.
warped creatures: A dungeon east of the Poison Waste. You'll have to purify them first.
They can't be killed as they are. Purify them somehow first.
waterfiends: Under the Baxtorian Lake. Slash and stab do little, so go blunt.
Made of water, so a blade goes straight through. Bring a blunt weapon.
werewolves: Feral things. Strong, tough, with sharp claws and teeth.
Strong and tough, and all teeth and claws when they turn.
wolves: Pack animals, always in groups. Watch for the bite, it's nasty.
Never just the one wolf. Mind the bite.
wyrms: The regular sort are under Karuulm. Strykewyrms, the Charred Dungeon.
Draconic things. Both sorts live on Wyrmscraig, if you'd rather.
zombies: Undead, so magic. There's a spell made specially for them.
Use magic on the undead. There's even a spell just for it.
zulrah: Venomous, but learn his patterns and you'll dodge most of it.
He does the same things in the same order. Learn it and you'll live.

closers: compliment: Maybe me not eat you.
insult: Run away now, little one.
compliment|remark: I hope that's what you wanted.

openers: compliment|remark: Ah, 'tis a foine day to be sure!

closers: insult: Go away human, we busy.
I'm keeping an eye on you.
insult: Or I eat you instead!
insult|remark: Good luck. It is far from simple.
compliment|remark: How may I help you?

Welcome to {place} bank, {you}. Mind the queue.
Welcome to {place} bank, {you}. Do come in.

openers: What can I do yer for?
closers: compliment|remark: Mind the step on your way out.

openers: Have a look at my wares.
closers: compliment|remark: Do come by the shop.
insult|remark: Come back when you've coins.

compliment: Ye gods, that staff's a sliver of sun straight out of the desert.
insult: A {item}. I do hope someone showed you how it works.
Who exactly are you planning to point that great staff at?
sharp/insult: A staff worth a kingdom, and you carry it like a walking stick.
remark: Don't leave that {item} lying about, round here.
Does that staff glow all night, or can you get it to stop?
kid/compliment: Is that real? Can I have it when you die?
kid/remark: Whoa. What's that?
trader/compliment: Three coins for that {item}, my friend, and that's me being generous.
banker/remark: That staff's worth more than this branch holds, but do come in.
shady/remark: Nice {item}. Be a shame if it went missing.
guard/insult: That staff's a lot of weapon for market day, so keep it sheathed.
No trouble in town. I've seen what that thing costs.
heartland/compliment: Is that a {item}? Gadzooks. I'd have to sell the farm.

compliment: That's no farm tool. Whatever that reaps, it isn't corn.
insult: A scythe. Are you Death, or just the help?
Who's all that scythe for? Nobody round here's worth pointing it at.
sharp/insult: A scythe that size. Never once cut so much as a weed, I'll wager.
remark: Don't leave that {item} lying about, round here.
Mind the lanterns with that scythe, and the doorways, and me.
kid/compliment: Is that real? Can I have it when you die?
kid/remark: Is that scythe for farming, or just for scaring people?
trader/compliment: A scythe, my friend? I've a field wants doing, call it a trial run.
banker/remark: Mind the scythe near the counter, the paperwork alone...
shady/remark: Nice {item}. Be a shame if it went missing.
guard/insult: That scythe stays on your back till you're past the stalls.
No trouble in town. I've seen what that thing costs.
heartland/compliment: A scythe like that. Gadzooks. Harvest's not till autumn, you know.

compliment: Gadzooks, who grew that bow?
Your bow's bent! Oh. It's meant to be like that?
insult: A twisted bow. Hope your aim's straighter than it is.
All that bow, and the rabbits still get away, I'll bet.
sharp/insult: A bow worth a castle, and you hold it like a fishing rod.
remark: Don't leave that {item} lying about, round here.
A bow like that, the arrows must feel underdressed.
kid/compliment: Is that real? Can I have it when you die?
kid/remark: Did you sit on your bow or is it meant to be all bendy?
trader/compliment: That bow, my friend. I'd offer the shop, but you'd want the stock too.
banker/remark: A bow of that value walking about has me quite pale, so do come in.
shady/remark: Nice {item}. Be a shame if it went missing.
guard/insult: Unstring that bow before you go through the market, please.
No trouble in town. I've seen what that thing costs.
tzhaar/compliment: Bendy bow. Looks like nothing. Shoots like TzHaar-Xil. Rare JalYt.
tzhaar/remark: Twisted bow. JalYt pay a mountain of TokKul for that, they say.
tzhaar/insult: Bow is bent. Did JalYt sit on it? TzHaar-Hur can fix. For TokKul.
ogre/compliment: Bendy bow! Creature shoots da chompies from far. Clever creature.
ogre/insult: Bow's all twisted. Creature sat on it? Ogres sit on fings too.
ogre/remark: Dat bow is worth all da bright pretties, dey say. Ogre not see why.
gnome/compliment: Great Guthix, human, a twisted bow! Did it grow like that on the tree?
gnome/remark: A bow like a branch of the Grand Tree. Did you ask the tree first?
dwarf/compliment: A twisted bow. Not metal, but by Guthix, that's craftsmanship.
dwarf/insult: A mountain of gold for a bent bit of wood... humans.
fremennik/compliment: A bow like a twisted root. Sigli would hunt with that gladly.
fremennik/insult: A bent bow worth a fleet, and still the sagas prefer axes.
moon_clan/compliment: That bow was grown rather than made, and so were you, dear.
moon_clan/remark: Oh my, everyone who passes is thinking about that bow, and noisily.
tortugan/compliment: That bow bends like coral, and that is very fine.
tortugan/insult: Bent like driftwood. Humans will pay anything for a tool.
goblin/insult: Bendy bow. Human shoot from far away? Not run from battle, human!
goblin/remark: Bow all twisted. Human sit on it? Bentnoze sit on things.
goblin/compliment: Twisty bow. Shoot far. Shoot beardy-short-people from far. Good.
troll/insult: Bendy bow. Shoot from far away? Trolls chuck rocks from far too.
troll/remark: Twisted bow. Look like root. Root is troll name. Good name.
troll/compliment: Twisty bow. Shoot far. Trolls like far. Far is where rocks go.
barbarian/compliment: The swift arrow on the wind. Aitan would want a go with that bow.
barbarian/insult: A bow that bent? Hah! Did you win it or wrestle it?
barbarian/remark: Twisted bow. Fine for the wind. A sword for the longhall, mind.

compliment: Not a stitch on you. You're braver than I am, traveller.
Well, nobody can say you're hiding anything.
insult: Did you lose your clothes, or did they finally lose you?
Bit chilly to be dressed in nothing but confidence.
plain/insult: Put some clothes on! There are children about.
Starkers in the street and not even a blush on you!
sharp/insult: Dressed in nothing but your own good opinion, I see.
remark: Laundry day, is it?
Not even a vest, in this wind?
kid/insult: Mum! That one's got no clothes on!
Ewww! Put something on!
kid/remark: Why are you in your pants?
nan/remark: Put something on, dear! You'll catch your death like that.
vicar/insult: Trousers aren't required in the churchyard, friend, merely customary.
banker/remark: Clothing isn't required in the bank, though it is a courtesy.
toff/insult: Has the peasantry given up on trousers entirely, and nobody told one?
fremennik/compliment: Hah! No armour at all. A warrior's spirit, outerlander.
Hah! Bare as a newborn and walking tall, there is nerve in that.
No cloth, no steel. Only the arm. That is how Thorvald likes it.
pirate/remark: Arr, lost yer shirt at cards, did ye?
guard/insult: Oi! Clothes! This is a public thoroughfare!
This is a city, not a bathhouse, so find yourself a towel.
Trousers, or the cells, and I know which one's warmer.
guard/remark: Put something on or I'll have to write this down.
Don't make me write 'no trousers' in the log again.
gnome/insult: Not even a hat, human? Hats are the one thing you lot get right.
Not a stitch on and still slower than a gnome, how do you manage it?
rough/insult: Cor. Not a stitch. Ye'll frighten the sheep.
rough/remark: Blimey. Put something on before the cows see.
barkeep/insult: No shirt, no service. And I'm being generous about the rest.
barkeep/remark: Did you lose your clothes in my cellar? Shall I go and have a look?
dwarf/remark: No armour at all? By Guthix, I feel cold just looking.
Lost your armour? Any smith worth his beard could sort you out.
dwarf/insult: No armour, no beard. What exactly are you working with?
Nothing to judge the craftsmanship of, and that's a first for me.
fremennik/insult: Thorvald's trial is fought unarmoured. Not unclothed, outerlander.
Peer asks you to carry nothing. He did not mean your clothes.
A yak has more hide on it, and the yak did not choose that.
burgher/remark: No clothes? Even we've got clothes, just about.
tzhaar/insult: JalYt wear nothing? Soft skin, no armour. Lava will not be kind.
No clothes, JalYt. Leaking water and shame. Strange creature.
tzhaar/remark: JalYt has no shell. TzHaar born with ours. Is better way.
tzhaar/compliment: No armour, still walk into Mor Ul Rek. Brave JalYt. Or daft one.
ogre/insult: Creature wiv no skin on! Hur, hur. Saves da peeling.
ogre/remark: No clothes, creature? Easier for da cooking pot, me suppose.
ogre/compliment: Creature got no clothes. Goodly. Less to pick out of da teeth.
gnome/compliment: Kar! No armour at all? That's brave of you, human, big but brave.
gnome/remark: Even the gnomeball players wear shorts, human.
dwarf/compliment: No armour and no fear. By Guthix, that's one way to live.
fremennik/remark: The Longhall bouncer would have short words about that bare skin.
moon_clan/compliment: Nothing to hide inside or out, and how refreshing that is, dear.
You dream unclothed too, and I had a look, so that is consistent.
moon_clan/insult: Oh my. I read minds, dear. I never asked to read the rest.
Your thoughts are as bare as the rest of you, dear, and I did check.
moon_clan/remark: On the island we'd simply conjure a robe, so do try thinking of one.
tortugan/compliment: No shell, no clothes, and still at ease, which is confidence indeed.
We are born with shells, and you go without even a borrowed one.
tortugan/insult: We are born with shells. You seem to have mislaid yours.
Humans need a tool for everything. Clothes too, I had thought.
tortugan/remark: At sea, nobody minds. On land, people seem to mind a great deal.
goblin/insult: Human got no armour! Not red, not green, not brown. Not anything!
Skin armour. Green too much like skin, Bentnoze say. This is worse.
goblin/remark: No clothes, human? Even Grubfoot wear armour. Orange one, once.
goblin/compliment: Human fight naked? Not run from battle, even with no armour. Good.
troll/insult: Human got no shell on. Less crunchy. Trolls like less crunchy.
No metal clothes? Good. Red metal hurt troll teeth.
troll/remark: Human wear nothing. Troll wear nothing too. Troll got rock skin, mind.
troll/compliment: Skin only? Brave human. Rocks hurt skin. Me know, me chuck dem.
cat/remark: No fur, no clothes. How do you humans keep warm at all?
cat/insult: Bare skin and proud of it? Humans are odd creatures.
cat/compliment: No clothes for me to shed on, very sensible of you.
camel/remark: Bare skin in this sun. You'll be a different colour by dusk.
camel/insult: No hide, no hair, no shame. I'll look at the horizon instead.
camel/compliment: Going about with no hide at all is foolish, but it's brave too.
leprechaun/remark: Not a stitch on ye. 'Tis the compost ye'll be smellin' of next.
leprechaun/insult: Nay, I'll not be holdin' yer clothes, for ye've none to hold!
leprechaun/compliment: Daft, goin' about like that, but brave, and foine by me.
parrot/remark: Squawk! Not a feather on that one, not a feather!
parrot/insult: Put it away! Squawk! Put it away, put it away!
mos_pirate/remark: Not a stitch on ye. Did the Horrors get yer clothes?
mos_pirate/insult: Arr, put somethin' on. Even the powder monkey wears breeches.
mos_pirate/compliment: Bold as brass, goin' about bare like that, and I'll give ye that.
moon_clan_wary/insult: I read minds, not bodies, so do put something on.
They say outsiders are loud and unguarded. Here you are to prove it.
Nothing on, and when I looked, nothing within either.
moon_clan_wary/remark: We clothe ourselves by magic. You seem to have given up entirely.
moon_clan_wary/compliment: Nothing hidden, inside or out. Honest. I will grant you that much.
barbarian/insult: No clothes at all? Hah! Is this how city folk fight now?
Starkers in our village? Even Gunthor wears a helmet.
barbarian/remark: Not a stitch on. Brave, that. Or the longhall beer's been at you.
barbarian/compliment: Fighting in your skin! Ho ho! There's barbarian blood in you.

compliment: Blimey, you went into the Inferno for that cape?
Fair play. Nobody gets a cape like that by accident.
insult: Lovely cape. Shame about the rest of you.
sharp/insult: Sat in lava for a cape. The things some will do for attention.
remark: Takes a certain sort to sit in lava for fun.
My cousin went after a cape like that once and never came right since.
kid/compliment: Whoa, is that the lava one?!
Can I touch it? Is it still hot?
kid/insult: My dad says he could do that, but he can't even light the fire.
nan/remark: Lovely cape. Did your mother know you went in the lava?
fremennik/compliment: Hah! Walking through fire and keeping the cape earns my respect.
Into the Inferno and out again. That is a saga, not a story.
pirate/compliment: Through the Inferno, were ye? Arr, I'd have sailed round.
barkeep/compliment: Into the lava and back? That cape drinks free tonight.
tzhaar/compliment: Cape of lava. JalYt stood before TzKal-Zuk and walked out. Rare.
TzKal-Zuk hungers for memories. JalYt gave him none. TzHaar remember.
tzhaar/remark: Lava cape. TzHaar-Hur did not make that one. Inferno did.
That cape came from Inferno. Our old birthing pool. Went too deep.
tzhaar/insult: Champion of the Inferno. Still JalYt. Still leaking.
Lava cape on a JalYt. Lava should be more careful.
ogre/compliment: Lava cape! Red and burny! Bestest pretty me ever seen, creature.
ogre/insult: Creature wears lava and still looks like a snack. Hur, hur.
ogre/remark: Dat cape is dripping fire. Keep it off da chompy feathers.
heartland/compliment: That cape. You're proper hard, you are.
heartland/insult: Infernal cape, is it? Bit flash for popping to the shops.
gnome/compliment: An infernal cape! Megal! You went into the Inferno and came out!
gnome/insult: Down into the Inferno and back, and still slow up a ladder, humans!
gnome/remark: That cape looks heavy, human. Even for one of the big folk.
dwarf/compliment: An infernal cape. By Guthix. That's hotter than any forge I've seen.
dwarf/remark: Lava-born, that cape. Even the Consortium can't buy one.
fremennik/remark: Olaf would sing of that cape, badly, and at great length.
moon_clan/compliment: That cape came from a place worse than any dream, and still you woke.
moon_clan/insult: Oh my. That cape is very warm. So is your opinion of it, dear.
tortugan/compliment: A cape from the deep fire... a gryphon would think twice, or once.
tortugan/remark: A cape from the deep fire, so they say. We keep to the deep water.
goblin/compliment: Lava cape! Very red! Thorobshuun red! Human mighty warrior.
goblin/insult: Cape of fire. Human still ugly behind it. Fire not help.
goblin/remark: Human cape is burning. Mudknuckles cooking look like that.
troll/compliment: Cape of lava! Trolls scared of fire. Human not. Human scary.
troll/insult: Fire cape very red. Me still not scared. Me little bit scared.
troll/remark: Cape burning. Human walk around burning. Humans strange.
barbarian/compliment: A cape of living fire! There's a saga in that cape and no mistake.
barbarian/insult: Lava on your back and still you walk like city folk.
barbarian/remark: That cape's burning. Mind the beer barrels.

compliment: Ye gods! Is that a real {item} on your head?
That {item} is worth more than this whole town.
insult: A paper hat worth a castle. Gielinor's a funny old place.
Wearing a {item} round here? You're either brave or daft.
plain/insult: That {item}'s out of a cracker, surely.
trader/compliment: Swap you that hat for a cabbage, and that's my final offer.
kid/compliment: Is that a crown?
Can I have your hat?
kid/insult: It's a paper hat. My nan's got loads.
shady/remark: Lovely hat. Plenty of dark alleys between here and the bank.
toff/insult: One's grandfather had one of those hats, and he had the face for it.
pirate/compliment: Arr, a hat worth more than me ship, so mind it in the harbour.
barkeep/remark: A hat like that, the Party Room'll want you.
burgher/remark: Funny paper hat, that. Did you lose a bet or something?
heartland/remark: There's light fingers about Lumbridge, so mind that {item}.
Wouldn't fancy walking that past Edgeville.
tzhaar/compliment: Paper hat worth more than all your armour, they say. Funny JalYt.
tzhaar/insult: Paper hat in city of fire. Silly JalYt. Very silly.
tzhaar/remark: Paper hat. Hold it away from lava. Paper burns. JalYt too, but slower.
ogre/compliment: Pretty paper hat! Bright pretty! Give it to ogre. Ogre asked nice.
ogre/insult: Paper hat. Hur, hur. Creature wearing its own lunch wrapper.
ogre/remark: Dat hat is worth lots, dey say. Ogre can't eat it. So, no.
gnome/compliment: A paper hat worth a kingdom. Humans are a mystery, and a marvel.
gnome/insult: A {item}? Kar, that'd blow right off the moment a glider took off.
dwarf/compliment: Mind that {item}. They say it's worth more than a Consortium seat.
dwarf/insult: A {item}? Not forged or mined or earned, just old.
dwarf/remark: Paper, worth a mountain of gold. By Guthix, I'll never understand.
fremennik/compliment: A paper hat worth a fleet. The sagas would not believe it.
fremennik/insult: A paper hat. The sea would have it off you in a breath.
moon_clan/compliment: Only a dreamer would wear a paper hat worth a kingdom, which is good.
moon_clan/remark: Oh my, half the street is thinking about your hat, and loudly.
tortugan/compliment: A paper hat worth so much, and you keep it dry, the hard part.
tortugan/insult: Paper, at sea? That hat would last one wave, human.
goblin/compliment: Paper hat! Pretty colour! Human give to goblin? Goblin ask nice.
goblin/insult: Paper hat on head. Not helmet. Human get hit on head, paper not help.
goblin/remark: Paper hat worth lots, humans say. Humans stupid with money.
troll/compliment: Paper hat! Pretty colour. Human give me? Me eat it. Still pretty.
troll/insult: Paper hat. Not stop rock. Rock go straight through. Me try?
troll/remark: Paper hat worth lots, humans say. Troll eat it, worth nothing. Funny.
parrot/compliment: Squawk! Pretty hat, pretty pretty hat!
parrot/insult: Squawk! Peck the hat, peck it, peck it!
mos_pirate/remark: A paper hat. Worth more'n the whole town, they say.
mos_pirate/compliment: Arr, now that be plunder worth the takin'.
mos_pirate/insult: Paper hat in a pirate town? Bold, or daft, landlubber.
guard/remark: Paper hat worth a castle. I'll be walking very close behind you.
guard/insult: Wearing that in the street. You want robbing, and then you'll want me.
guard/compliment: A {item}, and half the thieves in town just noticed it with me.
barbarian/insult: A paper hat! Peksa sells proper helmets, you know.
barbarian/remark: Paper on your head. One axe and it's confetti.
barbarian/compliment: Hah! A paper hat in a barbarian village takes nerve.

compliment: Master of everything, that cape says, and you still stop to chat.
That cape, adventurer! Is there anything you can't do?
insult: That cape says good at everything. It doesn't mention modesty.
remark: Must have taken you years, that.
A max cape! Your mother must be ever so proud... or worried.
kid/compliment: Is that the cape for being the best at everything?
wizard/insult: Master of everything, that cape claims, though of magic we shall see.
fremennik/compliment: Hah! That cape says master of everything, but can you drink?
Master of every craft. The council would vote for you at once.
heartland/insult: Master of everything in that cape, so you know where the queue starts.
tzhaar/compliment: That cape say JalYt master all. Mej, Ket, Xil, Hur. All one JalYt.
tzhaar/remark: Big cape. Many colours. TzHaar only need one colour. Red.
tzhaar/insult: Cape for being good at everything. Hot air too, TzHaar guess.
ogre/compliment: Big fancy cape wiv all da colours! Creature must be da biggun.
ogre/insult: Cape for being best at everyfing? Best at running away, maybe.
ogre/remark: Dat cape got lots of colours. Chompies would peck it. Me would too.
gnome/compliment: Master of everything? Even gnomeball? Now I'm impressed, human!
gnome/insult: Good at everything, human, except being small, and we win there.
dwarf/compliment: Master of every craft? Then your smithing's near as good as mine.
dwarf/remark: A cape for every skill. Years well spent, human.
fremennik/insult: Master of everything. Fine. Face Koschei unarmed, then say so.
moon_clan/compliment: A master of everything. Even yourself? That is the one that matters.
moon_clan/remark: Do you still dream of that cape, dear? I can see that you do, rather.
tortugan/compliment: Master of all things, that cape says, and that took patience.
tortugan/insult: Master of everything, they say. Everything on land, perhaps.
goblin/insult: Cape of many colours. Pick one colour, human! Even goblins pick one.
goblin/remark: Big cape with all colours. Red, green, blue... No brown. Shame.
goblin/compliment: Human good at everything, cape say. Even fighting? Then good.
troll/compliment: Big cape, all colours. Human good at everything, dey say. Even eating?
troll/insult: Fancy cape. Human good at everything? Try climbing icy mountain.
troll/remark: Cape of all colours. Trolls got one colour. Rock colour.
parrot/remark: Squawk! All the colours, all the colours!
mos_pirate/remark: All them colours. Ye look like a signal flag.
mos_pirate/compliment: Master of everythin', that cape says, but does that include the sea?
mos_pirate/insult: Fancy cape. Can ye tie a knot, though?
moon_clan_wary/insult: I see that cape of mastery did not come with any patience.
moon_clan_wary/remark: Every craft mastered, and still you came up here for ours.
moon_clan_wary/compliment: Master of everything but yourself, which is at least a start.
guard/compliment: Master of everything, says the cape. Ever tried standing still?
guard/remark: Done everything, that cape says. Not a shift on the gate, I'd wager.
guard/insult: Master of everything, and still walking through my gate like anyone.
barbarian/compliment: That cape says you're good at everything, so prove it with a drink.
barbarian/insult: Good at everything, that cape says, but can you fight?
barbarian/remark: A cape of every colour, and ours are furs, which don't boast.

compliment: In that plate you look like something that eats knights, kindly meant.
Ye gods, you look like the end of the world in that!
insult: Who's in there? Is it still you?
remark: How do you even see out of that?
Bet that's murder on the shoulders.
kid/compliment: You look like the scary one in Mum's stories!
guard/insult: That armour gets both my eyes, and I'd give it a third if I had one.
dwarf/compliment: I don't know who forged that, but I'd buy them two beers at least.
heartland/insult: Very fearsome. You'll frighten the chickens.
tzhaar/compliment: That armour look like it ate something. JalYt look dangerous. Good.
tzhaar/remark: Dark armour, heavy. Is JalYt in there? TzHaar cannot tell.
tzhaar/insult: Big fearsome armour. TzHaar-Ket still bigger. Nice try, JalYt.
ogre/compliment: Grrr! Big scary creature! Ogre nearly stepped back. Nearly.
ogre/insult: All dat scary armour and creature still smells like a toady.
ogre/remark: Creature in dat armour looks like a ogre. Little ogre. Hur, hur.
gnome/compliment: Megal! Human, you look like a war all by yourself.
gnome/remark: The children hid when they saw you, human. Don't take it personally.
dwarf/insult: Armour like a siege engine. Shame you move like one, human.
dwarf/remark: Ancient work, that armour. Forged before our history books begin.
fremennik/compliment: Hah! You look like a thing from a saga. The part the children fear.
fremennik/remark: Armour like that, and the trolls would move camp.
moon_clan/compliment: Fearsome armour with gentle thoughts inside it, and I like that.
moon_clan/insult: Oh my, armour like a nightmare, dear, and I have had better ones.
tortugan/compliment: In a shell like that you need fear no gryphon, perhaps the other way.
tortugan/remark: Dark heavy armour. In the water you would go straight down.
goblin/compliment: Big scary armour. Human nearly look like goblin champion. Nearly.
goblin/insult: Big dark armour. Human inside still small human. Me can tell.
goblin/remark: That armour heavy. Human walk like Wartface after beetle pie.
troll/compliment: Big dark armour. Human look like Dad. Dad is big troll. Is compliment.
troll/insult: Who in dere? Human? Troll crack it open an' see.
troll/remark: Heavy armour. Human sink in sea like troll now.
barbarian/compliment: Is there a giant in that armour, or just a mountainside?
barbarian/insult: All that black plate, and such a small person inside it!
barbarian/remark: Armour like a mountain. Our forefathers would've charged it anyway.

compliment: A fire cape! Nicely done, that.
You earned that cape the hard way, didn't you?
insult: A fire cape. Lovely. The infernal one's redder, mind.
Fire cape. Took a few goes, I expect.
remark: Ooh, toasty.
kid/compliment: Your cape's on fire!
kid/insult: Your fire cape's not even hot. I checked when you weren't looking.
fremennik/compliment: A cape won in fire. The sagas would have a verse for that.
A cape won in fire deserves a verse, and a good one.
heartland/remark: Mind you don't set the hedges off.
tzhaar/compliment: Fire cape. JalYt beat TzTok-Jad. TzHaar-Ket let you deeper now.
That cape was earned in Fight Cave. TzHaar know. TzHaar watched.
tzhaar/remark: TzHaar-Mej-Jal give TokKul for that cape. Keep it. Fire worth more.
Fire cape opens inner city. Deeper. Hotter. Mind yourself, JalYt.
tzhaar/insult: Fire cape warm JalYt, no? JalYt still cold inside. Is in the name.
Fire cape. Good. TzHaar-Ket-Keh want one too, before Inferno.
ogre/compliment: Ooh, creature's cape is on fire! Bestest cape. Me wants it.
ogre/insult: Cape on fire and creature not even cooked. Wasteful.
ogre/remark: Dat burny cape, creature. Good for da stew pot. Hur, hur.
gnome/compliment: A fire cape! Great Guthix, human. Did you have to stand in the fire?
gnome/remark: Keep that cape well away from the Grand Tree, human, which is a tree.
dwarf/compliment: A fire cape! Not smithed, but earned, and that counts, human.
dwarf/insult: Fine, a fire cape, but can it stop an axe?
dwarf/remark: That cape would do nicely by the forge, warm as it is.
fremennik/insult: A fine cape, but the fire did the hard work and you only stood in it.
moon_clan/compliment: A cape of fire. You walked through a nightmare awake, dear.
moon_clan/remark: Oh my, that cape is still thinking about the heat, and so are you.
tortugan/compliment: We know water trials, and that cape's trial of fire sounds worse.
tortugan/insult: Fire on your back. Do not come swimming in it, human.
goblin/compliment: Fire cape! Red and orange! Red best, Bentnoze say. Me like.
goblin/insult: Burny cape. Human stand in fire for cape? Humans stupid. Nice cape.
goblin/remark: Cape is orange-ish. Grubfoot wear orange once. Look like orange-fruit.
troll/compliment: Fire cape. Human stand in fire? Trolls not like fire. Brave human.
troll/insult: Burny cape. Keep it away. Trolls not like fire. Not funny.
troll/remark: Cape made of fire. Human cook self already. Save troll cook a job.
parrot/remark: Fire! Squawk! Fire, fire, feed the fires!
parrot/insult: Squawk! Keep it off me feathers, off me feathers!
mos_pirate/remark: Fire cape, eh? Keep it away from the powder.
mos_pirate/compliment: Arr, that be a hard-won cape, and no mistake.
mos_pirate/insult: Burny cape. Don't ye go near the rum stores with that.
moon_clan_wary/insult: A cape of fire. Loud, like the rest of your thoughts.
moon_clan_wary/remark: That cape fought something terrible. It did not teach you patience.
moon_clan_wary/compliment: A fire cape, so a trial survived. Ours is harder, but I grant it.
guard/remark: That cape's on fire. Keep it off the thatch.
guard/insult: A burning cape inside the walls. That's a fire risk, and a report.
guard/compliment: Fire cape. Earned the hard way, I hear. Still no smoking in town.
barbarian/compliment: You stood in fire for that cape and that's barbarian spirit!
barbarian/insult: Keep that fire cape off the thatch. We like our longhall as it is.
barbarian/remark: Cape of fire. The longhall fire never goes out either.

compliment: Ooh, a {item}. Very rare, that.
insult: Bit early for Halloween, isn't it?
remark: Gave me a right turn, that mask.
kid/compliment: Scary mask! Do it again!
kid/insult: You're not scary. My sister's scarier.
nan/insult: Take the mask off, dear. Oh dear! That was rude of me, wasn't it.

compliment: Not many can carry off a bald head like you do.
Not a hair up top to slow you down on the roads.
insult: I can see my reflection in that head.
plain/insult: Lost your hair, or just misplaced it?
Bald as a coot, you.
sharp/insult: Not a hair left. Did it leave of its own accord, or was it pushed?
remark: Must save you a fortune on combs.
kid/insult: Why have you got no hair?
Mum! That one's bald!
Your head looks like an egg.
nan/remark: Hat on, dear. You'll catch your death with a head like that.
toff/insult: Has somebody pinched your hair, citizen, or did you mislay it?
trader/remark: I've a lovely wig out the back, my friend, an absolute bargain.
wizard/insult: Bald? A pity. I know a spell for that. It doesn't work, but I know it.
banker/remark: Hats are permitted in the bank, just so you know.
gnome/insult: A head like a gnomeball. Stay well clear of the pitch, human.
pirate/insult: Arr, a head like a cannonball, so mind the gunners.
pirate/remark: A bald head and no hat? The gulls'll have ye, matey.
rough/insult: Head like a peeled turnip, that.
rough/remark: Ye'll want a hat in the fields with a head like that.
barkeep/remark: Lovely. I can see the whole bar in that head.
dwarf/remark: Nothing on top? Grow a beard, friend, and it balances out.
The forge takes the hair off eventually, and yours just went early.
fremennik/insult: No hair to braid? What will the sagas say of you, then?
A head like a Longhall table. Smooth, and seen some beer.
A bet in the Longhall, was it? The beer does not take hair, usually.
burgher/insult: Lost your hair? We lost ours to worrying.
heartland/insult: The sun's bouncing right off your head, traveller.
heartland/remark: Mind you don't get sunburnt up top.
tzhaar/remark: JalYt has no hair. Good. Hair burn. TzHaar never had hair.
tzhaar/insult: Head smooth like cooled lava. Shame rest of JalYt still soft.
tzhaar/compliment: Smooth head, like good obsidian. JalYt almost handsome.
ogre/insult: Creature's head is like a egg. Hur, hur. Me likes eggs.
ogre/remark: Shiny head, creature. Not shiny enough to keep, though.
ogre/compliment: No hair on creature. Goodly. Hair gets in da stew.
gnome/compliment: A smooth head is very aerodynamic. Pilots would approve, human.
gnome/remark: Not a hair on top. Great Guthix, humans do things thoroughly.
dwarf/compliment: Honest look, that, bald as a polished ingot.
dwarf/insult: Hair all gone and still no beard? Sort your priorities out, human.
fremennik/compliment: A bare head takes a helm better, Skulgrimen will tell you that.
No hair for an enemy to grab. That is a warrior's thinking.
fremennik/remark: A horned helm would sit well on that bare head, Skulgrimen sells them.
moon_clan/compliment: A clear head, inside and out. The moon likes that in a person.
Nothing between your thoughts and the moon, which is very convenient.
moon_clan/insult: Oh my. Your thoughts are easier to read with nothing in the way.
Do not fret, dear, for we can grow it back in a dream... briefly.
moon_clan/remark: The moon is bald too, and nobody minds... mostly nobody.
tortugan/compliment: Smooth as a good shell. A fine thing, where I come from.
Hair only slows you in the water, so you have the right idea.
tortugan/insult: Hair is for land creatures. You seem to have given it up early.
A tortugan is born without hair. You had to work at it, I take it.
tortugan/remark: Mind the hermit crabs. They would take that head for a shell.
goblin/insult: Human head shiny like helmet. Wrong colour helmet.
goblin/remark: No hair on human. Goblins not got much hair neither. Is fine.
goblin/compliment: Bald head look strong. Like big rock. Me approve.
troll/insult: Human head smooth like river stone. Me try nibble it, maybe.
No hair on top. Less to pick out of troll teeth.
troll/remark: Bald head look like egg. Trolls like egg. Me not eat head. Probably.
troll/compliment: Shiny head like good rock. Me like rocks. Good head.
cat/remark: Will the fur grow back on top, or is that it for you?
cat/insult: I've coughed up more hair than you've got on your head.
cat/compliment: Bend down, I want to check if that shiny head's as warm as it looks.
camel/remark: The sun will find that bare head, because it finds everything.
camel/insult: A bald head under this sun. You'll cook like a flatbread.
camel/compliment: A clean, smooth head. Rather elegant, like a dune.
leprechaun/remark: Not a hair on ye. Mebbe try a bit o' supercompost up top.
leprechaun/insult: Yer head's as bald as a fresh-raked patch, so it is.
leprechaun/compliment: A foine shiny head. Ye could see the weeds comin' in it.
parrot/insult: Shiny! Squawk! Shiny, shiny, peck it!
mos_pirate/remark: Bald as a cannonball, ye be.
mos_pirate/insult: Sun'll have that head, landlubber, so get yerself a bandana.
mos_pirate/compliment: A fine head for a bandana, that.
moon_clan_wary/insult: Your thoughts were easy enough to read before the hair went.
No hair between your thoughts and me now, and how I wish there were.
moon_clan_wary/remark: Nothing to hide under, up there. Nothing to hide, either, I expect.
moon_clan_wary/compliment: A clear head, and I can see straight in, so do keep it that way.
guard/remark: Description: bald. Saves me a line of ink.
No helmet, no hair. At least I can see what you're thinking.
guard/insult: No hair. Easier to describe to the sergeant, I'll give you that.
guard/compliment: Nowhere on that head to hide a weapon, which I appreciate.
barbarian/insult: Bald as a river stone. Nothing for a foe to grab, or to admire.
barbarian/remark: No hair? A helmet will fit you fine. Peksa's shop is just there.
barbarian/compliment: A bare head and no fear. That's a warrior's look, that.

item.pattern: ^(Rubber chicken|Bunny ears|Frog mask|Mime mask|Jester hat|Banana hat|Chicken head|Evil chicken head)

compliment: Love the {item}. Brightened my day, that.
Now the {item}, that's a proper look.
insult: What on earth is going on with the {item}?
Did you lose a bet, or did you actually choose the {item}?
remark: I won't ask about the {item}.
Fancy dress party, is it?
kid/compliment: Haha! Look at the {item}!
kid/insult: Are you poorly or something, going out in the {item}?
toff/insult: The {item}? How frightfully common.
pirate/compliment: Haha! A {item}! Ye'd fit right in below decks.

compliment: The {item}. Somebody's been at it for years, then.
The {item}! Proper dedication, that.
insult: Ah, the {item}. You'll want everyone to know, then.
Lovely {item}. Bit of a cardigan, mind.
remark: So you're the one who's good at that.
kid/compliment: Ooh, you're good at something!
rough/compliment: Ye've put the hours in for that {item}, fair play to ye.
dwarf/compliment: A {item}! A master. We masters must stick together.
heartland/remark: Wear that to the pub, do you?
tzhaar/compliment: Cape of a master. One thing done well. TzHaar-Hur understand.
tzhaar/remark: Cape means master, no? TzHaar born knowing. JalYt must learn.
tzhaar/insult: Fine cape. Does JalYt skill help in lava? No? Then is cape.
ogre/compliment: Nice cape. Yous good at sumfin. Is it cooking? Say cooking.
ogre/insult: Cape for being good at one fing. Ogre is good at all da smashing.
ogre/remark: Soft cape. Nice for wiping da chompy grease off. Hur, hur.
gnome/compliment: A {item}! You'd make a fine gnome, human, apart from the size.
gnome/remark: A {item}, is it? The children will want a look.
dwarf/insult: A {item}. Fine. Smithing's the one that counts, mind.
dwarf/remark: The {item}. A master, then. Masters are welcome at my forge.
fremennik/compliment: One craft, done until it was yours... that is honour, that cape.
fremennik/remark: A {item}. One craft, a lifetime. The bards respect that, when sober.
moon_clan/compliment: Years of one thought held steady for that {item}, and few can, dear.
moon_clan/insult: You are thinking of mentioning the {item}, dear, and you must not.
tortugan/compliment: The {item} is one thing done well for years, the tortugan way.
tortugan/remark: Leff would call the {item} boring, but Leff is young.
goblin/compliment: Human good at one thing. Goblins good at war. War best thing.
goblin/insult: Cape for being good at thing. Is thing fighting? No? Then not matter.
goblin/remark: Fancy cape. What colour is it? Not brown. Nothing is brown.
troll/compliment: Human good at one thing, cape say. Troll good at one thing. Eating.
troll/insult: Cape say human good at thing. Is thing cooking? No? Then not useful.
troll/remark: Fancy cape. Human wear cape, troll wear nothing. Troll warm anyway.
leprechaun/remark: Is that foine cape the farmin' one? Nay, I can see it's not, pity.
leprechaun/compliment: A cape for bein' good at a thing. Ye'd want the farmin' one, mind.
leprechaun/insult: Can that fancy cape hold a rake? Nay, so I'm still needed, then.
moon_clan_wary/insult: You are thinking of mentioning the {item}, and I would not.
Years given to one craft, and not one hour of patience for us?
moon_clan_wary/compliment: The {item}. Patience, then. Perhaps you can learn to listen too.
guard/compliment: The {item}, eh? All the watch gives us is a cloak, and it leaks.
guard/remark: The {item}. A master, then. Masters still pay the toll.
guard/insult: I've checked, and that fancy cape exempts you from nothing.
barbarian/compliment: A cape for a skill? If the skill's swinging an axe then good.
barbarian/insult: A cape for one skill. If it's not fighting, I'm not impressed.
barbarian/remark: Here we don't give capes for mastery, only scars.

compliment: In armour like that you could walk through a wall, if slowly.
Now that's what I call proper armour.
insult: Bandos. Bit much for popping to the bank, isn't it?
Looks like you've been dipped in mustard.
remark: Bet that's a faff to get on and off.
The goblins would be ever so proud of you.
tzhaar/remark: Big brown armour of a war god. Heavy. JalYt carry it well enough.
tzhaar/compliment: Armour of the war god. JalYt took it from his army, no? Strong JalYt.
tzhaar/insult: War god armour. Big. Loud. JalYt inside still small.
ogre/compliment: Bandos armour! Da big war god's own. Creature wears it goodly.
ogre/insult: War god's armour on a creature. Grrr. Should be on an ogre.
ogre/remark: Ogre-ish armour, dat. Big and brown. Creature nearly looks right.
gnome/compliment: Armour from the god of war himself. Great Guthix, human, you're brave.
gnome/insult: Bandos armour? You'd sink a glider in that, human, so you walk.
dwarf/compliment: Good, that Bandos plate, thick as a mine cart and twice as proud.
dwarf/insult: Bandos. Mustard-coloured. The Yellow Fortune would want a word.
dwarf/remark: Armour from the God Wars. Older than the Consortium, and still sound.
fremennik/compliment: Armour off a war god's soldier. The bards will want the details.
fremennik/insult: A war god's armour. It fits like it was made for someone bigger.
moon_clan/compliment: A war god's armour with a quiet mind inside it, how interesting.
moon_clan/insult: A war god's armour. Oh my. It is louder than your thoughts.
tortugan/compliment: Heavy armour, worn calmly. A shell is heavy too, and one adjusts.
tortugan/remark: A war god's armour. At sea, the sea is the only war we know.
goblin/compliment: Armour of Big High War God! Human wear it? Praise Big High War God!
Big High War God armour! Human must be mighty. Or sneaky. Both good.
goblin/insult: Armour of Big High War God on human? Human not even goblin. Wrong!
goblin/remark: Big brown armour. Brown! Generals both say brown best. Human listen.
troll/compliment: Big brown armour. Heavy like rock. Human strong like troll, nearly.
troll/insult: Big heavy armour. Human walk like troll now. Still not troll.
troll/remark: Dat armour big. Human inside small. Like nut in big shell.
barbarian/compliment: You carry that heavy brown plate like it's nothing, good!
barbarian/insult: Hah! The goblins' war god's armour, on you?
barbarian/remark: They say that war plate was the goblins' god's, and now it's yours.

compliment: Feathers and gold. You look like a very expensive bird.
Winged armour! Don't go taking off before I've had a proper look.
insult: Bit heavy on the gold trim, if I'm honest.
You look like a posh curtain.
remark: Don't stand near any magpies.
goblin/insult: Bird armour. Feathers. Human want fly away from battle? Cowards!
goblin/remark: Feathery armour. Bird god. Goblins not fight for bird god.
goblin/compliment: Shiny feather armour. Human look like big expensive bird. Tasty bird.

compliment: A Santa hat! Merry Christmas, traveller.
Ooh, very festive, that hat!
insult: It's not Christmas. Is it? Nobody tells me anything.
kid/compliment: Are you Father Christmas?!
kid/insult: My brother says Santa's not real, so whose hat is that?
heartland/remark: Christmas, is it? Nobody's told the goose.

compliment: By the look of that cape, you've helped everyone in Gielinor.
Every errand in the kingdom, and you've the cape to prove it!
insult: So you're the one who keeps poking about in everyone's sheds.
remark: You must have heard some strange requests in your time.
tzhaar/compliment: Cape for finishing every errand. JalYt who finish. Rare JalYt.
tzhaar/remark: Many deeds in that cape. JalYt carry stories like TzHaar carry memory.
tzhaar/insult: Cape for helping everyone. Everyone up top. Down here, is just cape.
ogre/compliment: Dat cape means creature helps everybody. Help ogre. Bring chompy.
ogre/insult: Creature does jobs for everybody? Stoopid. Ogre does jobs for ogre.
ogre/remark: Fancy cape for running errands. Ogres don't run. Ogres sit.
gnome/compliment: That cape! You've helped half of Gielinor, human, Narnode included?
gnome/insult: A cape for doing errands. Humans will wear anything, Great Guthix.
gnome/remark: Every errand in the land, they say. You must know every glider route.
dwarf/compliment: By Guthix, that cape says you've helped folk from here to Keldagrim.
dwarf/insult: A cape for running errands. I'd rather have one for smithing.
fremennik/compliment: A cape for finishing every task. Sigmund's errands alone break most.
fremennik/insult: A cape for errands. Sigmund has you fetching flowers, I expect.
moon_clan/compliment: A cape for helping everyone. Your thoughts are tidy for one so busy.
moon_clan/remark: That cape says you have been everywhere. Your dreams must be crowded.
tortugan/compliment: Helped everyone, that cape says. Few tourists stay long enough.
tortugan/insult: Everyone's errands done. Humans do love to be busy.
moon_clan_wary/insult: A cape for meddling everywhere. Now you have come to meddle with us.
moon_clan_wary/remark: Been everywhere, that cape says. Nowhere taught you to listen.
moon_clan_wary/compliment: A cape for helping everyone. We did not ask, but it is something.

compliment: Still standing. That's the spirit.
insult: You look like death warmed up.
Bit peaky, aren't you?
remark: You're looking a bit worse for wear, traveller.
You look awful. Go and have a sit down and a cup of tea.
You've been in the wars, haven't you?
kid/remark: Are you going to die?
nan/remark: Ooh, you've been in the wars. Sit down before you fall down.
vicar/remark: You look in need of healing. Or a decent night's sleep.
barkeep/remark: You look like you've been through the sewers, so sit by the door.
gnome/remark: You look like you lost at gnomeball, so have a toad crunchie.
You need a cocktail and a lie down, human, and in that order.
pirate/remark: Ye look half drowned. Rum first, questions after.
rough/remark: Cor, ye've been in the wars. Sit on that bale before ye fall.
barkeep/insult: Don't bleed on the bar. I've only just wiped it.
dwarf/remark: You look like a cracked anvil. Sit down before you split.
Sit down before you fall down, human. There's a stout in it for you.
fremennik/compliment: Wounded and still walking. Hah! There's Fremennik in you yet.
Bleeding, and your back is still straight, the spirits note that.
Hah! Wounds are a saga written on the skin, and yours has a chapter.
burgher/remark: You look pale, and pale's bad round here, so get indoors, eh?
tzhaar/remark: JalYt look cold. Cold JalYt soon dead JalYt. Go sit by lava.
tzhaar/insult: JalYt leaking again. Red water this time. Is worse, no?
tzhaar/compliment: Hurt, still standing. TzHaar-Ket would nod at that. Once.
ogre/remark: Creature looks half dead. Half dead is half cooked, me finks.
ogre/insult: Grrr, creature is leaking. Don't drip on da rock cakes.
ogre/compliment: Still walking wiv all dat leaking? Tough creature. Chewy, too.
gnome/compliment: Still upright, human! A gnome would be flat by now.
gnome/insult: Did a glider land on you? You look like a glider landed on you.
dwarf/compliment: Battered, but still standing. Good metal does the same.
dwarf/insult: You look like a pie that's been dropped twice.
fremennik/insult: You look like something a dagannoth spat out, half chewed.
Sit down before you fall down. Falling down is for the Longhall.
fremennik/remark: A warrior's wounds are an honour. Still, go and sit by a fire.
moon_clan/compliment: Hurt, but your thoughts are steady, and that is the harder part.
Still standing, with all that pain. The mind is the stronger part.
moon_clan/insult: Oh my. I can hear your head throbbing from here, dear, so do sit down.
Try to think less loudly about the pain. Some of us are listening.
moon_clan/remark: Rest, dear. The body knits itself best while the mind is dreaming.
tortugan/compliment: Wounded and still patient. You would make a decent tortugan.
You carry that hurt quietly, and that is the right way.
tortugan/insult: You look like a gryphon's leftovers, and they rarely leave any.
No shell to hide in, and it shows. Do find somewhere to sit.
tortugan/remark: Salt water would do those wounds good. Or sting, one of the two.
goblin/remark: Human leaking. Humans leak lots when hit. Goblins too, but quieter.
goblin/insult: Human half dead! Not show mercy, commandment say. Me show little bit.
goblin/compliment: Human hurt but not run from battle. Big High War God like that.
troll/remark: Human leaking. Humans leak when hit. Trolls heal quick, humans not.
troll/insult: Human look half cooked already. Burntmeat like dat. Me just hungry.
troll/compliment: Hurt but still standing. Tough human. Tough meat, though.
cat/remark: You smell of blood. Your own, I think, since humans leak so.
cat/insult: You look like something I'd bring in and leave on the step.
cat/compliment: Still on your feet. I'd have had a nap by now.
camel/remark: You look dry and wounded. I know the feeling, every day.
camel/insult: You sway like a tent in the wind. Sit down before you fall on me.
camel/compliment: Hurt and still walking? The desert respects that, and so do I.
leprechaun/remark: Ye look like a patch wi' the disease on it, so ye do.
leprechaun/insult: 'Tis plant cure ye need. Nay, I've none for people.
leprechaun/compliment: Ye're still standin', lookin' like that, and that's foine stuff.
parrot/remark: Man down! Squawk! Man down, man down!
parrot/insult: Squawk! Dead men tell no tales!
mos_pirate/insult: Dead men tell no tales, and ye be lookin' like one.
mos_pirate/compliment: Still on yer feet? Tough as old rope, ye be.
moon_clan_wary/insult: You are hurt, and thinking about it very loudly, so do it elsewhere.
Yes, I know you are in pain. I can hear it, and I would rather not.
moon_clan_wary/remark: Bleeding on our doorstep will not earn you anything.
moon_clan_wary/compliment: Wounded but upright, strong in body. We went the other way entirely.
guard/remark: You're bleeding on the paving. Someone will have to mop that.
You look half dead. Don't finish the job on my patch.
guard/insult: If you're going to fall over, do it outside the walls.
guard/compliment: Still upright after walking in like that, which is fair enough.
barbarian/remark: You're hurt. Good. Means you've been fighting, not talking.
barbarian/insult: Bleeding already? Bah! Walk it off, little one.
barbarian/compliment: Wounded and still on your feet. The longhall would drink to that.

compliment: Grand old armour. It's seen a few centuries and worn them well.
Lovely old armour, that. They don't make it like that any more.
insult: You dug that gear out of a grave, didn't you?
That armour smells a bit of crypt.
remark: Been rummaging in tombs again?
Some poor brother's missing that.
trader/remark: Grave goods, those, and I never ask where, only what they fetch.
pirate/remark: That armour's off a dead man, and arr, so were me boots.
barkeep/insult: You've brought the crypt in with you, so sit by the window.
dwarf/remark: That armour's old work, but good. Smiths cared about it back then.
fremennik/remark: Grave iron. The spirits don't care for that, outerlander.
tzhaar/remark: That armour from graves of JalYt. TzHaar dead become rock. Cleaner.
tzhaar/insult: Grave armour. JalYt dig up own dead? TzHaar keep ours as statues.
tzhaar/compliment: Old armour, still strong. Has memories in it. TzHaar understand that.
ogre/insult: Creature smells like a zogrie. Grrr. Stay away from da village.
ogre/remark: Dead man's armour. Dead man didn't need it. Fair, me suppose.
ogre/compliment: Old crypt armour. Creature dug it up? Ogre likes a creature what digs.
gnome/compliment: That armour might be older than the Grand Tree, human, and that's old.
gnome/insult: You smell of tomb, human. Kar, don't sit by the cocktail bar.
gnome/remark: Grave armour. Humans dig up the oddest things.
dwarf/compliment: Crypt work, but good crypt work. The smiths of old knew their trade.
dwarf/insult: Dug that out of a barrow? Give it a scrub before the forge sees it.
fremennik/compliment: You took that armour from a dead man's hands, and that is bold.
fremennik/insult: Grave iron, hah! A warrior wins his gear instead of digging for it.
moon_clan/compliment: That armour has dreamt a long time, and it is glad to be awake.
moon_clan/remark: Oh my, that armour still thinks about its old owner, and so does he.
tortugan/compliment: Old armour, well kept, and age is no shame, ask any elder.
tortugan/insult: Dug up, was it? We weave baskets for our dead and do not rob them.
goblin/remark: Human dig up old armour from graves. Goblins just take from crates.
goblin/insult: Old mouldy armour. Smell like worm stew left out. Me quite like it.
goblin/compliment: Old armour from tomb. Goblins fight in old armour too. Strong stuff.
troll/compliment: Old armour from graves. Smell like old troll cave. Me like.
troll/insult: Dug up dead human's clothes? Trolls not even do dat. Trolls eat fresh.
troll/remark: Mouldy armour. Smell like goat left out too long. Me still eat goat.
guard/remark: That armour's out of a grave, and grave-robbing's a crime somewhere.
guard/insult: Tomb armour in the street. If it's got a smell, keep upwind of me.
guard/compliment: That armour's seen things, same as me, though mine were mostly carts.
barbarian/compliment: Dug that out of a grave? Hah! A warrior keeps what he wins.
barbarian/insult: Grave armour, and it smells like it, so stand downwind.
barbarian/remark: Old armour from the swamp tombs. The dead don't need it anyway.

compliment: Blimey! That's a castle's worth of armour you've got on.
Look at you, done up like a duke.
insult: All that money on your back, and still no manners.
sharp/insult: All that finery, and still money can't buy taste, can it?
remark: Mind the pickpockets. They'll smell that money.
banker/remark: We do offer secure storage. You'd want the big vault.
trader/compliment: A customer of quality! Come in, come in, and mind the cheap stuff.
shady/remark: Careless, that much money walking about on one person.
guard/insult: Oi. All that steel's for outside the walls, understand?
All that gold. I'll be watching you, and so will worse than me.
gnome/compliment: You glitter like a spirit tree at midsummer, human, how splendid!
Rometti would sell his shop for that outfit, human.
gnome/remark: A gnome could retire on one of your boots, human.
pirate/compliment: Arr, ye're wearing a galleon's worth so mind the press gangs, eh?
pirate/remark: Shiny as a captain's chest, ye are. Don't walk the docks alone.
rough/insult: All that gold, and ye've never lifted a hoe, I'll wager.
rough/remark: Blimey. That lot'd buy my farm twice over.
barkeep/compliment: All that finery on you means you're buying, them's the rules.
barkeep/remark: Mind the step. Wouldn't want all that gold going over.
dwarf/compliment: Good steel, well kept. Someone forged that with love.
dwarf/remark: That's a year at the anvil you're wearing, friend.
The Consortium would make you a director on the spot, dressed so.
fremennik/compliment: A longhall's worth of gold on your back, and you still stand straight.
Trophies, or bought? Either way, you carry them like a chieftain.
Hah! Enough on your back to buy the Longhall a year of beer.
fremennik/insult: Gold on your back, outerlander, and gold wins no sagas.
All that gold, and I wager you have never hauled a net.
A dagannoth does not care what your armour cost, and nor do I.
guard/remark: Full plate on market day. I'll be two paces behind you.
guard/compliment: Armour like that could join the watch, if you'll take pay in soup.
burgher/compliment: All that shiny stuff. Never seen so much shiny.
burgher/remark: Don't wave all that finery about here, folk is hungry.
tzhaar/remark: JalYt wears much gold. Gold is soft. Will melt down here.
tzhaar/insult: All that soft gold on one JalYt. TokKul worth more. Hard money.
tzhaar/compliment: Fine gear for a JalYt. Someone paid many TokKul for that, no?
ogre/compliment: Ooh, creature all bright pretties! Bestest fing me seen today.
ogre/insult: All dem shiny bits, creature. Dey come off before cooking, yes?
ogre/remark: Creature is walking treasure. Ogres notice. Ogres always notice.
gnome/insult: All that finery, and you still can't fit in a glider.
dwarf/insult: Fine gear, human. Bought, I'd say, not earned at an anvil.
fremennik/remark: Sigmund the Merchant would follow you home for that gold, politely.
moon_clan/compliment: All that finery and no greed in your thoughts, how unusual, dear.
Riches outside, riches within. One does not always find both.
moon_clan/insult: Oh my. All that gold, and your thoughts are still rather small.
You are thinking about how much it is all worth, rather loudly, dear.
moon_clan/remark: We trade little for gold on the island. Magic is cheaper, and lighter.
tortugan/compliment: A fine shell you have built yourself, heavy, but fine.
All that is earned, I take it. Patience pays well, in the end.
tortugan/insult: Gold does not float. Mind where you fall in.
A tortugan carries one shell. You seem to have bought several.
tortugan/remark: At sea, that much metal is ballast. On land, I gather it is fashion.
goblin/compliment: Shiny armour everywhere! Human must be bigger than general.
goblin/insult: All that shiny stuff and human still ugly. Shiny not help face.
goblin/remark: Human wear lots of expensive. Goblins wear goblin mail. Brown now.
troll/compliment: Lotta shiny stuff on human. Human must be big boss, like troll boss.
troll/insult: All dat metal. Troll crack it open like nut. Human is nut inside.
troll/remark: Shiny human. Too much tin. Trolls not eat tin. Bad for teeth.
cat/remark: Does all that shiny metal come off, so I can sit in it?
cat/insult: Where are your priorities, dressed like a king with not a fish on you?
cat/compliment: Shiny armour. Warm when the sun's on it, so I may sit on you later.
camel/remark: All that metal in this heat. You could roast an egg on you.
camel/insult: Dressed like an emir, and still you smell of goat.
camel/compliment: Finery like that deserves a sonnet. I'll start on one tonight.
leprechaun/remark: All that shiny gear, and I'll wager ye've still no rake.
leprechaun/insult: Ye could buy the whole farm, and ye'd still not weed it.
leprechaun/compliment: Foine armour, that. Don't ye be muckin' it up in me compost.
parrot/insult: Shiny thing! Squawk! Mine, mine, all mine!
parrot/compliment: Squawk! Rich as a captain, rich as a captain!
mos_pirate/remark: Arr, there be plunder walkin' about on two legs.
mos_pirate/insult: Flash as a captain, and ye still walk like a landlubber.
mos_pirate/compliment: That be a fine haul ye're wearin', and no mistake.
moon_clan_wary/insult: All that gold, and still you came picking at our secrets.
Must you think about what all that gold is worth quite so loudly?
moon_clan_wary/remark: Gold buys nothing from us. Patience might. You brought the wrong one.
moon_clan_wary/compliment: Wealthy, and not thinking about it. Unusual, for a mainlander.
barbarian/insult: All that shiny armour, and I bet you bought every bit of it.
barbarian/remark: Rich, are you? Then you're buying in the longhall tonight.
barbarian/compliment: Armour like that gets taken off the beaten, so well taken!

compliment: Mix and match. Very individual.
insult: Did you get dressed in the dark?
Is that a bit of everything, or did a jumble sale fall on you?
plain/insult: Bit of a dog's dinner, that outfit.
remark: Matching's overrated, I suppose.
A scrap merchant would love you.
kid/insult: Does your mum know your armour doesn't match?
toff/insult: Nothing matches, citizen, not one plate, and one feels quite unwell.
