remark: Is that armour red, or has something happened?
vicar/insult: Armour the colour of blood, and I'll not ask whose.
guard/remark: Red armour, head to foot. I'll be keeping an eye on you.
kid/compliment: Are you a monster, all red and spiky like that?

compliment: Ooh, that armour shines like a chapel window!
insult: You shine like a polished kettle. I can see my face in your knees.
vicar/compliment: Infernal metal made clean again, and there's a sermon in that.
kid/compliment: You're glowing! Are you an angel?

compliment: Odd shape on that little shield, but it's very well made, isn't it?
insult: Does that little shield cover much, or just the hand holding it?
kid/remark: Your shield looks like a big snail shell!

compliment: Blimey, that cape's master of every craft and the arena besides?
remark: When do you sleep, with every craft and the arena on that cape?
insult: A cape for everything and a quiver on top, couldn't you choose?
kid/compliment: Your cape's got arrows in it! Shoot one at the sky, go on!

compliment: That's a veteran's cape. You've been somewhere awful, often.
remark: That's the cape you get for going back, and back, and back again.
fremennik/compliment: A cape won many times over. You honour your hall, outerlander.
kid/remark: What did you do to win that cape, and was it scary?

compliment: They say the elves don't give those capes out lightly, so well done.
insult: An elven cape. Did they make you sing for it?
wizard/remark: Prifddinas work, that cape. The elves are fussy who they honour.
kid/compliment: Did the elves that gave you that cape really live in trees?

compliment: The hood as well? A master of everything, down to the hat.
insult: A hood to match the cape. Some people do like to be sure.
remark: I'd know that hood anywhere. You're the one who's good at everything.
kid/remark: Did your mum make you match your hood to your cape?

remark: Matching hood and all. You've thought about this.
insult: The hood as well. In case anyone missed the cape.
nan/compliment: A hood! Good. Keeps your ears warm, dear.
kid/insult: Why the hood? Is it only raining on you?

remark: In that get-up you look like you've had a bad night, since you died.
vicar/remark: Are you still with us, traveller, or ought I to fetch the book?
kid/compliment: I can see your bones! Do it again and do the bones at me!

insult: Someone's left you in the bandage drawer too long.
nan/remark: All those bandages! Are you hurt, dear, shall I fetch someone?
kid/remark: Mummy! Not my actual mummy but you in the bandages!

remark: For a moment I thought a demon had come for the rent.
compliment: Good mask, that. Gave me a proper turn.
vicar/insult: A demon's face, worn for fun. Saradomin has a long memory.
kid/compliment: Rarr! Do it again and do the big demon rarr!

compliment: Fine foreign armour. From over the sea, is it?
remark: That hat's like an upturned bowl. Keeps the rain off, I'll grant.
kid/remark: Your hat's a pointy bowl!

remark: Dark robes, dark hood. Off to a meeting, are we?
wizard/insult: Robes of darkness, how very dramatic, and do you cackle as well?
kid/insult: You look like a shadow that forgot to go home.

remark: Should I bow to those robes? Nobody told me we'd a royal visit.
insult: Very regal. A king of somewhere small, I should think.
toff/insult: A crown? Citizen, there are proper channels for that sort of thing.
kid/compliment: Can I have a gold coin if you're a king? Kings have loads of them.

compliment: Now that's a hat. You don't see one like it twice.
remark: That's a hat with opinions, that is.
toff/compliment: Finally, someone round here dressed with a little style.
kid/remark: Ha! What's that on your head?

remark: You're swaying a bit there, friend, so steady on.
barkeep/insult: Bring your own ale past my door, would you, the cheek of it?
kid/remark: Why are you walking all wobbly, like my uncle at a wedding?

compliment: A feathered hat and a tabard. Very dashing, very foreign.
toff/compliment: Now there is a hat worth doffing, with a splendid feather on it.
kid/remark: Did you catch the bird that feather came off, yourself?

remark: Father Christmas gone off, eh? Festive, that, and ever so wrong.
nan/insult: That mask's not a nice face for Christmas, dear, not nice at all.
kid/insult: Shoo! You're the bad one who takes all the presents!

remark: Robes like that are for a ceremony. I'd rather not know which.
wizard/compliment: Old Zarosian vestments. Someone's been down the prison, hm?
kid/remark: Is that your real face under the funny mask, or a funnier one?

monkey/compliment: A ninja! Quick on the rooftops, I bet. Awowogei's guards like you.
monkey/remark: Ninja monkeys keep to the shadows. You keep to the middle of the path.
Mind the swing ropes if you're off to run the agility course.
monkey/insult: Funny-looking ninja. Bit stiff in the tail, you are.

monkey/compliment: Please don't eat my bananas, zombie, because I'll share them.
monkey/remark: A zombie monkey, up and about. The temple's lost one, then.
monkey/insult: Phew. You smell like the bottom of the temple.

monkey/compliment: A gorilla! Big and strong. You guard the temple, do you?
That beard, if you've got one, is very distinguished.
monkey/remark: Gorillas keep to the temple. What brings you out here?
monkey/insult: Gorillas aren't usually so clumsy, so why do you walk like a human?

monkey/compliment: You look as old as the island, and Marimbo bless you for it.
monkey/remark: An ancient one! I thought your kind were only bones now.
monkey/insult: Ancient, are you? You don't look a day over a hundred.

monkey/compliment: Welcome to Marim, cousin. Mind the guards, they're fussy.
monkey/remark: Karamja monkeys. Always smell of seawater and bananas.
monkey/insult: Country cousin from Karamja, are you? Mind yourself in the big town.

monkey/compliment: Kruk's shape suits you better than it ever suited him.
monkey/remark: You look just like Kruk. Please don't look like Kruk.
monkey/insult: Kruk's face, on a stranger. Awowogei won't like that one bit.

monkey/compliment: A human who bothered to learn our words, or to wear them at least.
monkey/remark: A talking human. That amulet's doing all the work, isn't it?
monkey/insult: You speak monkey like a gnome speaks monkey, which is badly.

compliment: A little lava beast, tamed. You must be braver than you look.
Fair play, not many could keep a little fire beast like that at heel.
insult: It's glowing. I do hope that's not your idea of a lantern.
Your creature's smouldering. I'd worry about the company it keeps.
remark: It's giving off heat from here. Handy in winter, I suppose.
kid/remark: Is it on fire? Can I poke it?
kid/insult: Yours is a rock on fire and mine's a dog, so mine's better.
nan/remark: Keep that smouldering thing off my doorstep, dear, as I've just swept.
vicar/remark: Straight out of Zamorak's hearth, that, and it's not coming in here.
rough/remark: Blimey. Don't let that anywhere near the hay.
heartland/remark: Keep that smouldering little thing off the thatch, would you?

compliment: That little ember of a thing glows like a forge, and it minds you!
That came from somewhere very deep, and chose to come back with you.
insult: All teeth and temper, that. It's clearly learnt from somebody.
That creature eats adventurers, surely. Does it know that you're one?
remark: Does it bite? It looks like it bites.
That thing's giving off heat. Stand a bit further off, would you?
kid/remark: Can your lava monster melt things? Could it melt my spoon for me?
toff/remark: Is that thing volcanic? Keep it off the rugs, citizen.
wizard/remark: Obsidian and heat bound into a thing that follows you, and I want one.

compliment: A cave lizard, and it comes when called? You've a way with beasts.
Ugly little lizard, but it adores you, and that's rarer than beauty.
insult: Your lizard's got more teeth than you've got sense, I'd wager.
Did you find that in a cave, or did it find you?
remark: What is that, some cave lizard? Why's it staring at me like that?
Pale as a mushroom, that creature. Never seen daylight, I'd say.
kid/remark: It's got big eyes. Why's it got big eyes?
kid/insult: Your lizard looks like it's never been outside, same as you.
wizard/remark: That lizard's from very deep underground, so keep it off my books.
rough/remark: Keep that lizard off the fish stall. It's got that look about it.

compliment: I've no idea what that is, but it follows you ever so faithfully.
No idea what that is, but it looks at you like you hung the moon.
insult: Whatever that is, it looks cleverer than its owner.
Did you make that yourself? It has the look of a first attempt.
remark: What in Guthix's name is that thing?
I've seen odd things follow adventurers, but that's a new one.
kid/remark: What is that? Mum, what is that?
wizard/remark: There's old magic in that creature, so kindly mind my books.

compliment: A little dragon! Mind it doesn't breathe on anything.
A dragon at heel. The White Knights would be green with envy.
insult: Your dragon's seen better days. Been dead a while, has it?
A dragon that small? I've had more trouble from a goose.
remark: Is that dragon of yours all right? It's looking a bit peaky and bony.
Is that dragon meant to be that colour, or is it just cold?
kid/remark: A real dragon! Has it burned you, or only other people?
kid/compliment: Can I ride your dragon? Please? I'm small and hardly weigh anything.
nan/remark: That dragon looks half-starved, dear, so do feed it something.
toff/compliment: A dragon, citizen! Rather a small one, but a dragon all the same.
fremennik/compliment: Hah! A little dragon of the north. A fine companion, outerlander.

compliment: Rather fine, a little storm cloud that follows you about like that.
I don't know what that is, but it's loyal, and that counts for a lot.
insult: Your little cloud can't settle on a shape. Takes after you, I expect.
Your companion's a cloud. I've seen weather with more purpose.
remark: What is that? It keeps changing its mind.
Is it raining out of that swirly thing? Keep it away from my washing.
kid/remark: Yours is a cloud! How do you stroke a cloud?
wizard/remark: Pure chaos, bottled and walking. Who thought that was wise?
nan/remark: I don't like the look of that swirly one, dear, not one bit.

compliment: Terrifying little beast, that, and it dotes on you.
I'd not sleep near that thing, but it follows you like a lamb, look.
insult: I hope you're pleased. That little horror's given me the shivers.
That thing looks like a bad dream. Find it under the bed, did you?
remark: Keep that away from me. I'll not sleep tonight.
Is it floating? Things shouldn't float.
kid/remark: I'm not scared of that thing. Make it go away though, just in case.
vicar/remark: Saradomin preserve us. What is that following you?
nan/remark: Ooh no, dear. That one's not coming in my kitchen.

compliment: Three heads on that dragon and it still comes when you whistle.
A dragon with three heads, and every one of them looks to you.
insult: Three heads, and not one of them thought to find a better owner?
Three heads. Between them they might make one sensible owner.
remark: Three heads on a baby dragon. That's two more than I'd like.
Do you have to feed all three heads, or just the one?
kid/remark: Three heads! Do they argue?
nan/remark: Three mouths to feed on that wee dragon, dear, and rather you than me.
toff/remark: A prince among dragons, I suppose. It bows to no one, I'll wager.

compliment: Devoted, that spider, eight legs and it still keeps pace with you.
Would you look at that, a spider that minds its owner!
insult: A spider for company. Couldn't afford a cat?
That spider has more manners than most adventurers I meet.
remark: There's a big spider following you, just so you know.
Where did you find a spider that size... no, don't tell me.
kid/remark: Is the spider poisonous? Does it eat flies and can I have one?
nan/remark: A spider, dear? Keep it out of my bath.
vicar/remark: Something unholy about that spider, so do keep it off the pews.

compliment: Not pretty, that, but it's faithful, and prettier things aren't.
You must be something, for a creature like that to mind you.
insult: Is that yours, or has something followed you home from a crypt?
remark: Whatever that is, it's not from round here.
Keep that ghoulish creature of yours off the graves, would you?
kid/remark: Ew! What is that? It's horrible and I love it!
vicar/remark: That has the stink of the undead about it, so mind my churchyard.
heartland/insult: That came from Morytania, didn't it. You can smell it from here.

compliment: All those heads, and every one of them looking up at you!
A hydra that follows you. You must be a steady hand.
insult: All those heads, and still not a sensible one among the lot of you.
Are you sure it's following you, or were you just outvoted?
remark: All those heads. How does it not fall over?
Do all those heads agree on where it's going?
kid/remark: How many heads has it got? I counted and lost count.
banker/remark: One creature, several heads. We count it as one, for the record.
wizard/remark: A hydra in miniature, and if it loses a head, does it grow two more?

compliment: Most folk run the other way from a kalphite, and yours follows you!
That beetle's gleaming. Someone's been polishing it.
insult: A beetle the size of a dog. I do hope you've told the neighbours.
Your beetle's eyeing my sandwich. Trained it yourself, did you?
remark: That's a very large beetle.
Is that a kalphite? They get a good deal bigger than that, mind.
kid/remark: A giant beetle! Does it fly? Make it fly at him and not me!
nan/remark: Keep that beetle off my vegetables, dear.
trader/remark: Kalphite shell. I know a man who'd pay for that, my friend.

compliment: Fair play, taming a little walking volcano.
That little volcano glows like a hearth. Handy on a cold night, eh?
insult: Do you feed that creature coal, or does it just smoke like that?
A walking volcano? I've met calmer adventurers, mind, though not many.
remark: Have you tried water on that little volcano, with all the smoke?
kid/remark: Does your tiny volcano erupt? Can you make it erupt right now?
dwarf/remark: Rock and fire walking about together is unnatural, but lovely with it.
heartland/remark: Keep that little volcano off the grass or it'll scorch.

compliment: A little gargoyle for a friend. Handsome thing, in a stony way.
Gargoyles usually sit on a roof and sulk, yet yours trots after you.
insult: Hard to say who has the stonier face out of you and that gargoyle.
remark: I can hear that thing flapping from here.
Is that a gargoyle? They're meant to stay on the roof.
kid/remark: If that bird's made of stone, why's it flapping its wings about?
vicar/remark: We've a gargoyle on the church roof. I'd best check it's still there.
nan/remark: All that flapping. It'll give me a headache, dear.
heartland/insult: A gargoyle belongs on the church, so you pinched that one, I'll bet.

compliment: That little brute stomps about like it owns the place, bless it.
Fierce little thing. It'd take on a troll for you, I reckon.
insult: Your creature's shouting at me. Did you teach it, or did it teach you?
Small, loud, and stamping about. Which of you is in charge?
remark: Your little general's shouting something, but I can't hear a word.
That little ogre stomps like anything, so mind the floorboards.
kid/remark: What's it shouting about? Shout back at it, shout louder!
guard/remark: Keep that thing quiet. We've had complaints about the stomping.
toff/insult: Does that thing ever stop bellowing? Rather like the peasantry.

compliment: Fine feathers on that bird. You keep it well, don't you?
That's trust, a bird that size staying at heel for you.
insult: Is it a bird? It's too big for a bird. Did you feed it too much?
Big bird, that. Does it carry you, or do you carry it?
remark: That's a very large bird. Looks like it's thinking.
Those wings would take the hat off my head.
kid/remark: Is that huge bird a chicken? It's much too big for a chicken.
rough/remark: Keep that bird off the seed or it'll have the lot.

compliment: Rather dignified, that little winged lady with the sword.
Wings and armour both. She's better turned out than most knights.
insult: Has your companion noticed it's better armoured than you are?
A little winged knight at heel. She's the one in charge, I take it?
remark: Is that a tiny angel with a sword following you about?
Wings on that one. Does it fly, or just look like it might?
kid/remark: Is that a fairy? It's got a sword! Fairies don't have swords!
vicar/compliment: A little winged warrior. Saradomin's own, by the look of it.

compliment: A little demon with two swords, and it heels like a hound!
Fierce little devil. Nobody'll trouble you with that about.
insult: Where did that demon even come from... no, actually, don't tell me.
remark: Little legs, big feet. I could hear it stomping from down the road.
kid/remark: A tiny demon! Does it do fire? Make it do fire at that bush!
vicar/remark: A demon at your heel, traveller, and rather you than me on that.
shady/compliment: A demon with two blades. Now that's a proper companion.
heartland/insult: A demon following you about. The vicar will have questions.
heartland/remark: Is that a demon? It's a demon. Keep it off the church steps.

compliment: A kraken, on land, following you about. Not many could manage that.
A sea beast this far from water must be very fond of you.
insult: How is it walking? More to the point, how are you?
Has anyone told your kraken it's not in the sea any more?
remark: That thing's a long way from the sea.
Is that a squid? Squids don't walk, as a rule.
kid/remark: A squid! On legs! That's not allowed!
pirate/remark: Arr, keep that kraken pocketed, for I've seen what the big ones do.
rough/remark: Keep that off the boats. The lads won't go out with that about.

compliment: A little smoke devil, tamed. Handy if the fire ever goes out.
How did you ever tame a smoke devil like that?
insult: Is that smoke coming off your creature, or your cooking?
Who started all that smoke, the little devil or its owner?
remark: Is something burning? Oh, that smoky thing of yours never stops.
Is that little devil giving off smoke, because my eyes are watering.
kid/remark: Is that creature on fire inside? Is that why it's smoking?
nan/remark: All that smoke. You'll get soot on my washing, dear.
barkeep/remark: Take that outside. I get enough smoke off the hearth.

compliment: A serpent at heel, and most folk would've been bitten by now.
Handsome snake, that. Lovely colour on it, too.
insult: A snake for company. Did it pick you, or were you all that was left?
Did you train that snake to eye my ankles, or does it just do that?
remark: There's a snake following you. Thought you'd want to know.
That snake's a long way from the swamp.
kid/remark: Does the snake bite? Make it bite him, not me!
nan/remark: A snake, dear? Keep it out of my knitting basket.
trader/remark: Snakeskin, my friend. I know a tanner who'd pay well.

compliment: There's something loyal about a little shadow that follows you about.
Not much to look at, that dark blob, but it never leaves your side.
insult: Is that yours, or did something follow you out of a nightmare?
A dark lump trailing you. Decide yourself if that's a compliment.
remark: What is that? It's giving me the shivers.
Is that thing even solid? I'd not try to stroke it.
kid/remark: You've got a ghost! Is it dead, or just see-through?
wizard/remark: That thing's not wholly of this world. Keep it away from my scrying.
vicar/remark: That beast following you is from the spirit realm. I'll say a prayer.

compliment: Few could get a sea beast to follow them up the beach like that.
Fierce little thing. Nobody will bother you with that about.
insult: A spiky sea beast. Did you win it, or did it adopt you?
All teeth and temper, your creature, and I can see where it gets it.
remark: What is that? Something from the sea, by the smell.
Spikes on that one. Mind the furniture.
kid/remark: Can I touch just the one spike? Ow! That one got me and it hurts!
fremennik/compliment: Hah! A dagannoth pup. You've been to Waterbirth, outerlander.
rough/remark: Keep that off the nets. It'll have them in shreds.

compliment: Sweet little mole, that. Mind it doesn't dig up the road.
A mole with a sunny disposition is a rare thing in these parts.
insult: A mole, and you've still got a garden? Not for long you haven't.
Did you dig that up, or did it dig you up?
remark: A mole! Shouldn't it be underground?
Fair enough, your mole can sniff my boots if it likes.
kid/remark: Is the mole blind? Can it see me if I wave at it like this?
nan/compliment: Ooh, a dear little mole. Keep it off my lawn, mind.
rough/insult: A mole. I've spent half my life trying to get rid of those.

compliment: A bear cub, sweet thing! Where's the mother got to?
That cub's growing. Bigger than your pack already.
insult: A bear cub. Lovely. And when it's grown, what then?
Your bear's sniffing my pie. I don't suppose it eats adventurers?
remark: A bear. In town. I'll just be over here, then.
Enjoy the quiet while that cub's still smaller than a house.
kid/remark: Can I hug the bear? It's only a baby one so I'm allowed.
nan/remark: A bear cub, dear? I hope you're feeding it porridge.
rough/remark: Keep that off the honey.

compliment: Still following orders, that little skeleton, loyal beyond the grave.
Handsome bones on that skeleton of yours, well kept and all.
insult: A walking skeleton. Have you been feeding it at all?
Your companion's all bones. You're not far behind, by the look of you.
remark: Does that skeleton following you know it's dead?
A skeleton with a sword. Mind, it looks well behaved.
kid/remark: A skeleton! Did somebody take its skin or did it fall off?
vicar/remark: The dead ought to rest, traveller, and yours is doing a jig.
nan/remark: Skin and bone, that pup of yours, dear. Not even skin, come to think.

compliment: A spider that stays at heel takes a patient owner.
Lovely markings on that spider, if you like that sort of thing.
insult: Why do you think a spider that size follows you about?
Nobody else would walk with you, so you settled for the spider?
remark: A spider the size of a dog. Now I've seen everything.
kid/remark: Big spider! Big spider! Everyone come and look!
nan/remark: A spider, dear? I've a broom for those.
rough/remark: Blimey. That'd clear the barn of rats, that would.
heartland/remark: That spider's eyeing the rafters. Don't let it in my cottage.

compliment: A scorpion at heel, and you minding that tail very carefully.
Not many could tame a scorpion. Steady hands, you've got.
insult: Mind the tail. The scorpion's, I mean. Yours is harmless enough.
A scorpion for company. Were the kittens all taken?
remark: That tail's up. Is that good or bad?
Keep that scorpion off the path where folk have sandals on.
kid/remark: Has the scorpion stung you? Show me where it got you!
nan/remark: Mind where you let that sit, dear. Scorpions and chairs don't mix.

compliment: A fiery pup, and it heels. Who's a good... whatever you are.
That pup's a credit to you, and warm company on a cold night.
insult: Your dog's on fire and you're just going to stand there?
A dog from the hot place. Does it fetch, or just burn the stick?
remark: Your dog's on fire. Is that normal?
That pup's warm enough to toast bread on.
kid/remark: Does the fire dog bite, and does the bite burn as well?
kid/compliment: I want one. Mum said no. Mum says no to everything.
nan/remark: Keep that pup off the hearth rug, dear, as it's burning already.
vicar/remark: That hound came up from somewhere I'd rather not name.

compliment: Odd little creature, but it looks after you, and that's what counts.
You've a soft heart, taking in a little abyssal thing like that.
insult: Did that follow you home, or did you follow it?
Your companion's all tentacles. Hard to say which end you talk to.
remark: What is that, all tentacles? Keep it off the mats, would you?
That thing looks like it crawled out of somewhere dark.
kid/remark: Tentacles! Can it hold things with them, like a cup?
wizard/remark: That's from the Abyss, or near it. Keep it away from my runes.

compliment: A well-behaved little demon is rarer than it sounds.
Follows you like a shadow, that dark little fellow.
insult: Does that little demon know you're in charge, and does it agree?
Your companion's a little dark one. Keeping you honest, I hope.
remark: Your creature's casting a very large shadow for its size.
kid/remark: Is your baby demon evil, or only a bit evil?
vicar/remark: A dark little spirit, that. I'd keep it out of the chapel.
shady/compliment: Spawn of darkness at your heel. Perhaps you're not so dull after all.
heartland/remark: Mind the church with that little demon, if that's what it is.

compliment: A spider that minds you? Now there's trust for you.
Lovely colour on that spider, not that I'd go stroking it.
insult: It's got eight legs and it still can't get away from you.
A spider that size for company. Were the dogs all spoken for?
remark: A spider that size. Nobody else bothered by that?
That spider's eyeing the eaves. Don't let it near my roof.
kid/remark: A spider! Can it make a web big enough to catch a cow?
rough/remark: That spider'd clear a barn of rats. I'll lend ye a barn to try it in.

compliment: A sea spirit, following you about. The fishermen will be jealous.
Angry little thing, but it follows you faithfully, takes all sorts.
insult: Have you fed that furious creature of yours, or at least apologised?
That little creature's small and cross, and I know how it feels.
remark: That thing looks cross. Is it always like that?
Smells of the sea, that creature, so keep it off the bread.
kid/remark: Why's that little one so angry? Was it something you did?
rough/remark: The sea spat that one out, and no wonder.
pirate/remark: Arr. A sea spirit, small as it is. Keep it sweet or it'll sink ye.

compliment: A phoenix! Beautiful, and lovely and warm to stand next to.
That bird glows like a hearth. Lovely on a cold night, that must be.
insult: Your bird's on fire, but I'm sure that's fine.
A phoenix. Does it rise from the ashes, or just make them?
remark: Is that bird meant to be glowing?
kid/remark: A fire bird! Does it lay fire eggs?
nan/remark: Keep that bird off the curtains, dear.
wizard/compliment: A phoenix, which dies and comes back by all accounts, a handy trick.
heartland/remark: Keep that fire bird off the thatch, because I like my roof.

compliment: A crystal beast. It catches the light like a chapel window.
Would you look at that, a crystal creature heeling like a hound!
insult: Your creature's see-through. Shame the same can't be said of you.
remark: Odd creature... why does it shimmer like that?
kid/remark: If that creature's made of glass, can I see its dinner inside?
wizard/remark: Living and walking crystal, which is elven work, surely.
trader/remark: A crystal creature? I'd give a fair price for a leg... joking, mostly.
heartland/insult: Made of glass, that. One trip on the cobbles and you're sweeping it.
heartland/remark: Is that thing made of crystal? Don't let it near the cobbles.

compliment: I don't know what that is, but it's magnificent in a terrifying way.
Devoted, that creature, keeping pace with you like a shadow.
insult: Your creature moves faster than you do. I'd have a think about that.
Did you lose a bet, or did you pick the one with all the arms?
remark: That creature of yours moves too quick for my liking.
Wings and claws and I don't know what, so keep it off the path.
kid/remark: It's got too many arms! Count them and then count them again!
vicar/remark: Saradomin preserve us. That's no creature of this world.
wizard/remark: That beast's older than it looks, much older, so mind where it steps.

compliment: A little walking statue. Fine workmanship on that.
Who trained that little guardian to keep step like a soldier?
insult: Lonely, were you, that you needed a statue to follow you about?
A walking statue. Does it do anything, or just judge quietly?
remark: Did that statue just move, or do I need a sit down?
Desert work, that. You can tell by the gold.
kid/remark: Statues don't walk, so why's that one walking about after you?
dwarf/compliment: By Guthix, stone that walks is craftsmanship and no mistake.
wizard/remark: An automaton with old desert magic in it, so keep it away from mine.

compliment: A hot-country creature that's fond of you? Both rare round here, that.
Odd little creature, that, but it's ever so fond of you.
insult: Did you ask that desert creature before dragging it all this way?
A desert creature, far from home. It misses the sand more than you.
remark: That's come a long way. Desert, by the look of it.
What is that? Not from round here, I'd say.
kid/remark: Is that creature from the desert? Can I touch it even if it's hot?

compliment: A grub with arms, and it adores you. Takes all sorts to make a world.
Odd creature, but it's loyal. That's worth more than looks.
insult: Is that a grub? With arms? Which of you thought that was a good idea?
A grub with arms. I'd say it suits you, but I'm far too polite.
remark: A grub that big, you'd want a very large bird.
That thing's got arms. Grubs don't usually have arms.
kid/remark: A worm with arms! Does it hug? Make it hug me and not him!
nan/remark: I don't like that spiky one, dear, with all those bits.
fremennik/remark: That beast came from the northern ice, outerlander, so keep it cold.

compliment: All teeth, that little fellow, and every one of them devoted to you.
Fine set of teeth on that. It keeps close to you, too.
insult: All teeth and stare, that beast, and it's judging you, and rightly.
All those teeth. Did you choose it, or did it choose you?
remark: I don't care for the way that little creature's watching me.
Mind your fingers with that many teeth on a creature that size.
kid/remark: Look at its teeth! Don't let it bite me because I'm only small.
toff/remark: Keep that creature off the hunting grounds, or the hounds would talk.

compliment: Remarkable, a headless little fellow with an axe, and it heels.
No head and all heart, that beast of yours, loyal as they come.
insult: Your companion's got no head. Between the pair of you, that's one.
A headless thing with an axe. Is it following you, or hunting you?
remark: Where's its head? Has it got a head?
Keep that axe away from the fence posts.
kid/remark: If your dog's got no head, where does it put its dinner?
vicar/remark: A headless thing. Ye gods. I'll not ask where you found it.
rough/remark: Blimey. Lend it to me for the firewood.

compliment: How does a sea serpent keep pace with you on dry land like that?
Odd creature, but it keeps close, so it must be fond of you.
insult: Is that from the sea? It looks like it lost an argument with it.
Your creature looks like it's seen things. Where did you drag it from?
remark: What is that? Something from very deep water.
That thing's a long way from the sea.
kid/remark: Does your tiny sea monster eat ships, tiny ships?
pirate/remark: Arr, seen bigger than that leviathan, though not many.
rough/remark: The nets wouldn't hold that sea beast, so keep it off the boats.

compliment: A little shadow that follows you. Rather beautiful, in its way.
Strange little thing, but it clearly adores you.
insult: Is that your companion, or your shadow finally giving up on you?
Your creature's half there. Not sure which half of you it takes after.
remark: Is that thing solid? It doesn't look solid.
What's that shadowy thing at your heel? I'd not stroke it, myself.
kid/remark: Hello, ghost! Is it a ghost? I can see right through it!
wizard/remark: Shadow given form, how interesting, but do keep it off my notes.
vicar/remark: A shadow that walks. I'll light a candle for you.

compliment: A rat, and a handsome one. Didn't think I'd ever say that.
That rat's cleaner than most adventurers I've met.
insult: A rat for company. The sewers must've been thrilled to see you.
Does your rat own the place, or does it just sit like it does?
remark: A rat that size, I'd be charging it rent.
Keep that rat out of my pantry.
kid/remark: A big rat! Does it sit? Make it sit and then make it beg!
nan/remark: A rat, dear? Keep it close because I've a cat for those.
barkeep/remark: Not that rat in my kitchen, the cook'll have a fit.

compliment: That creature has lovely manners. Better than most adventurers.
insult: Your companion bowed and you didn't, so I know who's got the manners.
A feathered snake. Did you pick the polite one on purpose?
remark: Is that a snake with feathers? That's a snake with feathers.
Odd beast. It looks like it's about to say good day.
kid/remark: Does the feathery snake fly, or bite, or both at once?
toff/insult: Now there's a creature with breeding. Rather more than its owner.
trader/remark: Feathers like that would fetch a price, my friend, not that I'd ask.
heartland/compliment: A feathered serpent. It's got better posture than the Duke.

compliment: A little warrior in armour, and it heels? That is impressive, that.
That little fellow stands like a champion. You must have earned him.
insult: A soldier the size of a boot, and it stands straighter than you.
A tiny soldier at heel. It's the one keeping you alive, I take it?
remark: Is that a tiny man in armour, with a spear and everything?
That one looks like it's won a fight or two.
kid/remark: Will the tiny knight fight me? No, wait, don't make it fight me.
guard/remark: Keep that spear pointed down. Even on a thing that size.
toff/compliment: A miniature champion. Rather splendid, citizen.

compliment: That demon looks down on everyone but you, lucky thing.
A proud little creature. It's chosen well, I'll grant.
insult: Your creature looks down on me. It's smaller than my boot.
A little demon with a big opinion of itself, so you've a type, then.
remark: That little demon's the size of a cat and it's sneering at me.
Is that a demon? It looks very pleased with itself.
kid/remark: Your demon looked at me funny, so I'm looking back at it!
vicar/remark: A demon with pride in its eye. I'd watch that, traveller.
shady/compliment: A demon that holds its head high. Finally, something worth seeing.

compliment: Frosty little thing. Keeps the butter cool, I'd think.
A creature of ice has taken to you. Warm heart and a cold friend, eh?
insult: Is that thing made of ice? Mind, it's the warmer of you two.
Your creature's leaving puddles. You can explain that to the landlord.
remark: Is that little fellow frozen? Because it's dripping all over my step.
Stand upwind of that creature. Brr, there's a cold coming off it.
kid/remark: That creature's made of ice! Can I lick it if nobody tells Mum?
nan/remark: Wrap that little one up warm, dear... oh. It's made of cold, isn't it.

compliment: I don't know what that is, but it'd die for you, wouldn't it?
Loyal, that dark little thing, following you like a shadow.
insult: A little dark one. Did it follow you home, or did you follow it?
Something from the deep places. I'd ask how, but you'd tell me.
remark: I don't like the look of that one.
kid/remark: Is that a monster, and is it your monster, or a wild one?
vicar/remark: Something unholy at your heel, traveller, so I'll pray for you both.
heartland/remark: Keep that thing in the daylight, where I can see it.

compliment: A tiny queen of insects, and she's chosen you of all people!
Fine shell on that creature. Someone's been polishing.
insult: An insect the size of a sheep. The neighbours must be delighted.
Your bug's got better posture than you, just so you know.
remark: That's a very large insect.
Is it laying eggs? Tell me it's not laying eggs.
kid/remark: Does your giant bug lay eggs, and can I have one to hatch?
nan/remark: Keep that off my cabbages, dear. Bugs that size eat a row a night.

compliment: Oh, a little chompy chick, sweet thing!
Keep that lovely little bird close, the ogres would eat it.
insult: That bird's loud for its size. Takes after its owner, eh?
A chompy chick. Did you hunt it, or just outrun it?
remark: Is that a chompy? Tiny thing, and loud with it, isn't it?
That chick's pecking at my boots, which is fair enough I suppose.
kid/remark: Your birdy's shouting at you! Shout back at it, go on, louder!
nan/compliment: Ooh, a dear little bird! Mind the cat doesn't get it.

compliment: A fine hound. Good nose on it, I'd say.
Lovely animal, that dog. I'll bet it could find anything at all.
insult: Good dog, that. I'd follow it rather than you.
That hound finds things, does it? Can it find your manners?
remark: What's that hound found, with its nose to the ground like that?
Fine dog. Does it dig? Keep it off my garden if it does.
kid/compliment: Who's a good boy? He is! He's such a good boy, aren't you, boy!
rough/remark: Keep it off the sheep, that one.
guard/remark: Fine animal, that dog, but keep it on a lead in town.

compliment: Your guardian watches you like a dog over a bone, and that's loyalty.
You've earned a proper little guardian like that one.
insult: It's guarding you, is it? It's got its work cut out.
A little horror from somewhere dark. Did it come with a warning?
remark: That creature's got a look about it. I'd not turn my back on it.
Is that creature of yours... it's watching me, isn't it?
kid/remark: Does your little monster bite, or does it just guard?
wizard/remark: Abyssal, that. Keep it well away from the altar.

compliment: Oh, what a colourful bird, look at those feathers!
Ooh, that bird's a picture, like a sunrise on wings!
insult: That bird's prettier than you, but I'm sure you've heard that.
Is that bird following you, or are you following it?
remark: Bright bird, that. Not from round here.
That bird's watching me. Birds don't usually watch.
kid/remark: Does the rainbow bird talk? Say my name, bird, say my name!
trader/remark: Feathers like those, my friend. I know a hatter who'd pay.

compliment: A gull at heel. Most of them just steal your fish.
Fine bird, that, and well fed too by the look of it.
insult: A seagull for company. Did it steal your dinner and refuse to leave?
Your gull's eyeing my lunch. Trained it yourself, did you?
remark: Is that scrongly little chicken following you?
kid/remark: A seagull! Mine! I want it! It's a chicken, isn't it?
pirate/remark: Arr. A gull. Follows ye for the scraps, same as the rest of us.
rough/remark: Keep that off the nets. Gulls and nets, there's no winning.
heartland/remark: That gull's eyeing the fish stall, so keep it close.

compliment: Lovely thing, a boar with a garden on its back.
That boar smells like a herb garden, which is nicer than most boars.
insult: Your boar's better dressed than you, or greener at any rate.
A pig in a herb coat. Dinner follows you about, does it?
remark: That boar's covered in herbs. Are you planning to eat it?
Is that a pig? With a hedge on it?
kid/remark: A green pig! Can I ride it? Too late because I'm already on it!
nan/remark: The herbs on your boar want proper drying, dear, and I'll not say how.
barkeep/remark: Seasons itself, does that boar? Handy for a kitchen like mine.

compliment: Oddly touching, a floating eye trailing you about like a hound.
Strange little spirit, but it's chosen well.
insult: What use is a floating creature that won't even carry your bags?
A floating something. Did you summon it or just find it?
remark: What is that? It's floating and I don't like it.
Is that floating thing watching me, or is it just all eye?
kid/remark: A floating eye! Make it blink at me and then at him!
wizard/remark: Soul magic in that little spirit, or I'm a goblin, so mind my desk.

compliment: A spider with manners. It bowed, I swear it did.
Very fine spider. Well groomed, if you can groom a spider.
insult: A gentleman spider, and you. One of you is dressed for company.
If I had to lend to one of you two, I'd pick the spider.
remark: That spider following you is enormous. It looks respectable, mind.
Eight legs and it still walks like it owns the road.
kid/remark: Spider! It's got fangs! Does it crawl in your mouth at night?
nan/remark: A spider, dear? I'd not have it on the bed, not even a polite one.

compliment: A little giant! Tiny, but it stands like a king.
You keep fine company, with that little fellow strutting like royalty.
insult: A tiny giant. Make up your mind.
Does your giant know it's the size of a boot?
remark: Is that a giant? A very small one?
Is that a short temper on that little one, or a very long one?
kid/remark: That's not a tiny giant! That's just a man that's gone small!
fremennik/remark: Hah! A giant in your pocket. Tell the hunters, outerlander.
toff/remark: A king in miniature. One wonders where its kingdom is.

compliment: Ooh, fluffy! Don't those go bang?
Ooh, what a sweet little fluffy thing, and such a lovely colour!
insult: I'd stand that chinchompa a bit further from the fire, and yourself.
Fluffy, isn't it. So's a bale of hay, and look what happens to those.
remark: Is that a chinchompa? Keep it away from the lamp.
Fluffy little thing! Why is it twitching like that?
kid/remark: Can I hold the fluffy one? Does it go bang if you squeeze it?
nan/compliment: Ooh, isn't it soft. Keep it off the hearth, mind.
trader/remark: Hunters pay well for a chinchompa, my friend, though not for that one.

compliment: A beaver! Handsome creature, and what fine teeth on it.
Hard worker, a beaver. Good company for a woodcutter.
insult: Did you not feed that beaver? It's eyeing the table legs.
A beaver. Does it do the chopping while you watch?
remark: Your beaver's looking at my fence and I'd rather it didn't.
Keep that away from the door frame.
kid/remark: Do beaver teeth really grow forever? Show me its teeth and prove it!
rough/remark: Keep that off my woodpile.
dwarf/compliment: Now there's a creature that respects timber, with fine teeth on it.

compliment: Fine creature. The forest's taken a liking to you, I'd say.
Well kept, that. The woods look after their own.
insult: Out of the forest and into town. It looks more surprised than you.
remark: That's come straight out of the forest.
kid/remark: If that creature's from the woods, can I keep it and feed it?
heartland/insult: A woodland creature. The gamekeeper will want a word.
heartland/remark: Keep that away from the chickens.

compliment: I'll bet a squirrel that size takes some feeding.
Lovely markings on that squirrel, big as it is.
insult: A squirrel the size of a dog. Still quicker up a tree than you.
Your squirrel's eyeing my basket. Was it brought up properly?
remark: That's a big squirrel. Nobody else mentioning how big that is?
Keep that off the roof. It'll have the tiles off.
kid/remark: Big squirrel! Make it climb the church, go on!
nan/remark: Ooh, isn't it big. Keep it off the bird table, dear.

compliment: Fine long legs on that heron, hasn't it, keeping step with you.
Handsome bird. Patient, too, standing like that.
insult: A heron. Does it do the fishing while you hold the bucket?
That bird's caught more fish than you have today, I'd wager.
remark: Does that bird keep up on those long legs?
kid/remark: Why's the big bird on one leg? Is the other one broken or something?
rough/remark: Keep that heron off the nets or it'll have the whole catch.
pirate/compliment: Arr, that heron's a fine fishing bird and worth its weight in cod.
heartland/remark: That bird's eyeing the fish stall, you know.

compliment: A floating guardian. Where did you even find a lead for that?
Odd little thing, but it clearly looks after you.
insult: Your creature floats. Does it do the walking for you as well?
A floating rock with eyes. Did the wizards have a sale on?
remark: Is that thing floating? Things shouldn't float.
What is that? It's humming.
kid/remark: How's that thing floating? Show me where the string is!
wizard/compliment: A rift creature means you've been through the Abyss, brave or lost.
vicar/remark: A floating thing. I'd not bring that into church.

compliment: Solid company, a little walking rock like that.
Fine little golem. Well polished, too.
insult: A rock for company. Cheaper to feed than a dog, I'll grant you.
Your companion's a rock. It's the livelier of you two.
remark: Is your rock meant to be following you like that?
Did that rock just... tell me it didn't move.
kid/remark: The rock's walking! Can I kick it? No, that'd only hurt my foot.
dwarf/compliment: A golem! Hah! Now that's a mining companion, and fine ore with it.
rough/remark: Blimey. If my rocks did that I'd never mine another.

compliment: Somebody's been brushing that raccoon's coat, haven't they?
That one's got a clever face. Takes after its owner, I hope.
insult: Your creature's got a thief's face. I'll be checking my pockets.
Your raccoon wears a mask. Is it honest work for either of you?
remark: Is that little raccoon of yours eyeing my purse?
Is that mask on your creature nature, or its own choice?
kid/remark: Is it a robber with that mask on, and are you one too?
guard/remark: Keep that animal in sight. We've had things go missing.
banker/remark: Would you mind keeping that creature away from the counter?

compliment: A walking plant! Well watered, by the look of it.
Lovely little tree. Someone's been tending it.
insult: Did that plant grow on you, or did you pick it for company?
Your creature needs watering. So do you, by the look of things.
remark: Your plant's following you. Plants don't usually do that.
kid/remark: Does the walking tree talk? Trees don't talk... does it, though?
nan/compliment: Ooh, a dear little tree. Does it want a bigger pot, dear?
rough/remark: If my crops walked about like that I'd never get the harvest in.
heartland/remark: Keep that away from the goats.

compliment: Lovely cat. Well looked after, that.
A cat at heel must like you, and cats don't like many.
insult: Did you train your cat to give that look, or does it come natural?
A cat? The rats round here won't lose any sleep over that one.
remark: That cat's got its eye on something, and it isn't you.
kid/compliment: Here, kitty! Why won't it come to me when I call it?
nan/compliment: A cat! Good for the rats, dear, but has it had its milk?
barkeep/remark: Cats are welcome. They sort the cellar.
heartland/remark: Keep that cat off the fish stall.

compliment: A red cat! Never seen one that colour, handsome thing.
That cat's glowing. Warm lap on a winter night.
insult: Has that cat been near the fire, or is that colour catching?
A cat the colour of a hot coal. I'd not let it on the bed.
remark: Is that cat on fire, or does it just look it?
Where did you find a cat that colour? On second thoughts, don't say.
kid/remark: Is the fire cat hot? I'm touching it! Ow, it really is quite hot.
nan/remark: A red cat, dear? Keep it off the curtains.

compliment: A little stone angel, and it follows you. Someone up there likes you.
remark: Is that a statue? Statues shouldn't walk about like that.
Is that little stone thing meant to glow like that?
kid/remark: That thing's got wings but it's made of stone, so can it fly or not?
vicar/remark: Wings and a halo of light. I'd like a word with whoever carved it.

compliment: A little bull in a bow tie, smarter dressed than most round here.
Well turned out, that calf. Somebody's proud of it, and no mistake.
remark: Why is your calf wearing a bow tie? Is it off somewhere nice?
kid/compliment: A cow in a bow tie! Does it moo posh or just normal?
rough/remark: Good bit of beef, that. Don't look at me like that, I'm only saying.
nan/compliment: Ooh, a little calf all dressed up. Is it off to a wedding, dear?

insult: A maggot's following you. A big one. I'd have a wash, if I were you.
remark: Why is that maggot so big, and why is it following you?
Something's crawling about in that creature and I'd rather not look.
kid/remark: Ew, a giant grub! Can I keep it, even though Mum said no?
nan/remark: Keep that wriggly thing off my step, dear, and out of the larder.
vicar/remark: That came out of something that died, so I'll pray for you both.

compliment: A goat at heel. Good-natured one too, by the look of him.
insult: Your goat's chewing on something. Hope it's not my washing.
remark: That goat's looking at me like it knows something.
kid/compliment: A goat! Does it headbutt? Make it headbutt that man!
fremennik/compliment: A fine goat. Hardy stock. It would do well in the snow.
heartland/remark: Keep that goat off the vegetable patch, would you?

compliment: A little turtle! Takes its time, doesn't it, the wise creature.
Lovely shell on that turtle. Someone keeps it polished.
remark: Your turtle's sniffing at the soup pot and I'd watch that.
kid/compliment: Can the turtle go in its shell? Make it go in and come out again!
pirate/compliment: A turtle aboard ship is good luck, sailor, mostly for the cook.
barkeep/remark: Keep that turtle out of my stew pot, eh? Or in it, whichever you like.

compliment: Sturdy little swine, that. Well fed, by the look of it.
remark: That hog's not moving. Is it meant to follow you, or not?
Keep that little swine downwind, because it smells of the swamp.
kid/remark: A hairy little pig! Does it want the mushroom I've got in my sock?
rough/remark: Hairy little hog. Keep it out of my turnips.

compliment: Carrying a fish in a bowl all this way is devotion, that is.
remark: Walking about with a fishbowl? Well, I suppose each to their own.
kid/compliment: Can I feed the fish? Can I tap the glass just once, please?
nan/compliment: Ooh, a little fish. Don't let the cat see it, dear.
barkeep/remark: Keep that bowl off the bar. Fish don't drink, I've found.

compliment: Is that the mayor? Very kind of you to carry him about.
insult: You've stolen the mayor. Catherby's going to want him back.
remark: Isn't that the fish they made mayor, with that serious face on him?
Very official look about that fish. Something in the posture.
kid/remark: Is it true that fish is in charge of a whole town, like Mum says?
toff/remark: A fish in office? One has known worse and voted for worse.

compliment: Sensible, that, a rock that follows you about and needs no feeding.
insult: You're walking a rock. I'd not say that out loud, in your place.
remark: Is that rock following you, or are you following it?
kid/remark: Your rock's walking and mine just sits there, can yours do tricks?
fremennik/compliment: A good rock. Loyal. It will never leave your side, outerlander.

compliment: A wind-up cat! Clever work. The joints move ever so smoothly.
remark: Why is your cat ticking? Cats don't tick, as a rule.
That cat walks ever so stiff. Is it made of wood or something?
kid/compliment: Who wound the toy cat up, and can I wind it next?
gnome/compliment: Lovely gearing on that cat. Not bad for a human, that.

compliment: A chocolate egg that walks about. That's the best kind of egg.
kid/compliment: A chocolate egg with legs! Can I have a bite, just a little one?
nan/compliment: Ooh, a chocolate egg. Mind it doesn't go soft, dear.
toff/remark: Rather a garish egg, though one supposes it is chocolate.
heartland/remark: Your egg's following you. Keep it out of the sun, it'll melt.

insult: Your chair's following you, and I'd not sit in it for a fortune.
remark: That chair just moved on its own and I saw it!
Why is there a chair behind you? Who brings a chair out walking?
kid/remark: The chair's haunted! Do I want to sit on it? Yes and no and yes again!
vicar/remark: There's something in that chair. I'd not sit in it, traveller.
nan/remark: A chair that follows you about would be handy, at my age.

compliment: A smiling egg. Can't help but smile back, can you?
remark: Don't drop that egg. It's following you and smiling at me.
Careful with that egg, it's got a face. Someone painted a face on it.
kid/compliment: Your egg's smiling at me! Hello, egg! Are you going to hatch soon?
nan/remark: Mind that egg, dear. One tumble and it'll be breakfast.

compliment: Lovely dog. Well kept, and it never takes its eyes off you.
Good dog, that. You can tell by the wag.
insult: Your dog's better turned out than you are, traveller.
remark: What's that dog sniffing for, lost a bone, has it?
kid/compliment: Can I stroke the doggy? Make it sit and then make it beg!
guard/remark: Keep that dog on a short leash, citizen. It's got a nose for trouble.
nan/compliment: A good dog! Has it had its dinner, dear? I've a bone put by somewhere.
heartland/remark: Keep that dog off the butcher's stall, would you?

compliment: A puppy! All paws and ears. It'll be a fine dog one day.
Aw, look at that little puppy trotting after you!
remark: Your puppy's chewing something. I'd check your boots if I were you.
kid/compliment: Can I hold the puppy and name it? I'm calling it Biscuit anyway!
nan/compliment: Oh, a little puppy. Give it a cuddle from me, dear.
rough/remark: Big paws on that pup. It'll grow into them soon enough.

cat/remark: Is that creature yours? Tell it to stop looking at me.
Your creature follows you about in plain sight, which I'd never do.
cat/insult: I was here first, so keep your creature off my patch.
cat/compliment: Clever thing, your creature. It knows to keep its distance.

alliance/compliment: Hello, little Orion. You're far better company than the big one.
If the little Ocellus can be tamed, there's hope for anything.
Look at that, walking a little Ocellus about like a lapdog.
alliance/insult: Couldn't find a nice cat? It had to be a little Ocellus?
Look at those two, both hunched. Hard to say who's following who.
Stand up straight, little one. Or is that your keeper's slouch?
alliance/remark: Everything goes a bit wobbly when your little friend walks by.
Hello, little one. You're not going to turn on us too, are you?
Hush now, little one. Nobody's annihilating anybody today.
compliment: Odd little fellow following you, but he's very well turned out.
Ooh, a little fellow in a robe! Is he your apprentice?
That face of his would scare the crows, but the robe's lovely.
insult: Shuffles after you like a tax man, that little robed one.
Some folk keep a cat. Some keep... whatever that is in the robe.
That one's got a little goblin in a dressing gown following on.
remark: Does he talk, that little robed fellow? He looks like he's thinking.
Something small in a robe just went by. I'll not look again.
Your little companion walks like my back feels of a morning.

slayer_master/remark: Still on {task}? Then don't let me keep you.
I gave you {task}, not a stroll, so get moving.
How are you getting on with {task}? No, don't answer, just go.
Read up on {task} before you go in, since it saves a funeral.
slayer_master/compliment: Making short work of {task}, by the look of you.
That's the look of someone who's been at {task}, so keep it up.
slayer_master/insult: Still not done with {task}? I'd have finished twice by now.
Is it {task} still? You're taking your time about it.
guard/remark: You're hunting {task}? Do it outside the walls, if you please.
You're after {task}, are you? Don't bring any back with you.
Is that {task} I can smell on you? Wash before you come in.
Hunting {task}, are you? Sign the book on your way out, then.
If it's {task} you're after, there's no bounty, I've asked.
Is that {task} on your boots? Not on the cobbles, if you please.
We had complaints about the last one hunting {task}, mostly the noise.
Word from the captain: anyone after {task} reports back before dark.
After {task}? Don't lead them to the gate. We've had that before.
Is it {task} this week? I only ask because the sergeant keeps a list.
Hunting {task}... I'll note it. The captain likes to know who's armed.
After {task}? Whatever you bring back doesn't come through this gate.
There's a form for hunting {task}. There's a form for everything.
Carrying all that for {task}? Don't block the gate with it.
The sergeant wants a word with anyone hunting {task}. About the mess.
guard/insult: Hunting {task}? Not in my streets, you're not.
You, against {task}? I'll have the lads keep a bed in the infirmary.
Hunting {task}? And here's me thinking you'd come about the laundry.
If you're the best they've sent at {task}, I'll keep the gate shut.
Off after {task}? I'll tell the sergeant to expect you back soon.
guard/compliment: You're hunting {task}? Good. Fewer of them, less paperwork for me.
Off after {task}? Rather you than me. Mind how you go, adventurer.
Someone has to see to {task}, and I'm glad it isn't the watch.
Hunting {task}? Good. The captain's had enough letters about them.

slayer_master/compliment: Nearly through {task}, by the look of you, and good work too.
Almost done with {task}? Then come and see me after for more.
Not many {task} left for you, eh, so finish the job.
slayer_master/remark: Nearly there. Don't get careless at the end.
slayer_master/insult: Nearly done and still standing? I'm almost impressed by that.

slayer_master/remark: No task? Come and see me, I've plenty.
Idle hands, adventurer. I've monsters that need killing.
slayer_master/compliment: You look ready for a new assignment, and I've just the thing.
slayer_master/insult: The monsters aren't on holiday, so why are you?

compliment: You're looking well, traveller.
Lovely to see a friendly face.
You've got a kind face, you.
insult: Face like a wet weekend, you.
plain/insult: Plenty of other adventurers about besides yourself.
You've the sort of face that improves with a helmet.
remark: Could murder a cup of tea.
toff/compliment: What a charming young adventurer.
toff/insult: One doesn't often see the peasantry so nearly well turned out.
toff/remark: One has a whole kingdom to run. Well, a corner of one, at any rate.
trader/compliment: Looking's free, my friend, touching isn't, and buying's encouraged.
trader/insult: Yours came off the cheap shelf, and I'd know, since I sold it to you.
trader/remark: Everything must go! Well, some things, the ones that aren't selling.
barkeep/compliment: Good to see you, love, the usual?
barkeep/insult: What'll it be? Besides a wash.
You've a thirst on you and a tab to match, I'll bet.
barkeep/remark: Rats in the cellar again, but don't tell anyone, eh?
banker/insult: Oh. It's you. You never use the bank.
banker/remark: Deposits to the left. Complaints to the Duke.
nan/compliment: Ooh, haven't you grown!
Lovely to see you, dear. You've a bit more colour today.
nan/insult: Mind your manners, dear. I've turned nicer people into toads.
nan/remark: In my day we walked everywhere, dear... uphill.
vicar/compliment: Lovely to see a new face. Most of mine are on gravestones.
vicar/insult: Saradomin loves us all. He does have to work at it, with some.
vicar/remark: Do come along to the church fete, and bring a cake if you can.
wizard/compliment: You have an aura about you, traveller, and a good one at that.
wizard/insult: An adventurer. Fetching and carrying for cleverer people, I expect.
wizard/remark: Not now. I'm concentrating on a very difficult spell.
rough/compliment: Good honest face, you've got.
rough/insult: Some of us have work to do, so go and bother a goblin.
Treasure hunters. Ye'll be after my shed next.
rough/remark: Blimey. Not another one of you treasure hunters.
Rain's coming. My knee says so.
shady/compliment: You've potential, the wrong sort... my sort.
shady/insult: Your sort aren't welcome round here.
shady/remark: You never saw me here, understood?
dwarf/compliment: Fancy a pie? No? Well, more for me, then...
You'll do, human, for a human.
Sturdy sort, aren't you, nearly dwarven?
dwarf/insult: Big folk. Always in a hurry, never any good at it.
Talk to a dwarf, do you? Most humans just look over us.
You'd make a fine miner, human. Once you learnt to stoop.
dwarf/remark: If a job's worth doing, do it well and then have a pie.
Kelda stout's the only drink worth the name, and a pity it's so rare.
Gold and rock, human. Everything else is just talk.
gnome/compliment: Nice to see an outsider, human. You lot get taller every year.
You've a kind face, for one so tall.
Welcome, human! Try a cocktail before you go, Blurberry's finest.
You've a good step on you, for one of the big folk.
gnome/insult: You've the build for gnomeball, human, as the ball.
Humans. Big, slow, and always asking the way.
Mind the branch, human. Big folk never look up.
gnome/remark: The gliders don't stop for humans when they barely stop for us.
The children say a new world will rise from underground, bless them.
King Narnode sends his regards. He sends them to everyone.
Ever played gnomeball, human? It's a bit rough on the big folk.
fremennik/compliment: Hah! You have a warrior's look about you.
Well met. You look like one who has a tale worth a beer.
You have the walk of someone the bards would not forget.
fremennik/insult: You walk like a southerner, outerlander, all knees.
Hah! You'd not last one trial, outerlander, not even Manni's.
Southerners talk a great deal. I will wait for the useful part.
You look like someone Peer would set a short riddle for.
fremennik/remark: The spirits are restless today.
The longhall's loud tonight, so Manni must be buying.
The Longhall will be loud tonight, as it is every night.
pirate/compliment: Arr, ye've the look of a sea dog.
Ye've a steady eye, matey. Ever thought of a life at sea?
pirate/insult: Arr, ye'd not last a day at sea, landlubber.
Arr, ye walk like the deck's moving, and we're on land.
pirate/remark: Arr, seen any rum about?
Arr, the Customs men are on the warpath again.
kid/compliment: You're ace. My mum says you're not, though.
kid/insult: You smell funny.
Why are you walking like that?
kid/remark: Got any sweets?
I'm not allowed to talk to strangers.
burgher/compliment: You got a kind face. Not many round here do.
Nice to see a face that ain't grey.
burgher/insult: You ain't from round here. Too much colour in your cheeks.
burgher/remark: Someone put a notice up, can't read it, but it looked important.
Mud's deep today. Mud's deep every day.
burgher/gossip: There's letters on the church door. Nobody knows what they say.
slayer_master/remark: Know your enemy. Half the job is knowing what kills you.
Every creature has a weakness. Find it before it finds yours.
Remember that some monsters can only be hurt the right way.
A sharp eye and a sharp blade, and not much else matters.
slayer_master/insult: You'd not last a day on a proper assignment.
Have you even got a nose peg?
heartland/remark: Looks like rain. It always looks like rain.
More goblins about these days, they say.
tzhaar/remark: JalYt again. Always JalYt. Where do all the JalYt come from?
Warm day. Every day warm. Is good. JalYt still complain.
You walk past TzHaar, TzHaar walk past you. Fair.
tzhaar/compliment: This JalYt not asking questions. Best JalYt all day.
JalYt looks warm today. Good. Keep it that way.
tzhaar/insult: Another JalYt. Lava does not care. TzHaar does not either.
ogre/remark: Chompies is scarce today. Me belly is complaining.
Yous is a creature. Me is an ogre. Dat is how it is.
Ogre is bored. Bored ogre is hungry ogre. Walk faster, creature.
ogre/insult: Grrr. Creature is too skinny to bother wiv. Come back fatter.
Yous walks funny, creature. Like a toady wiv a stabber in it.
ogre/compliment: Hur, hur. Creature got a goodly face. Not for eating. Just goodly.
moon_clan/compliment: Oh my, a quiet mind for a visitor, and thank you for that, dear.
You were going to say something kind, and I know, so thank you, dear.
moon_clan/insult: No need to say it, dear, for I heard it and did not care for it.
Your thoughts are very loud today, dear, and that is a mainland habit.
moon_clan/remark: I dreamt of you last night. Do not worry, it was quite dull.
tortugan/compliment: You stop to talk. Most tourists only hurry past.
A calm face, for a human. That is rare, and welcome.
tortugan/insult: Humans are in a hurry even standing still, so very well, off you go.
You will have moved on before I finish this sentence... there, gone.
tortugan/remark: A shell is a fine thing. Never in a hurry, always at home.
goblin/remark: Red armour best! No wait, brown. Brown best now. Me forget.
Worm stew again tonight. Me want beetle pie. Beetle pie give wind.
What you doing here, human? Me not sure that allowed.
Generals arguing again. Me not know what about. Nobody know.
Goblins mighty, war good, Big High War God greatest god!
Me not think today. Thinkers must die. Priest say so.
goblin/insult: Go away smelly human. Goblins busy.
Human ugly! All humans ugly. This one more.
goblin/compliment: You not bad, for human. Me not say that to many humans.
Human smell nearly like goblin. Is compliment.
troll/remark: Goat for dinner again. Me ask for human. Me get goat.
Trolls named after first thing we eat. Human named after what?
Goutweed in da stew tonight. Goutweed in everything. Is good.
Trolls not like boats. Boat go up an' down. Troll go down.
Fire bad. Rocks good. Dat is all troll need to know.
Trolls chuck rocks. Humans run. Dat is how it go.
Me not eat since breakfast. Breakfast was big, though.
Thrower trolls got best job. Chuck rock, sit down, chuck rock.
troll/insult: Human look like lunch. Early lunch.
What human do up here? Human not even crunchy.
Puny human. Lalli call you dat too, an' Lalli live in cave.
troll/compliment: Polite human. Polite humans taste... no. Polite humans is nice. Good.
Good human. Me not say dat much. Me not say much at all.
cat/remark: Is that fish I can smell on you... do say it is.
Would you shift? You're between me and the sun.
I was asleep. Now I'm not. Think about what you've done.
There's rats in the walls here. I'm not on duty today, mind.
Humans talk so much. Say what you mean and then feed me.
cat/compliment: Warm hands on you. I'll allow one stroke, then.
You walk quietly for a human, nearly like a cat.
cat/insult: Do you ever stop talking? The mice can hear you from here.
Dogs have owners, cats have staff, and you look like staff.
camel/remark: The sun's got no mercy today... it never has, mind.
I was composing a poem. You've rather trodden on the metre.
Shade, water and a little quiet... is that so much to ask?
camel/compliment: Thank you for stopping to listen, since hardly anyone does.
You walk gently. The sand thanks you, and so do I.
camel/insult: Did you say something? Only I was thinking of someone nicer.
You stare so. Were you raised in a tent?
leprechaun/remark: 'Tis a foine day for it, whatever it is ye're at.
Mebbe ye'd be wantin' yer stuff back, or mebbe not, so suit yerself.
A magic shed we have, and don't ask me where, as I don't rightly know.
leprechaun/compliment: Ye've the look of someone who waters their patch, and that's foine.
Ye walk like a body who's never lost a trowel, and that's rare.
leprechaun/insult: Ye must be dafter than ye look, and ye look plenty daft.
Were yez wantin' me, or just blockin' me light?
parrot/remark: Feed the fires! Squawk! Feed the fires, feed the fires!
parrot/compliment: Squawk! What will it be, what will it be?
parrot/insult: Squawk! Leave me alone, leave me alone!
mos_pirate/remark: What ship did ye pull in on, stranger?
Arr, that it be. Whatever it was ye said.
Keep yer voice down. The powder monkey's sleepin' it off.
mos_pirate/compliment: Aye, good day te ye too.
Ye've the look of a proper fillibuster about ye.
mos_pirate/insult: What's a landlubber like ye doin' here?
moon_clan_wary/insult: I can hear what you are thinking, so kindly stop.
I can hear you picking at our secrets like all the rest of them.
You think very loudly for someone with so little to say.
Outsiders are so easy to read. I wish you were worth reading.
You were about to ask something, and the answer is no.
Patience and interest. Show me either, and we might talk.
I read your mind. It did not take long.
The Fremennik never listen. You have the look of one who does not.
moon_clan_wary/remark: We do not suffer outsiders easily, so do keep walking.
Our secrets are our own. Do stop thinking about them.
A wise man listens. You might try it sometime.
You have not earned the right to anything of ours... yet.
Mainlanders always want something. I am waiting to hear what.
The Fremennik broke our altars. We keep our secrets closer now.
moon_clan_wary/compliment: You listen, at least. More than most of your kind manage.
Your thoughts are quieter than most outsiders', if only slightly.
Not entirely ignorant. For a mainlander, that is high praise.
There may be some insight in you, somewhere, very well hidden.
guard/remark: Twelfth hour on this gate, or thirteenth? I've stopped counting them.
Nothing to report. Nothing to report. I could say it in my sleep.
The sergeant says stand up straight, but the sergeant isn't here.
I count the carts in and then I count them out, and that's the job.
Feet went numb an hour ago. The rest of me is catching up.
Rations again. If you can call a turnip rations.
The captain's been on inspection since breakfast, in the pub.
Quiet shift, and don't you say it or you'll jinx it.
Word is there's trouble coming, but word is always that.
Paperwork for the paperwork now. The sergeant invented a form for it.
When the bells go I go home, and the bells haven't gone.
My relief's always late, and I'm starting to think he's a rumour.
Nobody's tried the gate all day, which is a bit insulting, really.
A cat came through the gate earlier. Didn't stop for questions.
Guarding, mostly. Standing, technically.
Someone's chalking rude words on the wall, and officially it's not me.
They promised a new helmet. That was three sergeants ago.
guard/compliment: Walking through without a fuss is rarer than you'd think.
Watched you cross the square with no bother, and I appreciate that.
You've the look of someone who pays their tolls, so carry on.
guard/insult: State your business. Loitering counts as business, by the way.
That's twice you've walked past this post, and I'm writing it down.
Nothing in your hands. Which is exactly what a thief would say.
Looking at the gate a lot, aren't you. Gates are for walking through.
Anything to declare? No? That's what they all say.
barbarian/remark: Yyeeeaaarrrggh! Go on, try it, and louder!
Sword, axe and arrow for us. The gods can keep their magic.
The longhall fire never goes out, and nor does the beer.
We came down from the mountains with Gunnar and we're not going back.
Nothing happens in this village without a fight breaking out, good!
Beer's in the longhall and so is the meat, so go on then.
barbarian/insult: What do you want, little one? Not a fight, that much I can tell.
Bah! Soft city folk never know what they want.
You look funny. No, really, has nobody told you?
Strolling through our village teaches you nothing, bah!
barbarian/compliment: You've the look of someone who'd scream and charge, good!
Not bad, for an outsider. The longhall might even let you in.

compliment: That headband keeps the hair out of your eyes, at least.
Nice headband. Very practical for the sweaty work, I'd imagine.
insult: Is that a headband, or did your hat shrink in the wash?
Just a ribbon round the head today? Rather you than me in this wind.
remark: A headband like that means you've done a day's work, I expect.
kid/remark: Why's your hat only got the bottom bit?

compliment: That woolly beanie looks warm enough for the Fremennik coast.
insult: Did your nan knit that beanie, or did it just happen to you?
remark: A beanie in this weather? Someone's feeling the cold.
nan/compliment: Pull that hat down over your ears, dear, or you'll catch your death.
fremennik/remark: A wool cap won't save your ears north of Rellekka, outerlander.

compliment: A nightcap! You're the only one round here who's had a proper sleep.
insult: Did you come straight from bed, or straight from the tavern floor?
You've the nightcap on. The rest of going to bed is up to you.
remark: Is that a nightcap? Did you sleepwalk all the way here?
barkeep/remark: Nightcap, is it? Usually that's something I pour, not something I see.
kid/remark: Are you going to bed? It's the middle of the day!

compliment: That imp mask's a good likeness. I've been bitten by worse.
insult: An imp face? The real ones at least have the decency to run off.
remark: You'll get chased round the Wizards' Tower in that imp mask, I'll bet.
wizard/remark: An imp mask. The genuine article would at least steal my beads.
kid/insult: You're not a real imp! Real imps are smaller and they run away!

compliment: Very convincing goblin mask, that, especially round the ears.
insult: Goblin mask, or is that just your face after a night out?
Did the goblins give you that face, or did you have it already?
remark: Half the goblins out east look happier than that mask does.
goblin/insult: Not real goblin. Face too clean and far too many teeth in it.
guard/remark: Take the goblin mask off at the gate, or I'll be asked to do it.

compliment: A fez! Very Al Kharid. Suits you better than it would me.
insult: A little red flowerpot on your head and a tassel to wave about.
Is the tassel on that fez for show, or is it how you steer?
remark: A fez from the desert markets, I'd say, with the tassel still on.
trader/compliment: That's a fez from Ali Morrisane's stall, my friend, or I'm no judge.

compliment: A crier's hat! You'll want a bell and a loud voice to go with it.
insult: A crier's hat, and not a word to say? That hat deserves better.
remark: Is the crier's hat for news, or do you just like the ribbon?
toff/remark: A crier's hat? Then do your job and announce me, citizen.
kid/remark: Hear ye, hear ye! Say it! Go on, say the hear ye bit!

compliment: Bright hat from Tai Bwo Wannai, that. They don't give those away.
insult: That hat's brighter than the rest of you put together.
remark: A jungle villager's hat this far north? That's a long way to walk.
kid/remark: Your hat's all stripy! Did you get it off a parrot?
pirate/remark: Arr, that's Karamja colours on yer head. Been trading sticks, have ye?

compliment: That carved wooden mask is proper jungle work, took weeks, that.
insult: Take that wooden mask off before you frighten the horses.
A painted wooden face, and still an improvement.
remark: The villagers down south run a mile from a mask like that, you know.
kid/remark: Is your face made of wood? Does it hurt when you smile?

compliment: That Menaphite hat keeps the sun off your neck better than mine would.
insult: Dressed for the desert sun, and here it's drizzling, as ever.
remark: That's a Menaphite hat. You've been down past Al Kharid, then.
trader/remark: Menaphite cloth, that hat, dyed properly. Ali Morrisane's, I'd wager.

compliment: A headdress and a beard. Nobody in the desert would look twice at you.
insult: That false beard fools nobody. It doesn't even match your eyebrows.
Is the beard yours? No. No, I can see the string.
remark: A headpiece and a false beard. Are we in disguise, or just warm?
guard/remark: False beard. I'm noting it down. Don't know why, but I'm noting it.
kid/remark: Your beard's falling off! Oh, it's a pretend one, can I have it after?

compliment: A beekeeper's veil! Those stripy chaps don't care who you are.
insult: Did you wear the veil to the hives, or are you hiding from someone?
remark: Beekeeper's hat. Where are the bees? Please say they stayed at home.
nan/remark: Oh, a bee veil, dear. Mind the honey, it gets everywhere.
rough/remark: Bees, is it? Keep 'em away from my sheep.

compliment: That grey zombie face is well done, even the eyes look properly dead.
insult: Are you wearing a zombie mask, or have you just had a long week?
remark: Grey face, sunken eyes... that's a mask you're wearing, isn't it?
vicar/remark: A corpse's face for a hat, traveller? The churchyard won't approve.
kid/insult: Zombie! Zombie! Oh, it's only a mask with a person inside it.

compliment: You look medical in that hat. Good, I've a knee that wants looking at.
insult: That hat says physician. The rest of you says apprentice.
remark: Are you a doctor, or did you just find the hat?
nan/remark: A hospital hat, dear? Have a look at my knee while you're here.
kid/remark: Are you a doctor? My brother's got a thing on his foot.

compliment: Antlers and a glowing nose! You've made my morning, truly.
insult: Antlers on, nose glowing, and not a sleigh in sight.
remark: Does that nose on your hat flash, or is it just a trick of the light?
kid/compliment: Antlers! Your nose is glowing! Can I pull them, just the once?
gnome/remark: A reindeer, human? I had no idea they came in your size.

compliment: A sheet with eyeholes. Simple, classic, and a bit unsettling, really.
insult: A bedsheet with holes cut in it. Did your mother see you leave?
Are you a ghost, or did the washing line get you?
remark: The ghosts at Port Phasmatys would laugh at that sheet, you know.
kid/remark: Woooo! Are you a ghost? You're a rubbish ghost, I can see your boots.
vicar/remark: Under that sheet is a living soul, I trust, and not something else?

compliment: Someone carved that pumpkin with care, before it ended up on a head.
insult: A whole pumpkin on your head, and honestly it's an improvement.
remark: Is that pumpkin on your head carved, or did it just grow that way?
Mind the candles. A pumpkin head goes up quicker than you'd think.
kid/compliment: A pumpkin head! Is there soup in it? Can I knock and find out?
rough/insult: That's a good pumpkin wasted, that is.

compliment: Pointy hat and a long nose... the witches in Draynor would be proud.
insult: That witch's hat came with a nose, and not a flattering one.
remark: A witch's hat, and no broom? Then how did you get here?
nan/compliment: Ooh, a proper witch's hat, dear. The nose is very like our Aggie's.
kid/insult: Your nose is massive! Is it the hat or is it you?

compliment: Flying cap, flaps down. You've been up in a balloon, I'll bet.
insult: Leather cap, goggles... did you fall out of the balloon, or jump?
remark: A flying cap, is it? I'd no idea people went up in the air on purpose.
gnome/remark: A balloonist's cap, human! Did Auguste finally get the thing airborne?
kid/compliment: You fly? In the sky? Can I come next time?

compliment: A hat with a propeller on it. That's a brave bit of headwear.
insult: Does the propeller on that hat spin, or is it as idle as you?
Little propeller on top, and I notice it doesn't even turn.
remark: I keep waiting for that propeller hat to lift you off the ground.
kid/compliment: A propeller! Spin it! Spin it! Why isn't it spinning for me?
gnome/remark: A propeller hat, human? Our gliders started off smaller than that.

compliment: A saucepan for a helmet. Honest cookware, and it'll turn a blade.
insult: Is that a saucepan on your head? Did the bucket people turn you down?
A pan on your head. Somebody's dinner is going cold somewhere.
remark: Say something. I want to hear if that saucepan rings.
barkeep/remark: Hang on. That's my saucepan. Where did you get my saucepan?
kid/insult: You've got a saucepan on your head! Is there soup in it as well?
dwarf/remark: A saucepan's iron and it's on your head, so it counts, I suppose.

compliment: A camel face, and a convincing one. Al Kharid's herd will adopt you.
insult: A camel's face for a hat. Did you choose the expression on purpose?
remark: Does that camel mask spit? The real ones do, I learned the hard way.
kid/remark: You've got a camel face! Do you eat sand? Camels eat sand, I think.
camel/remark: A camel's face, on a human. I have questions, but I'll keep them.

compliment: A snail shell helmet, cured properly. Mort Myre work, I should think.
insult: A snail shell on your head. Did the snail agree to that, or move out?
Shell on your head, slime in your hair... you've been in the swamp.
remark: That shell's off a swamp snail. Big ones down in Mort Myre, they say.
kid/remark: Is there still a snail in there? Can I see it if there is?
burgher/remark: Snail shell hat. We eat the snails here, and the shell's what's left.

compliment: A cake on your head, iced and everything! Is it somebody's birthday?
insult: A cake for a hat. Don't stand near me in the sun, you'll drip.
