remark: Is that cake hat real cake? I only ask because I've not had lunch.
kid/compliment: Cake! On your head! Can I have the top bit?
nan/remark: A cake on your head, dear? I'd have used a plate, but there we are.
barkeep/remark: Keep that cake hat off my candles. Icing's murder to get off a bar.

compliment: A rune helm with your face left free, so you can see what's coming.
insult: Rune on top and nothing over your face, so either brave or forgetful.
remark: A rune cap, half a helmet really. Did the rest of it cost extra?
dwarf/compliment: Proper runite, well beaten. Shame they stopped at the ears.

compliment: A Tyras guard helm. You've been a long way west, then, haven't you?
insult: A king's guard helm, with none of the king's guard inside it.
remark: That helm's the Tyras camp style. Long march from Tirannwn, that.
guard/remark: Tyras helm. Different outfit from mine, same job, standing about.
fremennik/insult: A helm from a king's bodyguard, worn by somebody nobody's guarding.

compliment: A dwarf-forged helmet, that, and it'll outlast the pair of us.
insult: A dwarven helmet on a head that size? It must pinch something awful.
remark: Dwarf work, that helmet. Heavy as a doorstop and about as pretty.
dwarf/compliment: By Guthix, that's one of ours! Keldagrim steel, so look after it.
dwarf/remark: That helmet belonged to a dwarf once. Hope he gave it up willingly.
kid/remark: Your helmet's too small for a human. Did you shrink in the wash?

compliment: Strange green metal on that helmet. I've not seen its like anywhere.
insult: Is it the helmet humming, or is that noise coming from you?
remark: Seers' Village metal, that helmet, from the old workshop, I'd wager.
wizard/remark: That helmet hums with something. Kindly don't stand near my books.
dwarf/remark: Never smithed that colour. Whatever ore that is, it isn't one of ours.

compliment: That's an old king's helm, by the look. Dug up, not bought, I'd say.
insult: An ancient helm, and you wear it like you found it in a hedge.
remark: Old iron, old style... that helm's older than the castle, I reckon.
toff/remark: A royal helm of some antiquity. One wonders which king is missing it.
kid/remark: Is that a king's helmet? Are you the king? You don't look like a king.

compliment: A ram's skull for a helmet. Horns and all. Nobody's arguing with that.
insult: A ram's skull on your head. The Lumbridge sheep will want a word.
Horns, a skull, and a smell. One of those is your fault.
remark: Where did the rest of the ram go? Asking on behalf of the farmer.
rough/insult: That's one of my rams, that is. Bring the rest of him back.
kid/compliment: Horns! You've got horns! Can you headbutt a wall with those?

compliment: A chompy hunter's hat, feathers and all. Ogres don't hand those out.
insult: Feathers in your hat? The chompies you shot would like them back.
remark: A chompy bird hat, that. You've been out Feldip way, shooting birds.
ogre/compliment: Good hat. Chompy feathers. You shoot many bird, me think.
kid/remark: Your hat's got feathers in! Did a bird explode on it?

compliment: A hood with an eye on the front. The runecrafters wear those, I hear.
insult: That eye on your hood keeps looking at me, and I don't care for it.
remark: An eye on the hood. Is that a Guardian's thing, or just a fashion?
wizard/remark: Guardians' robes. Do say you've not let anything out of that rift.
kid/remark: Your hat's got an eye! Can it see me? Can it see me if I hide here?

compliment: That headband's got a spirit's glow to it. You've been at Tempoross.
insult: A headband for fishing? Does it keep the fish out of your eyes?
remark: That's an Unkah headband, isn't it? The spirit anglers wear those.
rough/compliment: Spirit angler, are ye? Then ye've faced that storm and lived.

compliment: A gold miner's helmet! Someone's been catching falling stars.
insult: A gold helmet, for mining? You'll not want to drop that down a shaft.
remark: A prospector's helmet, but gold. The miners will talk of nothing else.
dwarf/compliment: A golden mining helmet! By Guthix, that'd light a whole shaft.
kid/compliment: Gold helmet! Are you rich? Can I have a little bit of the gold?
trader/compliment: A gold helmet, my friend! There's someone who's found their star.

compliment: A Hunters' Guild hat, that. They don't give those out for nothing.
insult: A hunter's hat, and you walked right past three rabbits on the way in.
remark: That's the Varlamore hunters' hat. You've been chasing rumours, then.
rough/remark: Hunters' hat. Hope ye're not after my chickens.

compliment: A solid gold helmet! Heavy, I'd think, but it does catch the light.
insult: A gold helmet. Heavy, isn't it? Your neck seems to think so.
remark: Solid gold on your head. The dwarves round Keldagrim make those.
dwarf/remark: Gold helmet. Dondakan's cannon still working, then, is it?
toff/compliment: Gold worn as armour. Vulgar, citizen, and yet I rather approve.
kid/compliment: Is that real gold? Can I bite it and see if it's real?

compliment: A unicorn mask with the horn and everything, which is fine, if odd.
insult: A unicorn's face, and the horn's the most honest thing about you.
remark: Is that a unicorn mask? There's real ones grazing north of here.
kid/compliment: A unicorn! A real one! Oh, it's a mask, but I still like the horn.
nan/remark: A unicorn, dear? Mother said the horns cure most things, but not that.

compliment: A cyclops head, big eye and all! Warriors' Guild work, I'd wager.
insult: One eye in the middle of your head. Does it make the stairs harder?
A cyclops face. Half the eyes, twice the staring.
remark: That cyclops head is looking right at me. Just the one eye, but still.
kid/remark: Where's your other eye gone? Did it fall out, or did you lose it?
barbarian/compliment: A cyclops head! Did you take it yourself, or buy it off a braver sort?

compliment: A leather coif in the god's colours. Blessed hide, that, I'd say.
insult: A hood painted in holy colours. Does the god know you're wearing it?
remark: That coif's in a god's colours. Picked a side, or just like the shade?
vicar/remark: A blessed coif, traveller. I hope those colours were chosen with care.

compliment: A fedora, worn properly. Tipped at the brim and everything.
insult: A fedora. Did you take it off the archaeologist, or did he give it up?
remark: A fedora like that belongs in a dig site, not a high street.
toff/insult: A fedora. One assumes the wearer has opinions on everything, citizen.
kid/remark: Tip the hat! Tip it! Do the thing with the hat!

compliment: A cavalier's hat with a highwayman's mask. Now that's a proper rogue.
insult: A mask and a feathered hat. Robbing the coach, or just late for it?
remark: A masked rider's hat. Stand and deliver, is it, or just stand?
guard/remark: Masked. Feathered hat. Keep your hands where I can see them.
toff/insult: A highwayman's mask, citizen? Do try not to rob me before luncheon.

compliment: A moon-faced mask, and old Kourend work by the carving on it.
insult: That moon mask is grinning at me and I'd rather it stopped.
remark: A pale moon mask. The druids under Forthos wore those, they say.
vicar/remark: A mask of the moon god, traveller. Guard your dreams, is all I'll say.
kid/remark: Your face is the moon! Is it night-time on your face?

compliment: Thick goggles like that mean you've been mixing something that spits.
insult: Those goggles make your eyes enormous, which I assume was the idea.
remark: Alchemist's goggles. The Varlamore potion folk wear those, don't they?
wizard/remark: Goggles for mixing potions. Someone has learned, then, the hard way.
nan/remark: Goggles, dear? Can you see out of those? Mind the step, just in case.

compliment: A hat from the magic arena! They say those ones talk back.
insult: Does that hat talk? I only ask because it seems the cleverer of you.
remark: I'm sure that hat just muttered something. Hats don't mutter, do they?
wizard/remark: An arena hat. Don't let it tell you your score in front of the others.
kid/remark: Your hat's talking! It said a word! Make it say my name next!

compliment: An ogre shaman's mask! You've been in the caves at Corsair Cove, then.
insult: An ogre's mask on a face that size? The ogres wear them bigger.
remark: That's an ogress's mask, the shaman sort. Does it still smell of ogre?
ogre/insult: Dat shaman mask. Too small for ogre head. You look like little shaman.
kid/remark: Is that a monster face? Did you fight a monster for it?

compliment: A fine animal mask, Varlamore made. Somebody held a very odd dinner.
insult: An animal mask, worn by a butler, I'd guess. Fetch my coat, would you?
remark: That mask's the sort the servants wear at those big villa parties.
toff/remark: A masked servant? Splendid. Do bring the sherry round, citizen.
kid/remark: Is that an animal face? Are you a person underneath?

compliment: A rune helm set with dragonstones! That's elf-chest work, that is.
Purple stones on a rune helm. Someone's been lucky in Prifddinas.
insult: Gems on your helmet. Does it stop a blow, or just a jeweller's eye?
remark: Dragonstones set in that helm. Mind who you let walk behind you.
toff/compliment: Dragonstones on a helm! At last, citizen, someone dressed for court.
kid/compliment: Purple shinies on your helmet! Can I count them, can I, can I?
trader/compliment: Dragonstones on a helm, my friend. Name a price and I'll cry at it.

compliment: A crown of elven crystal! The elves don't part with those lightly.
That crystal crown catches the light like Prifddinas at dawn.
insult: A crystal crown. Is there a kingdom to go with it, or just the hat?
remark: Elf-crystal on your brow. Which clan did you sweet-talk for that?
toff/compliment: A crystal crown. Finally, citizen, somebody who understands headwear.
toff/insult: A crystal crown on a commoner. The elves will sell anything, it seems.
kid/compliment: A see-through crown! Are you an elf queen, or an elf king, or what?
gnome/remark: Prifddinas crystal, human. Even King Narnode would look twice at that.

compliment: A metal dragon's face for a mask. They're hard enough to get near.
insult: A dragon mask in metal. Does your neck know what you've done to it?
remark: That dragon mask has a metal shine to it, and a hungry sort of look.
dwarf/remark: A metal dragon's face. Never thought I'd see one of those hold still.
kid/remark: A dragon! A metal one! Does fire come out? Go on, breathe some fire!

compliment: A Kourend house hood, crest and all. Someone's been very loyal.
insult: A hood with a house crest. Does the house know you're wearing it?
remark: That hood's in one of the Kourend colours. Long way from Zeah, this.
guard/remark: House colours on that hood. Keep it civil, the other houses have eyes.
toff/remark: A Kourend crest, citizen. One trusts you hold the matching title.

compliment: A monocle! Now there's a face that knows what it's looking at.
insult: A monocle. Only the one eye worth bothering with, then?
remark: A monocle on a traveller. Does it fall out when you're surprised?
toff/compliment: A monocle, citizen. Now you can look down on people properly.
kid/remark: Your glasses are only half! Where's the other half, did you sit on it?

compliment: Spectacles like those make a person look as if they've read something.
insult: Spectacles, and you still walked straight into me.
remark: Little spectacles. Needed, or just there to make you look wise?
wizard/remark: Spectacles. At last, someone else who has squinted at a page too long.
nan/compliment: Oh, spectacles, dear. Very distinguished. My late husband had a pair.

compliment: A smith's visor like that says you've stood at a forge and meant it.
insult: A smith's visor, and your hands are soft as a baker's.
remark: That's a forge visor. Keep it down near sparks and up near people.
dwarf/compliment: A proper smith's visor! Now that's somebody who respects the sparks.
dwarf/insult: A smith's visor, and not a single burn on those arms, I notice.

compliment: A fur hat with the flaps down. That's the one Uri wears, isn't it?
insult: That's Uri's hat. Did he give it up, or did you outrun him?
remark: Fur hat, flaps down, shifty look... you're an estate agent, I'll bet.
guard/remark: Hat like that usually comes with a clue scroll in the other hand.

compliment: A giant's boot for a hat. Well, it's dry, and nobody else has one.
insult: A whole boot on your head? Somewhere, a giant is hopping about.
A boot for a helmet. It still smells of the giant, you know.
remark: That boot on your head fits a giant. Did you ask for the other one?
kid/insult: You've got a boot on your head! It's huge! I bet it smells in there.
troll/remark: Boot hat. Boot big. Belong to cousin, maybe. Cousin have one foot now.

compliment: A forester's hat with bark on it. You've put the hours in among trees.
insult: A hat made of bark. Did a tree lose a fight, or did you?
remark: That's a forester's hat. The woodcutters round Draynor would envy it.
rough/remark: Bark on yer hat. Ye've been in the woods long enough to grow it.
gnome/compliment: A hat of leaf and bark, human? The Grand Tree approves, I'm sure.

compliment: An Ardougne knight's helm, full faced and red, the king's own colours.
insult: A red knight's helm. Did they knight you, or did you just paint it?
remark: That's an Ardougne knight's helm. Hardly see those outside the city.
guard/remark: Ardougne knight's helm. Not my city, not my problem, but I've seen it.
toff/remark: An Ardougne knight, here? Do give the East Ardougne court my regards.

compliment: An elite knight's black helm. You fought in the dark for that, I bet.
insult: A black knight's helm, the fancy sort. The Kinshra know you've got it?
remark: Black knight's helm, trimmed. Not the usual sort you see on the road.
guard/remark: Black knight helm. I'm meant to challenge that, so consider it done.
vicar/remark: A black knight's helm, traveller. The white knights will want a word.

compliment: A dark hood like that was made for sneaking into fortresses, I'd say.
insult: A dark hood over the face. Hiding from someone, or just from daylight?
remark: A cult leader's sort of hood, that, and you're not one, I hope.
guard/remark: Dark hood, face hidden. That's a search, that is, so hold still.
wizard/remark: That hood is a dark wizard's cut, and a rather senior one at that.

compliment: An Emissary's hood. You wore that among them and walked out again.
insult: A cult hood, and not so much as a chant? Half-hearted emissary, you.
remark: That hood's Varlamore cult cloth. The Emissaries don't hand those out.
vicar/remark: An Emissary's hood, traveller. I pray that's a trophy and not a vow.
shady/remark: The Emissaries' hood. Careful, meddler, some of us know that cloth.

compliment: A rusty helm that's taken blows and still holds, rather like you.
insult: That helm's more rust than iron. Did you dig it up, or did it dig you?
remark: That rusty helm came off a walking corpse, I'd wager, up in the fort.
dwarf/insult: Rust, shaped like a helm. I could smith you a better one in my sleep.
vicar/remark: That helm came off the walking dead, traveller, so do get it blessed.

compliment: A helm forged from moonlight, they say. It does have a glow about it.
insult: A moon helm. Does it wane, or is it full all month?
remark: That pale helm looks like the moon's come down to sit on your head.
moon_clan/remark: Moonlight, forged. Our people would know that helm anywhere.
kid/remark: Your helmet's glowing! Is it the moon? Did you steal the actual moon?
wizard/compliment: A helm of moonlight. Someone's been in the Moons' temple, I see.

compliment: A gilded mask with cat's ears. That's out of the tombs, that is.
insult: A cat-eared mask from the tombs. Did the dead agree to part with it?
remark: That mask's the old Menaphite style, cat ears and all, and very old.
vicar/remark: A mask of the desert gods, traveller. Icthlarin's or the other one's?
cat/remark: Ears. Good ears. Yours are wrong, but the mask has the idea.
toff/compliment: A Menaphite funeral mask. Grave robbery, citizen, but tastefully done.

item.pattern: ^(Twisted hat|Trailblazer hood|Shattered hood|Trailblazer reloaded headband|Raging echoes hat|Demonic hood) \(t[1-3]\)$
item.label: relic hunter's hat

compliment: A relic hunter's hat, with the glow. You've been somewhere strange.
That hat shines like a found relic. Somebody's been on an adventure.
insult: A glowing hat. Lovely for finding you in the dark, less so for hiding.
remark: Never seen a hat glow like that. Where on earth did you find it?
kid/compliment: Your hat's glowing! Is it magic? Make it do a spell, go on!
wizard/remark: That hat is enchanted, and not by anyone I'd recognise, which is rare.

compliment: That ornate helm was found, not bought, so you solved something.
insult: A very ornate helm for someone who looks lost.
remark: Fine engraving on that helm, the sort you dig up rather than forge.
dwarf/compliment: That's proper engraving. Whoever made that helm had a steady hand.
toff/compliment: An ornate helm, citizen. For once the peasantry dresses for dinner.

compliment: A desert water circlet! Clever, a drink that just sits on your head.
insult: A circlet that keeps you watered. The rest of you still looks parched.
remark: That circlet's got a water charm on it. Sophanem work, I'd wager.
wizard/remark: A circlet of water. Elegant enchanting, that, and not from round here.
kid/remark: Is your crown made of water? Can I drink it? Just a little sip, go on?
camel/remark: A circlet that holds water. Slowly, you learn what camels always knew.

compliment: A green man's mask, leaf and bark. The forest's taken to you, then.
insult: A face made of leaves. Does it shed in autumn, like the rest of you?
remark: A leafy mask, the old woodland sort. The druids used to carve those.
gnome/compliment: A green man's face, human! The trees must think you're one of them.
kid/remark: Your face is a bush! I bet there's a bird in it somewhere.

compliment: A diamond at your throat. Somebody's doing all right for themselves.
That white stone catches the light nicely, doesn't it?
insult: One of them's lying, that diamond amulet or the rest of you.
remark: Is that a real diamond, or glass? Don't tell me, I'd rather wonder.
kid/remark: Is that diamond real? Can I bite it? My dad says you bite them.
trader/compliment: Diamond, my friend? I could find you a ring to go with it.

compliment: That ruby at your neck is a bold bit of colour, I'll say that.
insult: Red stone at the throat. Is that so the blood doesn't show?
remark: Ruby, is it? Mind the pickpockets in Ardougne with that on.
rough/remark: Fancy red stone. Hope ye don't lose it down a mine shaft.
fremennik/compliment: A red stone for a warrior. The outerlander has some sense.

compliment: That green stone suits you, it goes with your eyes.
insult: An emerald at your neck and mud up to your knees, I see.
remark: Emerald, that? My nan had one just like it, only hers was glass.
nan/remark: Green suits you, dear. Mind you don't catch it on a bramble.
kid/remark: Is that stone green because it's old? Cheese goes green when it's old.

compliment: A blue stone on a gold chain looks very wizardly on you.
insult: Sapphire at your throat, is it? Shame it can't make you taller.
remark: Blue stone, that. The wizards at the tower wear the same.
wizard/remark: A sapphire amulet? I had one of those as an apprentice, long ago.
wizard/insult: Sapphire at your neck won't help if you can't spell the spell.

compliment: Neat little amulet, that. Did one of the wizards give it you?
insult: An amulet for aiming? You'd still miss the barn from inside it.
remark: That's the sort of amulet the Wizards' Tower hands out to visitors.
kid/remark: Did a wizard give you that? Which one? Was it the one with the imps?

compliment: Saradomin's star at your neck. Good to see it worn properly.
A silver star, polished and all. Someone was raised right.
insult: A holy symbol, and that face. Does the star know what it's hanging on?
remark: Silver star, is that? You'll want to keep it out of the sewers.
vicar/compliment: Saradomin smile on you, friend. His star sits well on you.
shady/insult: A little silver star. How reassuring that must be for you.

compliment: Takes some nerve, wearing that symbol round here.
insult: Zamorak's symbol worn in the open, and you're either brave or lost.
remark: That's Zamorak's mark at your neck. Not everyone here will like it.
vicar/remark: Greetings, traveller. I'll pray for you, whatever that thing says.
shady/compliment: Zamorak's mark, worn openly. Perhaps your sort has some use after all.
kid/remark: My mum says that symbol's naughty, so what does it actually do?

compliment: Ghost talk, that amulet. Takes a kind soul to listen to the dead.
insult: An amulet for talking to ghosts? Try talking to the living first.
remark: That amulet's the one for talking to ghosts, isn't it?
nan/remark: Talking to ghosts now, dear? Give my regards to my Albert.
kid/remark: Can you hear ghosts with that? What are they saying about me?
vicar/remark: That's the amulet from the Lumbridge graveyard, if I'm not mistaken.

compliment: An amulet for talking to cats. Finally someone who'll listen to them.
insult: A cat face at your neck, and the cat itself nowhere to be seen.
remark: Is that amulet purring at me, or is that your stomach?
nan/compliment: You can talk to cats with that, dear? Ask mine where she's been.
kid/remark: Does that let you talk to cats? Ask one why they hate baths!

compliment: The gnomes gave you that? They don't hand those out to just anyone.
insult: A gnome amulet. Did it come with a gnome, or just the string?
remark: That's gnome work, that amulet. Little hands make neat things.
gnome/compliment: You wear our amulet well, human, and the king chose rightly.
gnome/remark: That amulet came from the village, human, so do keep it close.

compliment: Plain gold, no fuss. There's something honest about that.
insult: A gold amulet with nothing in it. Rather like your purse, I expect.
remark: Plain gold amulet, no stone. Were you saving up for the gem?
dwarf/remark: Plain gold, that. Wants a stone in it. Bring it by and I'll set one.
trader/compliment: Gold with no gem in it, my friend? I could fix that for a price.

compliment: Cut that stone yourself, did you? It's a decent bit of work.
insult: A pretty stone on a chain, and not a drop of magic in it, I'll bet.
remark: Nice stone in that amulet. Somebody's been at the crafting bench.
wizard/remark: That amulet wants enchanting. As it stands, it's merely jewellery.
kid/compliment: Ooh, shiny! Can I hold it? I'll give it back, probably.

compliment: Simple gold chain, that. Suits you better than something gaudy.
insult: Gold necklace, grubby neck. One of those could do with a polish.
remark: A gold necklace, plain as you like. Was it a gift, or a purchase?
pirate/remark: Arr, gold round yer neck. Ye know what that does to a pirate.

compliment: A proper gem on a proper chain, and worn by somebody with taste.
insult: Lovely necklace, that. Did it come with the outfit, or in spite of it?
remark: That stone on your necklace catches the sun, so it isn't glass, then.
toff/remark: A gemstone necklace on a commoner. One does see everything these days.
nan/compliment: What a pretty necklace, dear. Don't wear it near the goblins.

compliment: Brass polishes up nicely if you keep at it, and you clearly have.
insult: Brass, is that? It's gone green where it touches you.
A brass necklace. Be careful, it'll turn your neck green by supper.
remark: Is that necklace brass? Looks gold from across the road, I'll say.
kid/remark: Is that gold? It's not gold. It's the colour of my dad's doorknob.
trader/insult: Brass, my friend. I could sell you something that doesn't go green.

compliment: Modest little stone, that. Shows more taste than a great gaudy rock.
insult: That stone's the sort you find on a beach. Did you find it on a beach?
remark: A little stone on a chain. Opal, is it, or one of the cheaper ones?
dwarf/remark: Jade or topaz, that? Fine for a first go, if you ask me.
kid/compliment: A pebble on a string! I've got loads of pebbles, yours is shinier.

compliment: Lovely warm scarf, that. Did someone knit it for you?
A woolly scarf for the cold. Sensible, for an adventurer.
insult: Woolly scarf in this weather? You'll cook before you reach the gate.
remark: That scarf looks like it's been down a toboggan run or two.
nan/compliment: Now that's a proper scarf, dear. At least one of you has sense.
kid/remark: Is that scarf for sledging? Can we go sledging, please, can we?

compliment: Bobbles on the ends and everything, somebody must love you.
insult: A scarf with bobbles on. Did your nan dress you this morning?
remark: That scarf's got bobbles. I keep wanting to flick them.
nan/remark: Bobbles on your scarf, dear. I knitted one just like it once.
dwarf/insult: Bobbles. On a scarf. And you call yourself an adventurer.

compliment: Cheerful colours on that scarf. Brightens the street, that does.
insult: Jester's colours at your neck. Does the king know you've escaped?
remark: A jester's scarf, in all those colours. Is the hat somewhere about?
toff/insult: A jester's scarf. Do say something amusing, citizen, I'm waiting.
kid/compliment: Your scarf's all the colours! Do a trick, jesters do tricks!

compliment: Every colour of the rainbow on one scarf, and a heart on it too.
That scarf's a rainbow with a heart on it, which is lovely to see.
insult: Found the end of the rainbow, did you? No pot of gold, just the scarf?
remark: A rainbow scarf. Gilbert's been handing those out again, I see.
kid/compliment: Your scarf's a rainbow! Did you get it from the flower man?
gnome/compliment: Rainbows round your neck, human! The gnomes approve of colour.

compliment: That festive scarf looks as warm as a hearth, and somebody chose well.
insult: A festive scarf. Is it festive season? It is not festive season.
remark: Festive scarf, that. Smells faintly of mince pies, I'll swear.
barkeep/remark: Festive scarf? Pull up a stool, it's nearly time for mulled wine.
vicar/compliment: A festive scarf. The season of goodwill suits you, traveller.

compliment: A rabbit's foot for luck. You'll want all you can get out there.
insult: Lucky rabbit's foot, is it? Wasn't very lucky for the rabbit.
remark: A rabbit's foot on a string. Wonder what the rabbit thinks of that.
kid/remark: Is that a real rabbit's foot? Where's the rest of the rabbit?
nan/remark: A rabbit's foot, dear? My mother swore by one of those.
rough/insult: Rabbit's foot round yer neck. Rest of it in a pie, I hope.

compliment: Half black, half white. There's a balance in that I rather like.
insult: The Makeover Mage's amulet, and yet here you are, unchanged.
remark: Black and white, that amulet. Like the one the Makeover Mage wears.
wizard/remark: A copy of the Makeover Mage's amulet. Try not to put it on backwards.
kid/remark: Is that the one that changes people? Turn me into a dragon, go on!

compliment: Games necklace, that. You keep yourself busy, I'll give you that.
insult: A games necklace. Off to Burthorpe to lose at something, are we?
remark: That blue necklace whisks you off to the games, doesn't it?
barkeep/remark: Blue necklace like that, you'll be off to the Burthorpe pub by dark.
kid/remark: Does that necklace do games? What games does it do, is it chess?

compliment: A cowbell at the neck. Honest work, that, whatever the cows think.
insult: A cowbell. Does the milkmaid know one of her herd's wandered off?
remark: Is that a cowbell round your neck? I heard you coming from the gate.
kid/remark: You've got a cowbell on! Ring it and I'll do the mooing, go on!
rough/compliment: A cowbell, eh? Gillie doesn't give those to just anybody.
goblin/remark: Cow bell on human. Where cow? Goblin want the cow, not bell.

compliment: A party necklace! Somebody's been celebrating, and good for them.
That necklace is the celebrating sort. Any excuse for cake, I say.
insult: An anniversary necklace. Did anyone remember yours, though?
remark: That's a necklace for an anniversary, though I couldn't say whose.
kid/remark: Is it somebody's birthday? If there's cake you have to share it.
toff/remark: An anniversary bauble. We held a ball for ours; the peasantry wept.

compliment: An egg pendant. There's something hopeful about an egg, I think.
insult: An egg round your neck and you still look like you were just hatched.
remark: Is that an egg on a chain? Mind you don't sit on it, then.
vicar/remark: An egg at your neck, traveller. Not a faith I know, but a gentle one.
kid/remark: Is that a real egg? If I poke it, will a chicken come out?

compliment: A bib for the feast. At least someone here plans ahead for gravy.
insult: A bib. At your age. Is there a jubbly dinner I'm not invited to?
A bib with a roast bird on it, and you're wearing it with pride.
remark: Is that a bib? With a jubbly on? I haven't had jubbly in years.
barkeep/remark: Bib on already? Dinner's not for an hour, love.
kid/compliment: You've got a bib on like a baby! I want one with a jubbly on it too!

compliment: An opal on a chain. Looks respectable, which I'm sure you are.
insult: Dodgy necklace, is it? Suits the dodgy look you've got about you.
remark: That's a dodgy-looking necklace, in the nicest possible way.
guard/insult: That necklace is the thieving sort. Hands where I can see them.
guard/remark: Dodgy necklace, is it? I'll be keeping an eye on you, then.
shady/compliment: A dodgy necklace. Perhaps your sort and mine aren't so different.

compliment: A root for a chain. Only a proper gardener would wear that.
insult: An amulet made of root. Did you grow it, or dig it up?
remark: Strung on a tree root, that amulet. Magic tree, by the look of it.
rough/remark: Root round yer neck. Talks to yer turnips, does it?
nan/compliment: A nature amulet, dear. Your cabbages will be grateful.

compliment: Witchwood, is that? Old charm, that. The sort that works, I hear.
insult: Is that a stick on a string? It is. You've a stick on a string on.
A twig on a bit of string. Did a kitten make you that?
remark: That stick round your neck must be for something, surely.
kid/remark: Why have you got a stick on a string? Is it a lead for a stick?
slayer_master/remark: Witchwood icon. Good. The caves are no place to go without one.

compliment: Opal at the neck. You've the look of someone with a tidy allotment.
insult: A farmer's amulet. The crops don't care what you wear, you know.
remark: An opal amulet, that. The farming sort, if I'm not mistaken.
rough/compliment: Opal amulet, eh? Me seeds always go further with one of them.
nan/remark: An opal, dear? My allotment never looked back after I got mine.

compliment: Jade at the throat and a whiff of herbs, you're a proper apothecary.
insult: An amulet for potions. Does it stop them tasting of pond?
remark: A jade amulet. Herblore folk wear those, don't they?
wizard/remark: A chemist's amulet. Do tell me you label your vials.
nan/remark: Jade, dear? Mine helps with the potions, the toad ones mostly.

compliment: That necklace gets you about, I'm told. Clever, keeping it handy.
insult: A travelling necklace. Can't walk anywhere like the rest of us?
remark: A jade necklace, that. The sort that takes you places, I hear.
wizard/remark: A necklace of passage. It'll bring you to the Tower, and then what?
kid/remark: Does that necklace take you places? Take me somewhere with no school!

compliment: Topaz at the throat. Warm colour, that, on a cold road north.
insult: That burning amulet means the Wilderness, and rather you than me.
remark: Topaz, that amulet? Warm colour. The sort folk wear up north, I hear.
guard/remark: Burning amulet. That's a Wilderness piece. Don't bring trouble back.
rough/insult: Burning amulet, eh? The Wilderness takes folk like you for breakfast.

compliment: Emerald at the neck and the smell of the altars on you, that's work.
insult: A binding necklace. Is it holding you together?
remark: Emerald necklace, that. The runecrafters wear those, I'm told.
wizard/remark: A binding necklace. Some actual runecraft, then, not just waving.
kid/remark: Does that necklace bind things? Bind my brother, he's annoying.

compliment: A phoenix at your neck. Sensible to have a way back, I'd say.
insult: A phoenix necklace. Planning on nearly dying, are we?
remark: A phoenix necklace. You expect to be in trouble, then?
vicar/remark: The phoenix is a hopeful bird, traveller. Rising again and all that.
fremennik/insult: A necklace to save your skin, outerlander? A warrior trusts the axe.

compliment: Dragonstone at your throat. Only serious tradesfolk bother with those.
insult: A skills necklace. Does it come with any skills, or just the stone?
remark: A dragonstone necklace, that. Off to one guild or another, I expect.
dwarf/compliment: That dragonstone necklace takes you to the Mining Guild, I'd wager.
trader/remark: Skills necklace? Off to the guilds and not buying anything, my friend.

compliment: Salve crystal, that. You've been down the haunted mine, haven't you?
insult: A salve amulet. Keeping the dead off you, or just the living?
remark: That's a mine crystal on a string, isn't it? The sort the undead fear.
vicar/remark: That crystal keeps the restless dead at bay, or so they say.
dwarf/remark: Crystal from a mine, on a string. Should've been in a pick, that.

compliment: A camel on a chain! You've been out in the desert, then, hot work.
insult: A camel amulet. Talking to camels now? They've very little to say.
remark: Is that amulet shaped like a camel? And did it just bray at me?
kid/remark: Your amulet's a camel! Does it spit? Camels spit, my dad says.
nan/remark: A little camel, dear? Mind it doesn't bray in church.

compliment: Those beads have seen some jungle. You've a tale or two, I'll bet.
insult: Bones on a string round your neck. Whose were they, do you know?
remark: Bone beads, those? There's a story behind that, I shouldn't wonder.
kid/remark: Are those beads real bones? Did they belong to somebody you knew?
shady/remark: Beads of the dead. At least your sort has some respect for them.
pirate/compliment: Arr, bone beads! Ye've been to Karamja and come back with yer neck.

compliment: A medal for training cats! There's a feat, nobody trains a cat.
insult: A medal for cat training. The cat got the rats, you got the medal.
remark: Is that a medal? For cats? Gertrude's been handing those out, I see.
nan/compliment: A cat medal, dear! Gertrude only gives those to the patient ones.
kid/remark: A medal! Did you win a race, or did your cat win it for you?

compliment: A garland of petals at your neck. Did the forest give you that?
Petals round your neck and all. Somebody in the woods likes you.
insult: Flowers round your neck. Are you off to a wedding, or coming from one?
remark: That garland's still fresh. Dryad work, that, nobody else manages it.
kid/remark: Flowers round your neck! Can I have one, just the yellow one, please?
gnome/compliment: Petals at your neck, human! The forest must think well of you.

compliment: Smart bow tie, that. Very tidy. Somebody's been invited somewhere.
insult: A bow tie and mud to the knees. The evening went downhill, did it?
remark: A bow tie, out here. Is the dinner later, or did it end badly?
toff/compliment: A bow tie! At last, a citizen who dresses for the occasion.
barkeep/remark: Bow tie, is it? Dining room's through the back, sir, mind the step.
kid/insult: Why've you got a bow on your neck? Is somebody going to unwrap you?

compliment: Shayzien red at your neck. You've served, or know someone who did.
insult: A skull on your scarf. Do the Shayzien know you've borrowed it?
remark: A red scarf with a skull on. That's Shayzien, that is.
guard/remark: Shayzien scarf. Soldier, are you? Then you'll know the rules already.
kid/compliment: A skull on your scarf! That's the best scarf I've ever seen!

compliment: House colours at your neck. Somebody in Kourend thinks well of you.
insult: A house scarf from Kourend. Did they give it you, or did it fall off?
remark: That scarf's got a badge on it. One of the Kourend houses, I'd say.
A Kourend scarf, that. Which house? I can never tell them apart.
trader/remark: Kourend colours, my friend? Whatever they're selling, I'll beat it.

compliment: A Saradomin stole, worn properly. The old priests would approve.
Blue and white at your neck. Saradomin's colours suit a kind face.
insult: A priest's stole, is it? When was the last time you were in church?
remark: That's a Saradomin stole. They don't sell those at the market.
vicar/compliment: Saradomin's stole, traveller! We'll make a brother of you yet.
shady/insult: A Saradomin stole. How very brave of you to wear it near me.

compliment: A Zamorak stole, worn without shame. That takes a certain nerve.
insult: Zamorak's stole at your neck. Are you a priest of his, or just cold?
remark: A red stole, Zamorak's. You don't see that in Lumbridge church.
vicar/remark: A Zamorak stole, traveller. I'll say nothing, but I will pray.
shady/compliment: Zamorak's stole on you. Perhaps your sort chose the right side.

compliment: Guthix's stole at your neck. There's a balance about you, I'll say.
insult: A Guthix stole. Can't pick a side, so you picked the middle?
remark: A green stole, that. Guthix's, if I know my colours.
vicar/remark: A Guthix stole, traveller. A quieter faith than mine, but a faith.
wizard/remark: Guthix's colours, how very even-handed of you.

compliment: Black stone on gold at your neck. That's a serious bit of jewellery.
An onyx at your neck? You don't see those outside the Karamja caves.
insult: An onyx amulet above that outfit, one of them must be borrowed.
remark: That black stone's an onyx, isn't it? Keep it away from the thieves.
tzhaar/remark: JalYt wears TzHaar stone at neck. Earned, no, or bought with TokKul?
dwarf/compliment: Onyx, set in gold like that. Proper craft, that, whoever did it.

compliment: Blood magic on an onyx, and whoever made it knew what they were doing.
insult: An amulet that drinks blood, is it? Keep it on your side of the road.
remark: That amulet's got a red glow about it that I don't altogether like.
vicar/remark: Blood magic in that amulet, traveller, and I can feel it from here.
shady/compliment: Blood on an onyx. Finally, your sort wears something with some bite.
kid/remark: Your amulet's glowing red! Is it angry, or is it just hungry?

compliment: A zenyte at your neck. Those come from the monkey island, I'm told.
insult: An amulet that burns within, and you with a face to match.
remark: That orange stone's glowing. Should it be glowing like that?
kid/remark: Your amulet's on fire! Not really, but it looks like it, doesn't it?
wizard/remark: A zenyte, glowing like that. Do try not to set your collar alight.
dwarf/compliment: Zenyte. Rarest stone there is. Set well, too, I'll give them that.

compliment: Zenyte on a chain. Only the best archers bother, I'm told.
insult: A necklace full of anguish, and a face full of the same, I see.
remark: That zenyte necklace is glowing, you know, does it ever stop?
toff/remark: A zenyte necklace on a commoner. The economy baffles me, frankly.
fremennik/compliment: A burning necklace, outerlander? The skalds will want to hear of it.

compliment: That dark necklace means business. Wizards go pale when they see one.
insult: An evil-looking necklace on a very ordinary-looking neck, that.
remark: There's something smoky about that necklace, and not in a nice way.
vicar/remark: That necklace has something unholy in it, traveller, do be careful.
wizard/compliment: An occult necklace, smoke devil work, and rather potent, I'm told.
kid/remark: Your necklace is all smoky and scary, can I wear it, I'm not scared.

compliment: Zenyte and spider venom at your neck, you've been under Morytania.
insult: A venom amulet, of course, you've the look of someone who'd own one.
remark: That amulet's got a green tint to it, and I'd wager that's venom.
kid/remark: Is that spider stuff on your amulet? How big was the spider, then?
shady/compliment: Spider venom in a zenyte. Perhaps your sort does learn, after all.
nan/remark: Spider venom, dear? Don't lick it. I knew a man who licked it.

compliment: An heirloom like that means you carry a dead house's name with you.
insult: An old family's amulet, is that? Which grave did you borrow it from?
remark: That amulet's an heirloom, surely. Old family, Morytania, by the look.
vicar/remark: That amulet belonged to the dead, traveller, so carry it with respect.
burgher/remark: That's an old Morytania amulet. One of the families that's gone now.

compliment: That skull amulet's a hauntingly lovely thing, in its way.
insult: A skull amulet, is it? It's got a better complexion than you.
remark: A skull on a chain at your throat. Where on earth did you dig that up?
kid/remark: A skull on a necklace! Does it talk, or does it just stare at me?
guard/remark: A skull on your neck is a Wilderness look, so don't start anything.
shady/compliment: A skull at your throat. Greedy, at least, which I can respect.

compliment: Dragon bones at your throat. Only one way to come by those, I'd say.
insult: Bones round your neck. Did you slay the dragon, or just find it?
remark: That necklace is made of bone. Big bone. Dragon, by the look of it.
fremennik/compliment: Dragon bone at your neck, outerlander! That's a boast I'd believe.
kid/remark: Is that necklace real dragon? Did it roar when you took its bones?
vicar/remark: Bones should be buried, not worn, traveller, but I expect it's fine.

compliment: Black onyx on a chain. Karamja work, that, and expensive-looking.
insult: A berserker necklace, worn by someone who looks half asleep.
remark: An onyx necklace. Those go with the obsidian blades, I'm told.
tzhaar/compliment: JalYt wears stone of the caves. TzHaar blade goes well with it, no?
fremennik/remark: A berserker's necklace, outerlander? Show me the berserker, then.

compliment: Xeric's talisman, that is. Not many know where to even look for one.
insult: An ancient relic round your neck, and you still can't find the bank.
remark: That talisman's old Kourend work. Older than the castle, I'd guess.
wizard/remark: A relic of Xeric's day. Do handle it carefully, it's older than you.
kid/remark: Is that from the bad old king? Does it make you do bad things too?

compliment: An ancient pendant with something frozen inside, that's a rare find.
insult: A frozen pendant on a chilly sort, at least the two of you match.
remark: That pendant looks frozen, is it cold to the touch, or just the look?
wizard/remark: Frozen tears in a pendant. Whose, one wonders, and why keep them?
fremennik/remark: Ice in a pendant, outerlander? We have plenty, if you want more.

compliment: An eye amulet, that, the sort the rune folk wear, and clever folk too.
insult: An eye on a chain. Is it a spare, or did you lose one of your own?
remark: An amulet shaped like an eye, and it's looking at me, I'm sure of it.
wizard/remark: An amulet of the Eye, so you've seen the temple that few have seen.
kid/remark: Your necklace has an eye on it! Does it blink when you're not looking?

compliment: A stone like that on a chain. Somebody's been working hard, or lucky.
insult: A rare stone, not even enchanted. All that money and nothing to show.
remark: That's a rare stone in that amulet. Wants enchanting, surely.
wizard/remark: That amulet's not enchanted, all that stone and not a spark of magic.
trader/compliment: A stone like that, my friend, I'd buy on the spot, so name a price.
kid/compliment: That's the biggest shiny I've ever seen! Can I have it when you die?

compliment: That necklace has a stone fit for a crown, honestly.
insult: A stone that size round your neck, and you still walk like a peasant.
remark: Big stone on that necklace, purple, is it, or black, I can't tell.
toff/remark: A stone that size on a commoner's neck. One begins to suspect theft.
dwarf/compliment: Now that's a stone, set properly too. Whoever cut it knew their craft.

compliment: An amulet charged at the altars. That's proper runecraft, that is.
insult: An elemental amulet, and you still look like you got rained on.
remark: That amulet's glowing with something, fire or air, I'd guess.
wizard/compliment: An elemental amulet, so someone's been to the altars with intent.
kid/remark: Your amulet's glowing! Is it fire? Can you set things on fire with it?

compliment: Fangs on a cord like that, you've been in the Fremennik caves.
insult: A necklace of fangs. Did you fight for them, or find them in a stew?
remark: Teeth on a string round your neck. Whose teeth, might I ask?
fremennik/compliment: Turoth fangs, outerlander? Then you've been in our caves and lived.
kid/remark: Are those real teeth? Did any of them come out of your own mouth?
rough/remark: Fangs on a string, eh? I've a few in the back of my jaw ye can have.

compliment: A heart-shaped amulet with sand inside. Rather sweet, for the desert.
insult: A heart full of sand. Says a lot about you, that.
remark: A little heart with sand in it. That's from the desert, I take it.
nan/compliment: A heart with sand in it, dear, somebody out there is fond of you.
kid/remark: Why's your necklace got sand in it? Did it come from a beach?
pirate/remark: Sand in yer amulet? I've sand in places ye don't want to hear about.

compliment: An old Morytania medallion. You've been where most of us won't go.
insult: A vampyre's medallion at your neck. Handy for them at biting time.
remark: That medallion's vampyre work, isn't it? Old and not very friendly.
burgher/remark: That medallion's from the castle folk, so keep it hidden round here.
vicar/remark: A vampyre medallion, traveller. I'd not wear it past the river.
kid/remark: Is that a vampyre thing? Are you a vampyre, then, show me your teeth.

compliment: Black robes suit you, in a stone-circle sort of way.
insult: Dark wizard robes, is it? Did you take those off one, or buy them?
remark: Those black robes have been south of Varrock, I'll bet.
wizard/remark: Black robes. One of Zamorak's lot, or just fond of the colour?
kid/remark: Are you a dark wizard? Mum says not to go near the dark wizards!
vicar/remark: Black robes at the chapel door... we're open to all, I suppose.

compliment: That little top's dwarf-made, isn't it? Keldagrim stitching, that.
insult: Did that shirt shrink in the wash, or was it made for a dwarf?
That top stops a good hand short of your trousers, you know.
remark: Keldagrim tailoring, is that? They do cut everything short.
dwarf/remark: That's one of ours, that top. Fits you... about halfway.
nan/remark: Oh dear, that top's a bit short. Are you not cold round the middle?

compliment: That's Tai Bwo Wannai cloth, that top, and lovely bright work too.
insult: Karamjan village top, and the pale arms to go with it.
remark: Did you trade sticks for that top, or did the village take pity?
kid/remark: Your top's got patterns on! Did you draw them yourself?
trader/compliment: That's island cloth, my friend. I'd give you a fair price for it.

compliment: Nice robe top. Canifis cut, if I'm any judge of a sleeve.
insult: Werewolf tailoring, that top. Mind it doesn't turn at full moon.
remark: Those wide sleeves came from Barker's, didn't they?
nan/remark: A plain robe top like that hides all manner of sins, dear.
barkeep/remark: Canifis robes, eh? They're usually worn by folk with more hair.

compliment: Beekeeping gear! Someone's brave around a hive, at least.
insult: Is that a beekeeper's suit, or are you expecting a swarm?
remark: A beekeeper's suit... are you expecting trouble from the hives?
kid/remark: Have you got bees? Can I see the bees? Where do you keep the bees?
nan/compliment: A beekeeper, how lovely. You'll have honey for your tea, then.
rough/remark: Keep that suit away from my hives. They don't take to strangers.

compliment: That's a shirt for keeping your head down, and sensible in some towns.
insult: That shirt's seen better days, and I doubt the days were that good.
Did you come by that shirt honestly, or did the gutter lend it?
remark: Meiyerditch cloth, that. Nobody wears that drab on purpose, surely.
shady/insult: Dressed like one of the herd, meddler, and it won't save you.

remark: You've come from the desert mines in that shirt, haven't you?
compliment: You got out of the mines in that shirt. That takes some doing, friend.
nan/remark: Give that shirt here, dear, it wants a boil and a prayer.

compliment: Blue shoulders on red, very Ardougne... a family piece, is it?
insult: Those shoulder pads... were they a family heirloom or a family joke?
remark: Carnillean colours, that armour. The old house still dresses well.
toff/remark: The Carnillean livery, on a commoner. Ceril must be short of staff.
kid/remark: Your shoulders are massive in that! Can you fit through doors?

compliment: Plain grey plate, nothing borrowed. You do it the hard way, I'd say.
insult: That grey plate looks like you forged it yourself, in the dark.
remark: You're the sort who won't take a hand from anyone, in that armour.
dwarf/remark: Honest iron, that. No gilt, no nonsense, just plate and stubbornness.
rough/compliment: Grey plate and no help wanted. I know the type, I married one.

compliment: That garb's seen a few holes dug, I'd wager, and it suits a wanderer.
insult: Laced tunic, knife on the belt... are you hunting treasure or trouble?
remark: Dug that garb up somewhere, did you? It's got that look about it.
barkeep/remark: Treasure hunter's garb. Found anything, or just the holes so far?
kid/remark: Is that a real knife on your belt? Have you found any treasure yet?

compliment: A bedsheet with eyeholes. Say what you like, it's a classic.
insult: Is that a ghost, or someone who lost an argument with their bedding?
Boo yourself. I've seen scarier laundry on a line in Lumbridge.
remark: You're going to trip on that sheet. I'm just warning you now.
kid/remark: A ghost! A ghost! Wait, I can see your boots under there.
nan/remark: That's a good linen sheet, that is. Whoever cut it wants a word.
vicar/remark: Not a real ghost, I trust? We've had enough of those in the crypt.

compliment: Properly chilling, those torn robes, and who did the clawing?
insult: Those robes look like a cat got at them, and a big cat at that.
remark: Ghastly robes, those. Keep the wailing down near the children.
kid/remark: Did a monster rip your clothes? Can I see where it got you?
barkeep/remark: Banshee look, eh? No wailing in here, love, it curdles the ale.

compliment: Honest mud on that tunic. Somebody's been doing proper work.
insult: Been digging graves in that, have you, or just lying in one?
That tunic's half mud. Which graveyard did you crawl out of?
remark: A gravedigger's tunic... on your way to work, or back from it?
vicar/remark: Gravedigger's clothes. We've a plot that wants doing, if you're free.
kid/remark: Are you a gravedigger? Have you ever dug up a skeleton?

compliment: That black coat with the brooch is smart, in a witchy sort of way.
insult: Witch's coat, is it? Tell me where you parked the broom.
remark: A witch's coat on a day like this. Someone's expecting newts.
nan/remark: Oh, I had a coat like that, dear, back before all the toads.
kid/remark: Are you a witch? Can you turn my brother into something?

insult: Straw's coming out of that shirt. Are you stuffed, or just untidy?
Scarecrow shirt, and yet the crows are following you about.
compliment: That scarecrow shirt's a good laugh. Does it keep the birds off?
remark: Straw in the collar, straw in the cuffs... you've been in a field.
rough/remark: Stand in my field in that shirt and you'll earn your keep.
kid/remark: You've got straw in your shirt! Does it itch or just tickle?

compliment: A pumpkin jumper! Somebody hand-knitted that, so somebody loves you.
insult: That pumpkin on your jumper's grinning more than you are.
remark: Pumpkin jumper, in this weather? You'll be warm, I suppose.
nan/compliment: Did Iffie knit that for you, dear? She does a lovely pumpkin.
kid/remark: Your jumper's got a face on it! Can you make the face talk?

compliment: A snow imp, in the flesh! Well, in the fur, and very convincing it is.
insult: That snow imp suit's stitched up the front, so not a real imp, then.
remark: White fur, little horns... you're either a snow imp or very lost.
kid/remark: A snow imp! Are you a real one? Can I touch the fur to check?
gnome/remark: A snow imp, human? Rather far south for one of those, surely.
rough/insult: Imp suit, is it? The stitching's showing, and so's the stupidity.

compliment: Red coat, gold braid, epaulettes. Very smart, that nutcracker look.
That's a proper toy soldier's coat, and all it wants is a drum.
insult: Dressed as a nutcracker, and I'll bet you can't crack a walnut.
remark: A nutcracker's coat, with the braid and everything... very festive.
guard/remark: Not a real uniform, that, and not a real soldier in it either.
kid/compliment: You look like a toy soldier! Do your arms go up and down?

insult: You're dressed as a tree, with baubles on, and I have questions.
A walking fir tree. Mind the woodcutters, they'll have you for logs.
compliment: A tree with baubles on! Well, that's the season sorted for me.
remark: Is that tree costume shedding? There's needles all down the road.
kid/remark: You're a tree! Can I hang something on you?
rough/remark: A tree, walking about. I'd chop it, but it'd only complain.

compliment: Icicles knitted right into that jumper, and clever work it is too.
insult: That jumper looks cold, and I'm not sure that's what a jumper is for.
remark: Icicles on a jumper... the Fremennik would call that summer wear.
nan/remark: An icy jumper won't keep you warm, dear, whatever it's called.
kid/remark: Are those real icicles on your jumper? I want to lick one to check.

compliment: A jumper with a toothy great face on it! Somebody's having a laugh.
insult: That jumper's got more teeth than you have, and better ones.
remark: Is that face on your jumper meant to be the thing from the caves?
kid/remark: Your jumper's got teeth! Does it bite? Has it ever bitten anyone?
tzhaar/remark: JalYt wears Jad's face on soft cloth. Jad does not approve, no?

insult: Is that armour made of egg? Chocolate, by the smell of it.
Stripy egg armour. One good knock and you're an omelette.
compliment: Stripes, shoulder eggs, the lot. That's a cheerful bit of armour.
remark: Mind the sun in that eggshell armour. It'll run down your legs.
kid/remark: Is your armour chocolate? Can I have a bit off the shoulder?
barkeep/remark: Egg armour, is it? Don't sit near the fire, we've just mopped.

compliment: Bright yellow robes with fur trim. Very devout, very visible.
insult: Yellow robes with chick fluff round the hem... which god is that for?
remark: An egg priest, is that? I didn't know the eggs had a church.
vicar/remark: Those yellow robes are no order I know of, and I know most of them.
kid/remark: Are you an egg priest? Do the eggs ever answer your prayers?

insult: A grown adult dressed as a carrot, and nobody's stopped you yet.
Carrot costume. The rabbits will have your legs off by teatime.
compliment: A carrot! Now that's a costume with a bit of heart to it.
remark: Orange from top to toe... are you a carrot, or just very sunburnt?
kid/remark: You're a carrot! Can I take a bite? Just a little one off the end?
rough/remark: Dressed as a carrot, in my field, and I've a row that wants planting.

compliment: A poet's jacket, satchel strap and all. Found any inspiration yet?
insult: A poet's jacket. Is there a poem in you, or only the jacket?
remark: Brown jacket, strap across the chest... you look like you rhyme.
toff/insult: A poet, by the jacket. The court has quite enough of those, citizen.
barkeep/remark: Poet's jacket, eh? No verses in here till after the third pint.

insult: That jumper's snug round the middle, so a good Christmas, was it?
Red jumper, laced at the collar, straining a touch at the belly.
compliment: A good thick red jumper for the cold, and that's just sense.
remark: That jumper's been near a lot of pies, I'd say.
barkeep/remark: That jumper's got ale written all over it, so I'll pour you the usual.
dwarf/compliment: That's a jumper that's seen some beer, human, and I respect that.

compliment: Black robes with gold at the seams, so someone's doing well.
insult: Trimmed black robes. A dark wizard with ideas above the stone circle.
remark: Those black robes have a trim on them. Did you earn that or find it?
wizard/remark: Trim on a black robe doesn't make the spells any better, you know.

compliment: Leather with a trim on it. Somebody takes care of their kit.
insult: Gold trim on cowhide. That's like putting a bow on a bucket.
remark: Trimmed leathers... found those with a spade, didn't you?
trader/compliment: Trimmed leather, my friend! That'd fetch a tidy sum at my stall.
kid/remark: Your leather's got gold on it! Can I scrape a bit off to check?

compliment: Green dragonhide with a trim. Now that's a smart bit of leather.
insult: Trim on dragonhide, and the dragon still comes off worse.
remark: That green hide's trimmed... somebody paid for that, or dug it up.
fremennik/compliment: Dragon hide, trimmed and worn well. A hunter's skin, outerlander.

compliment: Menaphite colours on that top. Very bright, very southern.
insult: Yellow with purple sleeves... did Ali sell you that, or dare you?
remark: That's a Menaphos cut, that top. Keeps the sun off, I'm told.
trader/compliment: Menaphite cloth, my friend! You've been trading in the south, I see.
kid/remark: Your top's two colours! Did they run out of one halfway?

compliment: Fur collar, big pockets. That's a jacket built for a balloon basket.
insult: A flying jacket, and your feet very much on the ground.
remark: An Entrana balloon jacket, isn't it? Did you land it, or fall out?
vicar/remark: Auguste's flying jacket... so you've been up in that balloon of his.
kid/remark: Have you been flying? In the sky? What's it like up there, then?

insult: Dressed like the vyrewatch, and fooling nobody with a pulse.
Black top, Vyrewatch style. Do they know you're borrowing the look?
compliment: Vyrewatch black. You must have walked through Meiyerditch to get that.
remark: That's vampyre livery, that top... the patrols buy it, do they?
burgher/remark: Vyrewatch clothes round here? We've seen enough of the real ones.
kid/remark: Are you a vampyre? You don't look like one. Show me your teeth, then.

compliment: That's vampyre noble finery. Very well cut, for Darkmeyer.
insult: Dressed like a Darkmeyer noble, and still queuing with the rest of us.
remark: Noble's clothes from Darkmeyer, those... mind who sees you in them.
toff/remark: Vampyre nobility tailoring, on a commoner. One has standards, citizen.
shady/insult: Playing at nobility, meddler? The real ones would smell you out.
burgher/remark: Fine clothes like that come from over the wall, and I'll not ask how.

compliment: Those old robes have Nardah's look about them, mended and all.
insult: An old robe sewn back together, and the stitches are winning.
remark: That's an old shrine robe, that is. Elidinis's, if I know my gods.
vicar/remark: A robe of Elidinis. The river goddess keeps her own, even now.
nan/compliment: Somebody's mended that old robe with a lot of patience, dear.

compliment: Purple tabard over steel plate. That's the Ardougne knights' look.
insult: Knight of Ardougne, are you? The real ones stand up straighter.
remark: That purple tabard's Ardougne knight colours... borrowed, I'd guess.
guard/remark: Ardougne knight colours. Papers, or I'll assume you stole the tabard.
toff/remark: Ardougne livery, is it? The knights there used to dress better.

compliment: Grey mantle, gold emblem on the chest... very sinister, very smart.
insult: Grey robes with a shiny badge. Which secret order's missing a member?
remark: Those robes have a Black Knight look about them, under the grey.
wizard/remark: That emblem on your robes is not any school of magic I'd admit to.
guard/remark: Grey robes and a badge I don't recognise, so I'm watching you, robes.

compliment: Pale robes with a red star on the chest, and very striking they are.
insult: A red star on your robes. Are you selling something, or recruiting?
remark: That star on your robes... I've seen that sign somewhere, I'm sure.
vicar/remark: That red star's no sign of Saradomin's, so whose robes are those?
kid/remark: There's a big red star on your robes! Did you fall out of the sky?

compliment: Leather tunic and braces... that's forge-hand's kit if ever I saw it.
insult: A smith's tunic with not one burn on it. Never touched a forge, then.
remark: That tunic's cut for anvil work, with the braces and all.
dwarf/compliment: Now that's a proper smith's tunic. Dwarf-stitched, by the collar.
dwarf/insult: Smith's tunic, human? Show me a hammer arm to go with it, then.

compliment: Grey robes, orange cuffs... a runecrafter, by the look of you.
insult: Runecrafter's robes, and pockets full of essence dust, I'll bet.
remark: Those robes have been near the Abyss, by the smell of them.
wizard/compliment: Robes of the Eye. So you're the one making the runes we burn through.
wizard/insult: A runecrafter. Fetching and carrying essence for cleverer folk, then.

compliment: Hide and leather, cut for creeping. That's a hunter who knows the job.
insult: A hunter's top, and you still trod on every twig on the way here.
remark: Spotted hide and a sash... you've been with the hunters down south.
gnome/remark: A hunter's top, human. Have you been after the chinchompas again?
rough/remark: Hunter's gear. If you're after my chickens, think again.

compliment: Rope strap on that angler's vest... you've been out on rough water.
insult: A fisherman's vest. Do you smell of fish, or is that just the look?
remark: That's a sea-angler's vest. Tempoross weather, I'd call this.
rough/compliment: Proper angler's vest, that. You've been out where the sea gets angry.
kid/remark: Are you a fisherman? Have you ever caught a shark with your hands?

compliment: Green caped top with a glowing leaf on it... that's woodland finery.
insult: Forester's top, glowing leaf and all, and the trees still hate you.
remark: That leaf on your chest is glowing. Is that normal for a woodcutter?
gnome/compliment: A forester's top, human! The trees speak well of whoever wears that.
rough/remark: Fancy green for a woodcutter. In my day we chopped in a vest.

compliment: A gold-plated miner's jacket. Now that's someone who's hit a seam.
insult: Gold on a miner's jacket. You've not been down a pit in that, surely.
remark: That jacket's gilded with something that fell out of the sky, I'd say.
dwarf/compliment: Gold trim on a prospector's jacket? By Guthix, that's a rich seam.
kid/remark: Your jacket's gold! Are you rich? Can I have some of the gold?

compliment: Shayzien plate, worn right. Their army turns out smart soldiers.
insult: A soldier's platebody, and you salute like a wet fish.
remark: That's a Shayzien soldier's plate. Did you serve, or just win it?
guard/remark: Shayzien plate. Different army, same rules, so stay out of trouble.
fremennik/remark: Soldier's plate, outerlander. Armies are for those who fear a duel.

compliment: A town crier's coat, blue and gold... loud even before you speak.
insult: Crier's coat, and nobody's asked you to announce anything.
remark: Hear ye, hear ye... you've the coat for it, but where's the bell?
kid/remark: Are you the crier? Shout something! Shout that I'm late for tea!
guard/remark: Crier's coat. Announcements go through the watch first, understood?
toff/remark: A crier's coat. Do tell the peasantry something useful for once.

compliment: A butler's uniform, apron and all. You could serve at a villa in that.
insult: Dressed as a butler. Fetch me a drink, then, since you're here.
remark: That butler's uniform is mostly clean, and I do mean mostly.
toff/remark: A butler's uniform! Finally. The silver wants polishing, citizen.
barkeep/remark: Butler's uniform? Good, you can collect the glasses on your way out.

compliment: Clean white coat, buttoned up... someone mixes potions carefully.
insult: White coat, and not a stain on it. Not much of an alchemist, then.
remark: That's an alchemist's coat. Stand downwind, if you don't mind.
wizard/remark: An alchemist's coat. Potions are magic for folk who enjoy washing up.
nan/remark: A nice white coat like that wants keeping away from the toads, dear.

compliment: Hood, tunic, belt... that's a traveller who's seen a few roads.
insult: Dressed like an adventurer. The roads are full of those, you know.
remark: Grey hood and a brown tunic. Off questing, or just back?
guard/remark: Another adventurer in a hood. Keep it down and keep it moving.
barkeep/remark: A traveller's tunic. Sit down, you look like you've a story.

compliment: Black plate with gold edging. That's armour for a parade, that is.
insult: Black and gold plate. Were you going to a parade, or just lost it?
remark: That ornate plate's a bit much for the high street, friend.
toff/compliment: Black and gold, how heraldic. One almost mistook you for someone.
kid/remark: Your armour's got gold on! Are you a king, or just pretending?

compliment: Purple stones set right into the plate... that's wealth you can hear.
Dragonstones on a platebody! Elven work, I'd stake my boots on it.
insult: Gems on your armour. One good blow and you've bought someone a house.
remark: Those purple stones on that plate catch the light from here.
trader/compliment: Dragonstones in the plate itself! Name a price, my friend, any price.
kid/remark: Your armour's got purple jewels in it! Can I have the smallest one?
toff/compliment: Dragonstone plate. At last, a citizen who dresses to be seen.

compliment: White with a gold sash across it. That's Prifddinas cloth, surely.
insult: Elven clothes on human shoulders. The elves must have been laughing.
remark: That top's cut the way the elves cut things, all sash and no seams.
toff/compliment: Elven tailoring. One has heard of it, naturally, but rarely sees it.
gnome/remark: Elven cloth, human? You've been further west than most of us.

compliment: Several beasts' hides stitched into one top, and clever work too.
insult: That top's three animals at least, and none of them volunteered.
remark: Grey hide, pale fur, a sash across... that's a Varlamore hunter's top.
rough/remark: Patchwork hide, that. Somebody's been busy with a skinning knife.
kid/remark: What animal is your top made of? It looks like it's more than one.

compliment: Black plate, gold edges... that's knight's armour of the serious sort.
insult: Black Knight plate with gold on. Promoted, or just looted?
remark: That's Black Knight armour, the fancy sort. Keep it away from Falador.
guard/remark: Black Knight colours with gold on. I'll be watching you very closely.
guard/insult: Black Knight plate, in my town. Take it off or take it elsewhere.
shady/compliment: Black and gold plate. Perhaps your sort has some taste after all.

compliment: Green sleeveless tunic, cut for the bow... that's proper ranger's kit.
insult: Ranger's tunic, and arms like two bits of string in it.
remark: That green tunic's the sort the forest rangers wear, arrows to match.
fremennik/compliment: Ranger's tunic, light and quick. The cold will find you, outerlander.
kid/remark: Are you Robin Hood? You look a bit like Robin Hood.

compliment: A tailcoat, waistcoat, the lot. Somebody's off somewhere grand.
insult: A tailcoat, in the mud. Was the ball cancelled, or were you?
remark: That tailcoat's the smartest thing on this road by a mile.
toff/compliment: A tailcoat, at last! A citizen who knows what evening wear is for.
barkeep/remark: Tailcoat, is it? You'll be wanting the good glasses, then.
kid/remark: Why are you so smart? Is it a wedding? Can I come to the wedding?

compliment: Dark robes and a red sash... somebody's been reading the wrong books.
insult: Robes that say ruin, and a face that says lost on the way to market.
remark: Grey and red robes like that usually come with a skull somewhere.
vicar/remark: Robes of that cut have no business near a chapel, but do come in.
wizard/remark: Ruinous-looking robes. They don't cast any better for being gloomy.

compliment: Chain and hide, cut for the arena. Been in the pit, haven't you?
insult: Arena armour, and I've seen you flinch at a chicken.
remark: That's fighting-pit gear from out Al Kharid way, isn't it?
rough/remark: Arena chain, eh? I used to watch the duels, back when they had them.
kid/remark: Are you a fighter from the arena? Did you win or did you lose?

compliment: Navy coat, gold buttons. That's a captain's coat if ever I saw one.
insult: Captain's coat, and I'd not trust you with a rowing boat.
remark: That coat's been through weather. Salt on the buttons, I'd say.
pirate/remark: Arr, a captain's coat. Which ship, and does she know ye've got it?
pirate/compliment: A storm captain's coat. Ye've sailed through worse than rain, I'd say.
kid/remark: Are you a captain? Have you got a ship with cannons on it?

insult: A waistcoat and no shirt under it. Did the swamp eat the shirt?
Open waistcoat, bare chest, this wind. The swamp's got to your head.
compliment: That waistcoat's a swamp sailor's look, and you carry it off, somehow.
remark: No shirt under that waistcoat... you've come up out of the marshes.
nan/remark: Put a shirt on under that, dear. You'll catch your death in the fens.
pirate/compliment: Bare chest and a waistcoat, matey. Now that's how ye sail a swamp.

compliment: Teal and brown with a crystal pinned on... elegant sailing wear, that.
insult: A sailor's waistcoat, and you walk like the deck's still moving.
remark: That crystal pinned to your waistcoat is elf work, surely.
gnome/compliment: A glider's jacket, human! Not our sort of glider, but well done.
pirate/remark: Pretty jacket for a sailor. Did ye sail the ship, or just pose on it?

compliment: A quartered tabard in blue and gold, and very heraldic it looks too.
insult: Quartered tabard, hourglasses and all. Whose herald are you, then?
remark: That tabard's quartered like a knight's... a tourney prize, was it?
toff/compliment: A quartered tabard. One approves of a commoner with proper heraldry.
kid/remark: Your tabard's got hourglasses on! Is it time for something?

compliment: Brown waistcoat, scarf, rolled sleeves... that's an explorer's rig.
insult: Explorer's waistcoat, and you got lost between the bank and the well.
remark: That waistcoat and scarf have been down more roads than I have.
gnome/remark: An explorer's waistcoat, human! Where to next, and can I come?
trader/compliment: Explorer's gear, my friend! You've seen things I'd pay to hear about.

compliment: A long dark coat with a high collar. Very dramatic in a doorway, that.
insult: Long coat, high collar, stars on the waistcoat... expecting applause?
remark: That coat's cut for sweeping into rooms, not walking into them.
toff/remark: A collar that high is theatrical, citizen, but one allows it.
wizard/remark: Stars on the waistcoat and not a spell in sight... fashion, I suppose.

compliment: A dark grey tunic with a plate on the front, plain but well made.
insult: That grey tunic looks like it was stitched out of an old shield.
remark: Blue-grey tunic with a crest panel... a guild's colours, is that?
guard/remark: Grey tunic with a panel on it. Not one of ours, so whose are you?

compliment: That blue tunic with the shoulder cape is a smart bit of tailoring.
insult: A little cape on the shoulders. Were you a herald, or just hopeful?
remark: Blue tunic with a half-cape... that's a courier's look, isn't it?
barkeep/remark: Half a cape on that tunic. Did they run out of cloth, or money?

compliment: A red wrap top with a sash, simple and well worn, and it suits you.
insult: Red wrap top, tied at the waist. Did you dress in a hurry, or a wind?
remark: That red top's wrapped and tied the way the far travellers do it.
fremennik/remark: A wrapped red top, outerlander. Thin cloth for a long road.

compliment: Grey robes, red hood, a flame pinned on... ominous, but neat.
insult: Red hood and grey robes. Which cult, and are they taking beginners?
remark: Those red-hooded robes have a whiff of brimstone about them.
vicar/remark: A red hood and a flame on the breast... not one of ours, I think.
shady/compliment: Red hood, grey robes. Perhaps you've finally picked a proper side.
kid/remark: Is that a demon costume? If you're a demon, where are your horns?

compliment: Black robes suit a wizard. You look like you mean your spells.
insult: Black robes on a wizard... trying to look sinister, or just unwashed?
remark: Black robes down to the ankle. Dark wizard, or just in mourning?
kid/remark: Are you a bad wizard? My mum says the ones in black are the bad ones!
wizard/insult: Black robes don't make the spells stronger, whatever you were told.

compliment: That black skirt's got a proper trim. Very smart for a spellcaster.
A wizard's skirt with a trim on it! Somebody's been following clues.
insult: Trim on a wizard's skirt. Does the magic come out fancier too?
remark: Is that gold round the hem of your skirt, or just good lighting?
nan/remark: Ooh, a trimmed skirt, dear. Don't catch that hem on a cauldron.

compliment: A trimmed blue skirt! The Tower would take you on looks alone.
insult: A trim on a blue wizard's skirt. Is that to hide the scorch marks?
remark: That blue skirt's had a trim added. Been digging up caskets, have you?
wizard/remark: A trimmed blue skirt, how the Tower used to dress before it burned.
kid/compliment: Your skirt's got gold on! Can I have the gold bit when it falls off?

compliment: Gold trim on leather chaps. Making the best of a humble start, I see.
insult: Gold trim on cowhide trousers? That's a ribbon on a cow, that is.
remark: Those leather chaps have a gold edge. Did a tanner come into money?
trader/compliment: Gold-edged chaps, my friend! I could sell a dozen of those by teatime.
rough/insult: Fancy trim on tanned cow. Still smells of the tannery from here.

compliment: Studs and a trim on those chaps. You've put some thought into that.
insult: Trimmed studded chaps. Did the cow mind the studs or the colour more?
remark: Studded leather with a trim... somebody's been opening caskets.
plain/insult: All those studs and a pretty trim. Dressed up for a goblin fight, eh?
kid/remark: Your trousers have dots on! Are they buttons, and do they come off?

compliment: Shorts in this weather? There's a dwarf's good sense in you somewhere.
insult: Those shorts stop where they do because they were cut for a dwarf.
remark: Shorts from Keldagrim, those. They fit a dwarf rather better.
dwarf/compliment: Keldagrim shorts on a human! By Guthix, they nearly reach your knees.
kid/remark: Did you lose a bet, or are your trousers only half there on purpose?
nan/remark: Shorts, dear? You'll catch your death. Have you a vest on under there?

compliment: That's a lovely plain skirt. Dwarven cloth, I'd say, by the weave.
insult: A dwarf's skirt on a human... it's more of a belt with ambitions.
remark: That skirt's Keldagrim cloth, I'd wager. The dwarves weave it thick.
dwarf/compliment: Now that skirt's from home. Good thick weave, that'll outlast you.
trader/remark: Agmundi's work, that skirt? The dwarves do a fine seam.

compliment: Good plain trousers, those. Honest cloth, nothing to prove.
insult: Those trousers were cut long for a dwarf. On you they're barely shins.
remark: Dwarf-made trousers, I'd say. They always run short on a human.
dwarf/remark: Vermundi's trousers, those. The long cut, meaning they reach the knee.
kid/remark: Your trousers are too short! Did you grow in the night?

compliment: Canifis cloth, that robe. The haberdasher there does a lovely hem.
insult: Canifis robe bottoms, are they? I'd check the hem for hair, myself.
remark: Barker's robes, I'd say. He makes them roomy, for reasons of his own.
They say the Canifis tailor's a werewolf, hence the roomy cut.
nan/remark: Robes from Canifis, dear? Do give them a wash before you sit down.
kid/remark: My dad says robes from Canifis grow fur when the moon's out!

compliment: That's a Tai Bwo Wannai robe, isn't it! Lovely bright dye on that.
A Karamja villager's robe. The colour's cheered the whole street up.
insult: Bright robe for Karamja, that. In this drizzle it looks a bit lost.
remark: They weave those on Karamja. Paid for in trading sticks, I expect.
kid/compliment: Your skirt's so bright! Did you dye it with a parrot?
pirate/remark: Arr, that's island cloth. Ye've been trading with the Tai Bwo folk.

compliment: A Menaphite kilt. Sensible in the heat, and it does show the calves.
insult: A desert kilt. Those knees haven't seen the sun before, have they?
Kilt's lovely. Knees look like two unbaked loaves, though.
remark: Desert kilt, that. Sophanem or Pollnivneach, going by the colour?
toff/insult: A kilt, citizen? Keep those knees in the desert, where they belong.
kid/remark: Is that a skirt or a kilt? Is the difference how much knee you show?

compliment: Light desert robes, those. You'd stay cool on the walk to Sophanem.
insult: Thin desert robes in this wind. Rather you than me, frankly.
remark: Menaphite cloth, that. It's woven thin, for the heat down there.
trader/compliment: Menaphite robes, my friend! Ali Morrisane's cut, if I'm any judge.
nan/remark: Desert robes, dear? Very light. I'd want a petticoat under that.

compliment: Coarse desert cloth, that. Hard wearing, and it'll shrug off the sand.
insult: Robes the colour of sand. Did you fall over in it on the way here?
remark: Beige desert robes. Rough as sacking, but they do the job out there.
rough/remark: Sacking-coloured robes. Ye've been out past the pass, I'd say.
kid/insult: Your skirt's the colour of porridge!

compliment: You dress like the Meiyerditch folk. Brave, going about like that.
insult: Those trousers look like they've paid the blood tithe themselves.
remark: Meiyerditch trousers, those. Patched more than they've been washed.
Meiyerditch trousers, those. Blending in with the serfs, are you?
shady/insult: Dressed as a tithe-payer. Your sort always did like a disguise.
vicar/remark: Meiyerditch clothes, traveller... Saradomin keep those poor souls.

compliment: Black desert robes. Keeps the sun off and the look stern, that.
insult: A desert robe dyed black? In the sun that's a kettle with legs.
remark: That desert robe's been dyed black. Mushroom ink, by the smell of it.
shady/remark: Black robes from the desert. Someone's been keeping to the shadows.
kid/remark: Your robe's all black! Did you fall in the ink?

compliment: You got out of that desert mining camp in one piece, robe and all.
remark: That's a robe from the desert mines. You got out, then? Good.
nan/remark: Take that robe off this instant, dear, and I'll boil it twice.

compliment: Thick leather trousers. Nothing's getting through those, plague or no.
insult: Those leather trousers creak so loud the street heard you coming.
remark: Plague trousers, those. The doctors in Ardougne swear by them.
Dressed to prod sheep, by the look of those trousers.
rough/insult: Leather all the way down. Hope ye don't need to sit in a hurry.
kid/remark: Are those trousers for the plague? Can I touch them if they work?

compliment: Flares! Nobody wears flares any more. Good on you for standing firm.
insult: Trousers wider at the bottom than the top. Was that done on purpose?
Lovely flares. Shame the wind's got into them.
remark: Flared trousers. You could hide a chicken in each leg.
kid/remark: Do it again! Your trousers go whoosh when you walk, I love it!
toff/insult: Flares, citizen? The peasantry's tailors have much to answer for.

compliment: Pantaloons! Now that's how a gentleman takes a bow.
insult: Someone's slashed your pantaloons. Or did they come like that?
remark: Pantaloons, puffed like a loaf. Very courtly for a market day.
