toff/compliment: Pantaloons! At last, a citizen dressed for the court and not the barn.
kid/insult: Your trousers look like two pillows! Can I have a sit on them later?

compliment: Beekeeper's trousers. Someone who isn't afraid of a sting, good.
insult: Beekeeper's trousers, not a bee about. Did they all up and leave you?
remark: Those are beekeeper's trousers. Got any honey on you, by chance?
nan/remark: A beekeeper, dear? I'll take a jar of honey if you've one spare.
kid/remark: Are you the bee man? Where are the bees? Are they in your trousers?

compliment: Elven cloth, those trousers. Prifddinas tailors sew finer than ours.
insult: Elf trousers on a human. Not sure the elves would be flattered.
remark: Those trousers came from Lliann's in the crystal city, I'd bet.
gnome/remark: Elven legwear, human? You've been up to Prifddinas, then.
toff/compliment: Elven tailoring, citizen. One does admire a people with proper seams.

compliment: An elven skirt! The Prifddinas cut flatters anyone, even a human.
insult: An elf's skirt on you looks like a tablecloth that's lost its table.
remark: A Prifddinas skirt, I think. They do like a clean line, the elves.
fremennik/remark: An elf's skirt, outerlander? Thin stuff for the north, but pretty.
kid/compliment: Is that an elf skirt? Did an actual elf make it, with pointy ears?

compliment: Plain grey platelegs, those. You're the do-it-all-yourself sort.
insult: Those grey platelegs say you'll not borrow a thing, not even a comb.
remark: Grey plate with a badge on. The ones who go it alone wear those.
dwarf/remark: Grey platelegs, plain as a pie tin, but honest iron underneath.
trader/insult: Grey platelegs and a badge. Not buying anything today, then, friend?

compliment: Plain wool skirt, well made. Island work, that, by the weave.
insult: A work skirt. Has it seen any work, or just the walk here?
remark: That's a Wyrmscraig skirt, isn't it? Thick wool for a windy island.
rough/remark: Wool skirt like the Wyrmscraig folk wear. Ye've been over the water.
nan/compliment: Good thick wool, that skirt, dear. Island sheep make the warmest.

compliment: Now that's a fine wool skirt. Noble cut, and the weave's lovely.
insult: A noble's wool skirt. Do the manners come with it, or are those extra?
remark: Wyrmscraig wool, the good sort. Somebody paid dearly for that skirt.
toff/compliment: A proper noble skirt, citizen. Thick wool, good seams, some pedigree.
kid/remark: Your skirt's all woolly! Is it made of a whole sheep?

compliment: Someone's patched that robe with care. It was loved once, I think.
insult: A robe with more patches than robe. Did the moths win, in the end?
remark: That robe's been mended by hand. Nardah cloth, by the look of it.
vicar/remark: A patched temple robe... the desert faithful mend what they can't buy.
nan/compliment: Neat stitching on those patches, dear. Somebody taught you properly.

compliment: A butler's trousers, pressed and proper. Somebody's in service, then.
insult: Butler's trousers. You're not the one who's been stealing the spoons?
Smart trousers for a butler. Mostly clean, which is the main thing.
remark: Butler's uniform, those trousers. Which household are you serving?
toff/remark: A butler, citizen? Good. The drinks tray is through there.
kid/remark: Are you a butler? Do you have to say 'yes, sir' to everyone, even me?

compliment: Proper adventurer's trousers, those. Built for running, by the cut.
insult: Adventuring trousers. Have they had any adventure yet, or is this it?
remark: Dressed for a dash somewhere, are you? Don't let me keep you from it.
guard/remark: Adventurer's trousers. Keep running, and don't knock anyone over.
barkeep/remark: Dressed for a dash, are you? Drink up, then, I'll not be offended.

compliment: Vyrewatch trousers. Bold thing, dressing as the ones who bite.
insult: Dressed like the Vyrewatch, are we? They don't take recruits, I hear.
remark: Those are Vyrewatch trousers. The vampyres won't like the borrowing.
shady/remark: Vyrewatch cloth. Playing at being one of them... how very clever.
vicar/remark: Vyrewatch garb, traveller... Saradomin forgive the disguise.
kid/remark: You're dressed like the bat people! Go on, show me you can fly!

compliment: Pheasant feathers on your legs! Handsome, in a gamebird sort of way.
insult: Feathered trousers. Keep away from the cook, he's got a brace in mind.
remark: Those trousers are all pheasant feathers. Did you pluck them yourself?
rough/insult: Pheasant feathers on yer legs. One gust and ye're in the next field.
kid/remark: You've got bird legs! Can you lay an egg? Lay one right now, go on!

compliment: Alchemist's trousers. You know your mixtures, I shouldn't wonder.
insult: Breezy trousers for an alchemist. Did one of your potions go bang?
remark: Potion stains down those trousers. Mind what you sit on, won't you?
wizard/remark: An alchemist's trousers. Potions are a trade, you know, not an art.
nan/remark: Stains on those trousers, dear. Vinegar and a stiff brush, I'd try.

compliment: Smith's trousers. Leather that's taken sparks and shrugged them off.
insult: Blood on those smith's trousers. Yours, or did the hammer get someone?
remark: Those are foundry trousers. The giants' forge, by the scorching.
dwarf/compliment: Scorch marks on those trousers. By Guthix, you've done a proper shift.
rough/remark: Dried blood on the waist there. Did the hammer slip, or did somebody?

compliment: Gold prospector's trousers! Somebody's been catching falling stars.
insult: Gold trousers for mining. Like wearing a crown to muck out the stable.
remark: Gold prospector's trousers. The miners will see you coming a mile off.
dwarf/remark: Gold prospector's legs. Stardust, is it? Fancy, for someone who digs.
kid/compliment: Your trousers are gold! Can I scrape a bit off if it's real gold?

compliment: Forester's trousers, those. Been making friends with the foresters?
insult: Forester's trousers. Do the trees know you're coming, or do you sneak?
remark: Those are forester's trousers. Pockets full of bark, I expect.
rough/remark: Forester's trousers. Chopped anything today, or just admired it?
gnome/remark: A forester, human? The Stronghold's trees would like a word, I think.

compliment: Those are Hunters' Guild trousers. Somebody's a dab hand with a trap.
insult: Hunter's trousers from the guild. Caught anything, or mostly brambles?
remark: Guild hunter's trousers. Tough leather, for pushing through scrub.
rough/compliment: Hunter's leathers. Ye've knelt at a few traps in those, by the knees.
kid/remark: Are you a hunter? Have you got a chinchompa, and does it go bang?

compliment: Hide trousers, and a few hides at that. Nothing wasted, I like that.
insult: Three animals in those trousers, at least. Did none of them fit alone?
remark: Mixed hides on those legs. I can't tell where the kebbit stops.
rough/remark: Patchwork hides. Whatever ye couldn't skin whole, I'd say.
kid/remark: Your trousers are made of animals! Which ones, and were they friends?

compliment: Dragonstones set into platelegs! Somebody's been lucky with a chest.
Purple stones in rune plate. Jeweller's work on a smith's armour.
insult: Gems in your platelegs. Lovely, until the first goblin prises one out.
remark: Dragonstones in those platelegs. Mind who you turn your back on.
dwarf/compliment: Dragonstones in rune. By Guthix, two trades on one pair of legs.
trader/compliment: Dragonstone platelegs, my friend! Name a price and I'll weep at it.

compliment: Polished like an Ardougne knight's. Someone's been busy with a cloth.
insult: Ardougne knight's platelegs. Did you earn them, or just polish them?
remark: Those platelegs shine like a knight's, but it's plain steel under.
guard/remark: Knight of Ardougne, are you? Papers, then. Or at least a good excuse.
toff/remark: Ardougne plate, citizen. Their knights do keep a shine on the steel.

compliment: Grim dark leggings, those. You look like you've buried a few.
insult: Deadman's leggings. Numb from the knees down, by the way you walk.
remark: Those leggings came off a corpse, I'd say. Did the owner object much?
shady/remark: Deadman's leggings. Wear them long enough and the name fits.
kid/remark: Are those a dead man's trousers? Did you dig him up, and was he cross?

compliment: Those waders have a ghostly glow. Been fishing somewhere strange?
insult: Glowing waders. Do the fish see you coming, or just the ghosts?
remark: Blue see-through waders. Spirit-touched, I'd say, or just haunted.
rough/compliment: Spirit waders. Blimey, ye've been out at Unkah in a storm.
pirate/remark: Arr, glowing waders. Ye've met the storm spirit and lived to fish on.

compliment: Emissary robes, worn well. You'd pass for one of them, in poor light.
insult: Twilight Emissary robes. Joined up, or just borrowed the uniform?
remark: Those are the Emissaries' robes. Fortis folk give those a wide berth.
shady/remark: Emissary robes. The Twilight lot don't lend those, so you took them.
vicar/remark: Twilight Emissary robes... not a faith I'd keep, traveller.
guard/remark: Emissary robes. I'll be keeping an eye on you, if it's all the same.

compliment: Relic hunter's trousers. You look like you dig old things up.
insult: Fancy trousers for a relic hunter. Found anything, or just the outfit?
remark: Those trousers have a great many pockets. Collecting relics, are you?
wizard/remark: Relic hunter garb. Do try not to dig up anything that bites.
kid/remark: Treasure hunter, are you? Did you find any, and is it in your pockets?

compliment: Explorer's trousers, well travelled. Blazed a trail or two in those.
insult: Trailblazer's trousers. The trail round here is a road, you know.
remark: Those trousers have seen some paths. Mud from three kingdoms on them.
fremennik/compliment: A trailblazer, outerlander? The north has trails nobody's named yet.
trader/remark: Explorer's trousers, my friend? Maps are sold two doors down.

compliment: Relic hunter's trousers, well made. Have you found much, lately?
insult: Relic hunter's trousers. Most relics round here are in the museum.
remark: Dressed for digging up old things? The Varrock museum pays, I hear.
rough/insult: Relic hunter, eh? That's a grave robber with better trousers.
kid/remark: Have you found a relic? What is a relic, is it like a bone?

compliment: A swamp captain's trousers. Takes a brave sailor to love those waters.
insult: Those trousers smell of bog. Whoever owned them sailed somewhere foul.
remark: Captain's trousers, stained with bog. Been out on the marsh, have you?
pirate/remark: Arr, swamp sailor's breeches. Ye've been where the water don't move.
nan/remark: Those trousers want airing, dear. I can smell the marsh from here.

compliment: A fine captain's trousers, those. Calm seas all the way, were they?
insult: Fine captain's trousers. Sailed for them, or found them in a chest?
remark: A sea captain's trousers. Salt in the seams, I shouldn't wonder.
pirate/compliment: Arr, a proper captain's breeches! Ye've sailed far lagoons in those.
fremennik/remark: Sailor's trousers, outerlander. The sea's ours, but you may borrow it.

compliment: Evening trousers with white stockings! Off to the Party Room, are you?
insult: Dark trousers and white stockings. Some ball is missing a guest.
remark: Dress trousers and stockings. Bit formal for the sewers, that.
toff/compliment: Evening dress, citizen! Finally, someone who knows their forks.
kid/remark: Are you a lord? Is that why your socks go right up to your knees?

compliment: Pale evening trousers. Bold, in a kingdom this muddy, and dashing.
insult: White trousers and white stockings. One puddle and the evening's over.
remark: Light dress trousers. Somebody's keeping those away from the stables.
toff/compliment: Pale evening dress, citizen. The summer ball, I presume, or a wedding.
barkeep/remark: White trousers in here, love? Mind the ale, it's been a messy night.

compliment: Blessed dragonhide, blue and white. Saradomin's own rangers, nearly.
insult: Saradomin's star on your chaps. The holy bit doesn't cover the rest.
remark: Dragonhide chaps with Saradomin's star. Blessed by someone, anyway.
vicar/compliment: Saradomin's star on dragonhide, traveller. His blessing suits it well.
shady/insult: Saradomin's colours on your legs. Your sort does like to be seen.

compliment: Red hide with Zamorak's mark. Striking, if you don't mind the stares.
insult: Zamorak's mark on your chaps. Does your mother know you wear those?
remark: Zamorak's mark on those chaps. Blessed, they say, which is a stretch.
vicar/insult: Zamorak's mark on your chaps, traveller... I'll pray for the leather.
shady/compliment: Zamorak's mark on dragonhide. Perhaps there's hope for you yet.

compliment: Green dragonhide with Guthix's mark. Balanced, and a nice colour too.
insult: Guthix's mark on your chaps. Balance in all things but your spending.
remark: Those chaps carry Guthix's symbol. The druids would approve, I think.
dwarf/compliment: Guthix's mark on good green hide. By Guthix, that's a sight to see.
gnome/compliment: Guthix's sign on your chaps, human! Balance looks well on you.

compliment: Dragonhide with Bandos's mark. The war god's blessing on a ranger.
insult: Bandos's symbol on your chaps. Half the goblins will want a word.
remark: Those chaps carry Bandos's mark. Not a god known for his tailoring.
goblin/compliment: Big High War God mark on legs! You good. You smash things with us.
vicar/remark: The war god's mark on your chaps, traveller... a troubling blessing.

compliment: Dragonhide with Armadyl's wings. Light as a feather, I should think.
insult: Armadyl's wings on your chaps. Pity they do nothing for the legs.
remark: Those chaps bear Armadyl's symbol. The bird god's folk would approve.
wizard/remark: Armadyl's sigil on dragonhide. The aviansie would find that most odd.
kid/compliment: Your trousers have got wings on! Jump and see if you can fly!

compliment: Purple dragonhide with that old symbol. Blessed by something very old.
insult: That symbol on your chaps belongs to a god nobody mentions any more.
remark: The mark on your chaps isn't one of the usual gods, it's much older.
wizard/remark: That sigil on your chaps is the Empty Lord's, if my books are right.
shady/compliment: An ancient mark on dragonhide. Somebody's read the right books.

compliment: Ranger's tights! You could outrun a kebbit in those.
insult: Tights, on a ranger? The deer will be too busy laughing to run.
remark: Green tights, like the old rangers wore. Not many of those about now.
rough/insult: Tights. On a grown archer. Blimey, the deer'll never take ye serious.
kid/remark: You're wearing tights! My sister's got tights, are those hers?

compliment: That's the Black Knights' better plate. Heavy, and worn like nothing.
insult: Elite black plate. Did you take those off a knight, or off a peg?
remark: Black Knight plate, the elite sort. Taken off one of them, I assume.
guard/insult: Black Knight plate on my street. Explain yourself, and keep it short.
toff/remark: Black Knight plate, citizen? Do keep that away from the White Knights.

compliment: Dark robes with a storm in the weave. The first owner meant it.
insult: The Dark Squall's robes. On you they're more of a light breeze.
remark: Those robes belonged to someone the Black Knights called master.
shady/remark: The Squall's own robes. Either very bold or very foolish, meddler.
wizard/remark: The Dark Squall's robes. I'd not wear them near a Saradominist.
guard/remark: Dark robes, Zamorakian cut. I'll be noting the time you passed.

compliment: Red crystal legs. Grown in the dark under Prifddinas, those, I'd say.
insult: Red crystal armour. Crystal's meant to be blue, so that's gone off.
remark: Those crystal legs have gone red. The elves call that corrupted.
gnome/remark: Red crystal, human? Even the elves don't wear that colour on purpose.
kid/remark: Your legs are made of red glass! Do they go clink when you walk?

compliment: Vyre noble's trousers, and worn like you were born in Darkmeyer.
insult: Dressed like a vampyre noble. The teeth don't match, though, do they?
remark: Vyre noble's trousers. Scented with something I'd rather not know.
shady/compliment: Darkmeyer finery. Now that is a disguise worth the trouble, meddler.
vicar/remark: A vampyre noble's clothes, traveller... I'll say a prayer regardless.

compliment: Vampyre noble's trousers, finely cut. The Darkmeyer seamstress, is it?
insult: Vyre noble's trousers. Did the sneer come with them, or is that yours?
remark: Those trousers are cut the Darkmeyer way. Narrow and a bit funereal.
toff/compliment: Darkmeyer tailoring, citizen. Dreadful people, but faultless seams.
kid/insult: You're dressed like a vampyre! Can I see if your teeth are pointy?

compliment: A vyre noble's skirt. Darkmeyer cuts a cold line, and it suits you.
insult: A vampyre's skirt. Hemmed in the dark, or is that the look they want?
remark: That skirt's Darkmeyer finery. The living don't often get to wear it.
nan/remark: A vampyre's skirt, dear? Hang it in the sun, that'll sort the smell.
shady/remark: A Darkmeyer noble's skirt. Somebody got close to the vyres and lived.

compliment: A Darkmeyer gown. Grim colours, but there's craft in every fold of it.
insult: A vampyre's ball gown, in daylight. Someone's missed the point of it.
remark: A Darkmeyer court gown, that. Long, dark, and no good for running in.
toff/remark: A vampyre court gown, citizen? One hopes the invitation was genuine.
kid/remark: Is that a vampyre dress? Does it turn into a bat when you spin?

compliment: Coat tails, Darkmeyer style. Very grand, in a graveyard sort of way.
insult: Coat tails from the vampyre court. Mind they don't trip you up.
remark: Coat tails cut like a vyre noble's. Long enough to sweep a crypt.
toff/compliment: Coat tails, citizen! At last, someone in town who owns a tailcoat.
barkeep/remark: Coat tails in here? Keep them off the fire, they'd go up a treat.

compliment: Relic hunter's robeskirt, and a grand one. You've travelled for that.
insult: A robeskirt for relic hunting. Most relics are underground, you know.
remark: That's a relic hunter's robeskirt. Where do you keep what you find?
wizard/compliment: A relic hunter in robes, not leathers. Finally, one with some sense.
kid/remark: Is that a skirt or a robe? Which half is which, and does it matter?

compliment: Temple of the Eye robes. The runecrafters wear those with pride.
insult: There's an eye on your robes, and it keeps looking at me.
remark: Temple of the Eye robes, those. There's a whiff of the Abyss on them.
wizard/remark: Temple of the Eye robes. Do give my regards to the Great Guardian.
kid/remark: Your trousers have got an eye on! Does it blink, and can it see me?

compliment: Green dragonhide with a trim on it. A ranger with a bit of polish.
insult: A trim on green dragonhide. Did the dragon come decorated, or did you?
remark: Those green chaps have a coloured edge. Somebody's been reading clues.
trader/compliment: Trimmed green hide, my friend! Rangers pay dear for that edge.
kid/compliment: Your green trousers have stripes! Is it real dragon, and did it roar?

compliment: Gravedigger's leggings. Honest work, and somebody's got to do it.
insult: Gravedigger's leggings. There's a finger bone in the hem, you know.
remark: Gravedigger's leggings, muddy at the knee... I shan't ask whose grave.
vicar/remark: A gravedigger's leggings, traveller. The churchyard thanks you.
kid/remark: Are you a gravedigger? If you dig up a skeleton, can I have it?

compliment: Sensible gloves, those. Keeps the splinters off, I'll bet.
insult: Leather gloves? Were you expecting a stiff breeze?
remark: Off to muck out the stables in those gloves, are you?
nan/remark: Keep your hands warm, dear. Those gloves will do for a start.
kid/remark: Are those gloves real cow? Did you know the cow, or was it a stranger?
rough/compliment: Proper work gloves. Somebody here's done a day's graft.

compliment: Leather on the forearms, nice and plain, and nothing to go wrong.
insult: Armour on your wrists and nowhere else? Bold plan for the goblins.
remark: Bracers like those, you're either a bowman or a bit cold.
kid/insult: Those aren't gloves, they stop at the wrist, so where's the rest?
rough/remark: Leather on the arms. Bowstring been biting you, has it?

compliment: Stiff leather, those gloves. They'll soften up with wear.
insult: Can you bend your fingers in those, or do you point at things now?
remark: Hard leather gloves. Somebody boiled those, by the look of them.
barkeep/remark: You'll not get a grip on a tankard in those stiff gloves, love.
kid/remark: Your gloves look like they'd stand up on their own!

compliment: Claws on your bracers! Nobody's grabbing your wrist in those.
insult: Spikes on your wrists? Don't scratch your nose, whatever you do.
remark: Kebbit claws on your bracers, is it? Rather you than the kebbit.
kid/compliment: Spiky arms! Can you climb trees with them, like a cat?
rough/insult: Spikes on yer wrists? Mind you don't scratch yourself shaving.
nan/remark: Careful with those spiky things, dear, you'll have my knitting.

compliment: Green dragonhide on your arms. The tanner did a fair job of that.
insult: Green hide bracers. Did you find a dragon, or a very big lizard?
remark: Dragonhide, that is. Green, so the dragon was one of the small ones.
kid/remark: Is that from a real dragon? Did it mind you taking its skin?
rough/remark: Green hide. Hunted it yerself, or bought it off a stall?

compliment: Snakeskin on your arms, very exotic. Came off the islands, I expect.
insult: Snakeskin bracers. Does it still hiss when it rains?
remark: That's snake on your arms, isn't it? Big snake, by the look of it.
pirate/remark: Arr, snakeskin. Them swamp snakes on Mos Le'Harmless, I'll wager.
kid/insult: Snake arms! Did you eat the rest of it?

compliment: Nice colour on those gloves. Barkers' in Canifis, I'd put money on it.
insult: Coloured gloves and nothing to match. Dressed in the dark, were we?
remark: Those gloves are from the haberdasher's in Canifis, aren't they?
nan/compliment: Pretty gloves, dear. I had a pair that colour once.
kid/remark: Why are your gloves that colour? Did they come like that, or did you?
toff/insult: Dyed gloves. The peasantry discovers colour, and uses all of it.

compliment: Metal in the weave of those gloves, sturdier than they look.
insult: Metal gloves? You'll jingle when you clap.
remark: Were those gloves from the chest under the castle at Lumbridge?
dwarf/remark: Iron thread in a glove. Fiddly work, that, and no mistake.
kid/remark: Are your gloves magnetic? Hold still, I've got a nail.

compliment: Boxing gloves! You've the stance for it, I'll give you that.
insult: Boxing gloves. Who are you fighting, and do they know?
Padded gloves, eh? I'd worry, if you looked like you'd landed one.
remark: Can you hold anything in those boxing gloves, or do you just wave?
kid/compliment: Boxing gloves! Hit him, not me, he's the bigger one!
barkeep/remark: Boxing gloves in my bar? Take it outside, and mind the window.
guard/insult: Boxing gloves. No brawling in the street, padded or otherwise.

compliment: White gloves, spotless. You've not touched a thing all day, have you?
insult: White gloves. One handshake with a farmer and that's over.
remark: White gloves like the knights wear in Falador, are you one of theirs?
toff/compliment: White gloves. At last, a citizen who understands how to dress.
rough/insult: White gloves? Never done a day's muck in yer life, then.
kid/remark: Your gloves are really white. Can I touch them with jam on?

compliment: Plain gold bracelet. Says more than a big stone would, that.
insult: A gold bracelet and no stone in it? Did the jeweller run out?
remark: That bracelet catches the sun. Keep your sleeve down near the docks.
trader/compliment: Gold on the wrist, my friend! Now there's a customer I can work with.
kid/remark: Is that real gold on your arm? Bite it, that's how you can tell.
goblin/compliment: Shiny arm thing. Goblin want shiny arm thing.

compliment: Blue stone in a gold band. That's a tidy bit of work on your wrist.
insult: A sapphire bracelet. Pity it's wasted on that sleeve.
remark: Sapphire on the wrist, is it? Blue suits you better than you'd think.
nan/compliment: Ooh, a sapphire, dear. My Albert never bought me so much as a bead.
kid/remark: Your bracelet's blue! Is it made of ice, or just pretending?

compliment: Green stone on gold. Someone's been to a proper jeweller.
insult: An emerald bracelet. Shame the rest of you's not up to it.
remark: Is that an emerald on your wrist, or a nice bit of bottle glass?
gnome/compliment: Green on gold, human! Very nearly gnomish taste, that.
trader/remark: Emerald, my friend? I know a buyer, and he's standing right here.

compliment: A ruby on the wrist. Red as a good wine, that one.
insult: Red stone, gold band, and a muddy hand under it, I see.
remark: Ruby bracelet. Were you given that, or did you earn it?
kid/remark: Your bracelet's got a red sweet stuck in it! Can I have the sweet bit?
vicar/remark: A ruby, traveller. Mind it doesn't become a thing you love too much.

compliment: Milky little stone on that bracelet. Pretty, in a quiet sort of way.
insult: An opal bracelet. The sort of thing you buy when the ruby's gone.
remark: Opal, is it? Changes colour when you turn your wrist, I'll bet.
kid/compliment: Your bracelet's all rainbowy inside! How did they get that in there?
dwarf/remark: Opal. Soft stone, that. Don't go hitting anything with it.

compliment: Jade on your wrist. Cool green, that, like a pond in shade.
insult: Jade bracelet. Did you win it, or was it just the one left?
remark: Green stone bracelet. Jade, isn't it, the green that's nearly grey?
nan/remark: Jade, dear? My mother swore it kept the toads off, and she'd know.
trader/compliment: Jade on the wrist, my friend. A quiet stone for a quiet fortune.

compliment: A red topaz on gold. Catches the firelight nicely, I should think.
insult: Topaz bracelet. Red enough to pass for ruby from across the road.
remark: Is that a ruby on your wrist? No, topaz. Near enough from here, mind.
kid/remark: Your bracelet's gone all orange! Is it one of those boiled sweets?
trader/remark: Topaz, my friend. Looks like ruby, costs like topaz, the clever buy.

compliment: Sapphire bracelet and clay under your nails. A potter with some taste.
insult: Nice bracelet, and clay up both arms. Did you fall in the clay pit?
remark: Been at the clay pits, have you? Your bracelet's gone grey with it.
kid/remark: Is that clay on your bracelet? Were you making pots without me?
rough/remark: Clay bracelet, eh? Soft clay comes up easy with one o' them, they say.

compliment: Emerald bracelet. Castle Wars, is it? Pick the side that's winning.
insult: An enchanted bracelet for a game of flags? Whatever happened to legs?
remark: That's one of the bracelets the Castle Wars lot wear, isn't it?
kid/remark: Is that for the flag game? Which side, and are you winning?
fremennik/compliment: A charm for the castle game. A fight over a flag is still a fight.

compliment: Jade bracelet and mortar on your cuff. Been at the temple in Mort'ton?
insult: Jade and plaster dust. Half jeweller, half builder, and all of a mess.
remark: Jade on the wrist, is it? Looks like it's been through a lime kiln.
vicar/remark: Jade charm for the Mort'ton temple, is it? Even the dead want a roof.
burgher/remark: That bracelet. Them temple builders over at Mort'ton wear 'em.

compliment: Thick warm gloves, those. You've been up north with the pyromancers.
insult: Warm gloves? It's not even snowing. Where do you think you are?
remark: Those gloves look singed. Been feeding something very large a fire?
kid/remark: Your gloves are all sooty! Did you put your hands in the fire?
nan/compliment: Sensible warm gloves, dear. At last, someone dressed for the weather.
dwarf/remark: Warm gloves. Fireproof, they say. I'd test that on someone else first.

compliment: Thick leather gloves. Keeping the spider bites off, I'll bet.
insult: Leather gloves for spiders? Round here we use a boot.
remark: Those gloves look made for handling something you'd rather not touch.
slayer_master/remark: Gloves for the fever spiders. Those bites fester something awful.
kid/remark: Are those spider gloves? Can a spider bite through a glove, then?

compliment: Wolf fur in those gloves! Warm hands and a story, I shouldn't wonder.
insult: Fur-lined gloves. Did the wolf agree, or did you just outrun it?
remark: Dug those gloves up, didn't you? There's still soil in the seams.
rough/remark: Wolf fur gloves, dug up under an oak. Who buries a pair of gloves?
kid/compliment: Furry gloves! Is that wolf? Did you fight a wolf for them?

compliment: Steel gauntlets at the stove? Whatever keeps the fish from burning.
insult: Gauntlets on, and you still smell of burnt lobster, if I'm honest.
remark: Grease on those gauntlets. You cook in them, do you, or just eat?
barkeep/remark: Gauntlets for cooking? My cook uses a cloth and swears a lot.
dwarf/compliment: Steel gauntlets for the frying pan. By Guthix, that's the proper way.

compliment: Gold dust on those gauntlets. You've a furnace that likes you.
insult: Gauntlets for melting gold. Shame none of it stuck to you.
remark: Those gauntlets have a goldsmith's look. Much time at the furnace?
dwarf/remark: Goldsmith's gauntlets. Made for the furnace and a steady hand, those.
trader/compliment: Gauntlets for gold, my friend? You and I should talk about rates.

compliment: Those gauntlets hum. Something's been cast through them, often.
insult: Gauntlets that give a spell more bite. Shame they can't aim it too.
remark: Odd gauntlets, those. They'd sting if you shook my hand, I'd say.
wizard/remark: Enchanted gauntlets for bolt spells. Blunt magic, but loud, I grant.
vicar/remark: Those gauntlets have a touch of chaos about them, mind the candles.

compliment: Fine steel gauntlets. Old family work, those, by the engraving.
insult: Steel gauntlets and not a scratch on them. Heirloom, or just unused?
remark: Those gauntlets look like they belong to somebody's great-grandfather.
toff/remark: Those gauntlets bear a crest. One hopes you came by them honourably.
dwarf/compliment: Steel gauntlets, proper jointed. Somebody knew what they were about.

compliment: Ruby bracelet with a charm on it. Keeps the sickness off, they say.
insult: Charmed against disease, is it? You could just not lick the ogres.
remark: That ruby's enchanted, isn't it? Been near the zogres, I'd guess.
nan/remark: A charm against sickness, dear? Soup and an early night works too.
vicar/remark: A charm against disease on your wrist. Prayer helps too, traveller.

compliment: An opal charm on the wrist. Gets the dull work done quicker, I hear.
insult: A charm to hurry your chores along. Couldn't just work faster, then?
remark: Opal charm. You've a list of things to kill and no patience for it.
slayer_master/remark: An opal charm to hurry the task. I'd sooner you did it properly.
kid/insult: Your bracelet makes chores go faster? My mum needs one more than you.

compliment: Topaz charm on the wrist. Makes the fight last, for them that like it.
insult: A charm so the killing lasts longer? Some people take up fishing.
remark: Topaz charm, is it? The one that keeps you at your work a bit longer.
slayer_master/compliment: Slaughter charm. Good. Nothing wrong with wanting more of a thing.
guard/remark: Bracelet of slaughter, is it. That's a name I'm writing down.

compliment: Diamond charm for the Abyss. Rather you than me, going through there.
insult: Charmed for the Abyss? There's a perfectly good hole by the mill.
remark: That diamond's enchanted. You've been through the Abyss, haven't you?
wizard/remark: An abyssal charm. Sensible, if you must go poking through that place.
kid/remark: Is your bracelet for the monster hole? What do the monsters look like?

compliment: Dragonstone on the wrist, charmed. The guilds know your face, I'd say.
insult: A bracelet that counts your kills for you? Fingers not enough, then?
remark: That bracelet talks, they say. Tells you how many are left to kill.
slayer_master/remark: Bracelet counts the task for you. I'll still want the full tally.
kid/remark: Does your bracelet really talk? Make it say something to me!

compliment: A diamond on your wrist. Every window in town just noticed.
insult: Diamond bracelet. All that sparkle, and mud on both your knees.
remark: That diamond catches the light. Keep your sleeve over it in Varrock.
trader/compliment: A diamond, my friend! Now we're talking the same language at last.
shady/remark: Diamond on the wrist. Noted. Your sort never learns to cover up.
kid/compliment: Your bracelet's got a diamond in! Is it the biggest one in the world?

compliment: A dragonstone, no less. That bracelet's worth more than my roof.
insult: A dragonstone bracelet, and you still haggle over bread, I've seen it.
remark: Is that a dragonstone? Purple, deep. You don't see many on a wrist.
trader/compliment: Dragonstone, my friend! I'd name a price but my heart would give out.
kid/remark: A dragon's stone? Did you pinch it while the dragon was asleep?

compliment: Proper mining gloves, those. Belona's, from the guild in Falador.
insult: Mining gloves with no dust on them. Admiring the rocks, were we?
remark: Those gloves are from the mining guild, aren't they, under Falador?
dwarf/compliment: Mining gloves from the guild. Now you're dressed like you mean it.
dwarf/remark: Gloves for the pick. Saves the hands, but you'll miss the calluses.
rough/remark: Fancy mining gloves. In my day ye just bled on the ore an' got on.

compliment: Smith's gloves, scorched at the fingers. You've been at the big forge.
insult: Smith's gloves. Does the hammer come with them, or do you borrow one?
remark: Heavy gloves, those. Giant's forge, I heard, over in Kourend.
dwarf/compliment: Smith's gloves from the giants' foundry! By Guthix, that's proper kit.
rough/remark: Them's forge gloves. Heat like that'd take the skin off yer knuckles.

compliment: Ice gloves! Took those off the queen under the mountain, I'd wager.
insult: Gloves that stay cold. Handy for the fish, murder on a handshake.
remark: Your gloves are steaming in this air. Are they actually made of ice?
kid/compliment: Ice gloves! Can you freeze a puddle so I can slide on it?
nan/remark: Ice on your hands, dear? You'll have chilblains by supper.
dwarf/remark: Ice gloves. Lets you lift a bar straight from the furnace, that does.

compliment: Gloves from Karamja. Pirate Jackie's lot give those to island friends.
insult: Karamja gloves. Do they smell of rum, or is that just you?
remark: Island gloves, those. The shops over there will know your face.
pirate/compliment: Arr, Karamja gloves! Ye've done the island a good turn or two, then.
tzhaar/remark: Gloves from the island above. JalYt walk our land, not just under it.
kid/remark: Island gloves! Did you see the volcano go bang?

compliment: Mourner's gloves, and you still look like yourself, which is a trick.
insult: Mourner's gloves. Working for that lot, or did you just find a pair?
remark: Those gloves are from the mourners in West Ardougne, aren't they?
guard/remark: Mourner's gloves, west side issue. I'll not ask how you got them.
shady/compliment: Mourner's gloves. Perhaps your sort has its uses after all.

compliment: Dark fur gloves. I never heard you come up, and I was listening.
insult: Gloves that soft are for other folks' pockets, and mine's empty.
remark: Kebbit fur, those gloves. The dark sort, that you don't hear coming.
guard/insult: Thief's gloves, those. Keep your hands where I can see them.
kid/remark: Your gloves are so quiet! Clap in them, I want to see if it's silent.
trader/remark: Soft gloves, my friend. I'll be watching my stall all the same.

compliment: Gloves that light, you must have earned them at the barbarian outpost.
insult: Gloves from the barbarian outpost. Which role did you let down, then?
remark: Those gloves look like they'd blow away. Do they stay on in a wind?
barbarian/compliment: Outpost gloves! You've stood against the Penance and kept your hands.
fremennik/remark: Light gloves from the outpost. Our cousins there fight strange wars.
kid/compliment: Light gloves! Can you catch eggs in those, or do they go splat?

compliment: Crab shell on your knuckles! Rellekka work, that, and good work.
insult: Gloves made of crab shell. Is that the tide I can smell, or you?
remark: Those gloves are bits of rock crab stitched together, aren't they?
fremennik/compliment: Rock-shell on your hands, outerlander. Our crabs have made you a gift.
kid/remark: Your gloves are made of crab! Can they still pinch anybody?

compliment: Bone gloves, stitched neat. Whatever it was, it's working for you now.
insult: Gloves made of bone. Do you take them off, or is that just your hands?
remark: Those gloves are bone fragments. Some sea creature's, by the colour.
fremennik/remark: Wallasalki bone, outerlander, and those beasts take some killing.
vicar/remark: Bones on your hands, traveller. I trust whatever it was had no family.
kid/insult: Skeleton hands! You're not a real skeleton, I can see your face.

compliment: Granite gloves! From the gargoyles on the tower roof, I'd wager.
insult: Stone gloves. Try waving at someone, I've got all day.
remark: Are those gloves granite? How do you lift your arms?
dwarf/compliment: Granite on the knuckles. By Guthix, that'll leave a dent in something.
kid/remark: Your gloves are rock! Can you punch through a wall with them?
troll/compliment: Rock hands. Troll like rock hands. Taste like mountain, maybe.

compliment: Light gloves for the bowstring, those. They fit like a second skin.
insult: Ranger's gloves. Nothing a bowman likes more than being seen in kit.
remark: Those are an archer's gloves, aren't they, without a mark on them yet?
gnome/compliment: Ranger's gloves, human! A gnome archer would be proud of those.
kid/remark: Are those bow gloves? Shoot an apple off my head, I'll hold still.

compliment: Mystic gloves, with the trim. Somebody's been earning their robes.
insult: Fancy wizard gloves. Do they stop the sparks, or just hide the burns?
remark: Those gloves match a mystic robe, don't they, so where's the rest?
wizard/compliment: Mystic gloves. One sees them on the better sort of apprentice.
wizard/insult: Mystic gloves. Can you actually cast, or are they just for warmth?
kid/remark: Wizard gloves! Do sparks come out of the fingers when you point?

compliment: Suqah leather gloves. You've been to the moon folk's island and back.
insult: Gloves from the lunar isle. Still talking to yourself in your sleep?
remark: Pale gloves, those, with the moon markings, and not from round here.
moon_clan/compliment: Suqah hide on your hands. You walked our dream, and it let you go.
wizard/remark: Lunar gloves. The Moon Clan's magic is peculiar, but it's not nothing.
kid/remark: Are those gloves from the moon? Did you go on a boat or just float up?

compliment: Bark gauntlets bound in fine cloth. Clever stuff to get from a tree.
insult: Are those gauntlets bark? Mind the woodpeckers don't take a fancy.
remark: Those gauntlets look like tree bark. They are tree bark, aren't they?
wizard/remark: Splitbark gauntlets. The old wizards swore by it, and by leeches.
kid/remark: Your gloves are made of tree! Is there a bird living in them?

compliment: Green bark gauntlets, with a whiff of the nature altar about them.
insult: Swamp bark gauntlets. Does it smell, or is that just the swamp on you?
remark: Those gauntlets are bark gone green. Something's been growing on them.
wizard/remark: Swampbark. Bark soaked in nature magic, and it does smell of it.
leprechaun/remark: Green bark on yer hands, is it? Me compost heap's jealous.

compliment: Red bark gauntlets. That's blood magic in the wood, and it's held.
insult: Bark gauntlets gone red. Is that blood, or did you just paint them?
remark: Those gauntlets are bark, but red through. Been near the blood altar?
vicar/remark: Red bark on your hands, traveller. I'd rather not ask what soaked it.
wizard/compliment: Bloodbark! Bark that's been to the altar and come back the stronger.
kid/remark: Your gloves are red! Did a tree bleed on them, or was it you?

compliment: Coloured dragonhide on your arms. That hide came off something angry.
insult: Bright dragonhide bracers. Nothing says hunter like being seen first.
remark: Was the dragon that colour, or did the tanner dye those bracers?
rough/remark: Dragonhide bracers, coloured. Cost more than my cow, I'll bet.
kid/compliment: Dragon arms! Was it a big dragon? Was it bigger than a house?

compliment: Good solid gloves, those. Somebody fitted them properly.
insult: Nice gloves. Nicer than the rest of you, if we're being honest.
remark: Those gloves are from the chest under Lumbridge castle, aren't they?
barkeep/remark: Gloves from the Lumbridge cellar, eh? That cook still owes me a pie.
kid/remark: Your gloves look like sneaking gloves. Are they for sneaking up on me?

compliment: Very nice gloves. You did the Lumbridge cook a good turn, I hear.
insult: Fine gloves. Shame about the hands in them.
remark: Gloves like those come from the cellar at Lumbridge, so the cook says.
dwarf/remark: Rune thread in a glove? Fiddly work. I'd want a pie after that.
kid/compliment: Your gloves are really nice! Can I try the left one on, just the left?

compliment: Black dragonhide on your arms. That came off something with a name.
insult: Black hide bracers, very fierce. The dragon's still about, I take it?
remark: That hide's black. A big dragon, that, the kind you hear about.
fremennik/compliment: Black dragonhide, outerlander. Even our sagas are short on those.
kid/compliment: Black dragon arms! Did you kill it yourself, or did someone help?

compliment: Very fine gloves. The cook at Lumbridge must think the world of you.
insult: Fine gloves. Did you save a dinner for those, or just attend one?
remark: Those gloves have a red trim to them. Not from any stall round here.
barkeep/remark: Gloves from the Lumbridge cellar, eh? Luckier cook than mine, him.
kid/compliment: Red gloves! Are they dragon? Are they made of actual dragon?

compliment: Those gloves! The last pair out of that Lumbridge cellar, they say.
Finest gloves I've seen on anyone this side of the palace.
insult: Fine gloves. Saved a dinner party from a mad cook for those, did you?
remark: Those gloves fit like they were cut for you and nobody else.
toff/compliment: Now those are gloves. A citizen with some sense of occasion at last.
trader/remark: Those gloves, my friend, are the sort I'd keep behind the counter.
kid/remark: Are those the best gloves? My dad says there's a best pair somewhere.

compliment: Those gloves shimmer. Earned at the mages' arena, I shouldn't wonder.
insult: Shimmery gloves. Do they do anything, or just catch the light?
remark: Those gloves aren't quite one colour, are they, the way they shift?
wizard/compliment: Infinity gloves. Someone has been paying attention at the arena.
wizard/insult: Infinity gloves. The arena hands those to anyone with enough patience.
kid/remark: Your gloves are sparkly! Do they go on forever, or stop at the wrist?

compliment: A black stone on gold. Onyx, that is, and I've only seen one before.
insult: Onyx on the wrist. Did you buy that, or has someone not noticed yet?
remark: That stone's black as a well at midnight. Where did you come by that?
trader/compliment: Onyx, my friend. Don't shake my hand, I'd never let go.
tzhaar/remark: Black stone on JalYt wrist. That stone is from our caves, no?
kid/remark: Your bracelet's got a black stone! Is it a hole, or just very dark?

compliment: That onyx has a warmth to it. You'll heal quicker than most, I'd say.
insult: A bracelet that mends you faster. Planning on needing it, then?
remark: Charmed onyx, isn't it? Your cuts close while you walk, they say.
nan/compliment: Ooh, that onyx charm. You'll be right as rain by teatime, dear.
vicar/remark: A healing charm on your wrist. Prayer does the same, and costs less.
kid/remark: Does your bracelet fix cuts? I've got one on my knee, look, fix it!

compliment: That stone on your wrist glows. Zenyte, they call it, and it's rare.
insult: A glowing bracelet. Handy if you lose your hand in the dark.
remark: Is that bracelet glowing, or is it the light in here?
kid/compliment: Your bracelet's glowing orange! Is it hot, or just pretending to be?
monkey/remark: That orange stone. Gorillas carry those, and they don't give them up.
trader/compliment: Zenyte, my friend! Put it away before the whole street wants one.

compliment: That bracelet burns from the inside. You wear it like it's nothing.
insult: A bracelet in torment. Wouldn't be the first thing you've upset.
remark: There's something angry in that bracelet. Can you hear it, or just me?
vicar/remark: That bracelet is in torment, traveller, and I can feel it from here.
wizard/compliment: A tormented zenyte. Whoever enchanted that knew exactly what they did.
kid/remark: Your bracelet looks angry! Why is it angry, did you forget to feed it?

compliment: That bracelet came off a revenant. Took nerve to walk out with it.
insult: A revenant's bracelet. Did they lend it to you, or did you just run?
remark: That bracelet's got a pale glow. Something from the Wilderness, that.
vicar/remark: A trinket from the Wilderness dead. Keep it off my altar, please.
guard/remark: Revenant bracelet. Been north of the ditch, then, and I've noted it.
kid/remark: Is that a ghost bracelet? Does it moan at you in the night?

compliment: Green hide bracers with the mark of Guthix. A balanced sort, are you?
insult: Guthix bracers. Sitting on the fence, and well padded for it.
remark: That's Guthix's sign on your bracers. Not many wear his colours now.
vicar/remark: Guthix's mark on your arms. He sleeps, they say, but we don't forget.
gnome/compliment: Guthix's colours, human. The forest approves, and so do I.
rough/remark: Guthix bracers, eh? Me dad kept a bit o' green by the door for him.

compliment: Saradomin's star on your bracers. The monks will like you for that.
insult: Saradomin's star on dragonhide. The lord of order, worn by a poacher.
remark: Those bracers are blessed, aren't they? Saradomin's colours, anyway.
vicar/compliment: Saradomin's star on your arms, traveller. May he steady your bow arm.
shady/insult: Saradomin's star. Of course. Your sort always needs a father watching.
kid/remark: Is that the star sign on your arms? My mum prays to him at bedtime.

compliment: Zamorak's mark on your bracers. Brave, wearing that in this town.
insult: Zamorak's colours on your arms. Best keep them away from the chapel.
remark: Red bracers with the chaos mark. The vicar's going to have a word.
vicar/insult: Zamorak's sign on your arms, in my parish, so I'll be praying for you.
shady/compliment: Zamorak's mark on your bracers. Perhaps you're not entirely hopeless.
guard/remark: Chaos mark on the bracers. Stay out of the chapel and we'll get along.

compliment: That mark on your bracers is older than any church I know of.
insult: An old god's sign on your arms. Does anyone still answer to that one?
remark: Odd sign on those bracers. I don't know it, and I know most of them.
vicar/remark: That symbol on your arms is in the oldest books, and nowhere else.
wizard/remark: The Empty Lord's mark, on dragonhide. How very little you must know.
kid/remark: What's that squiggle on your arms? Is it a secret sign for a club?

compliment: Armadyl's wings on your bracers. Fitting, for someone who draws a bow.
insult: Bird god's bracers. Do you squawk when you loose, or just flap?
remark: Those bracers have wings on them. The winged god's mark, isn't it?
vicar/remark: Armadyl's sign, traveller. He stood for justice, so mind you do too.
gnome/compliment: Armadyl's wings, human! Anything that flies has my respect.
kid/remark: There's a bird on your arms! Why doesn't it fly off, is it stuck?

compliment: Bandos's mark on your bracers. The goblins will step aside for that.
insult: The goblin god's sign, on an archer. Did you read it before buying?
remark: Those bracers carry the mark of the war god the goblins follow.
goblin/compliment: Big High War God mark! Human got good arms. Goblin not hit you today.
goblin/remark: That Bandos sign on arm. Human join which goblin tribe, then?
vicar/insult: War god's mark on your arms, traveller. I'll not be blessing those.

compliment: Hydra leather on your hands! You went to the old vault for those.
insult: Gloves from a hydra. Which head did you take them off, the clever one?
remark: Those gloves have scales. Many-headed sort of scales, by the look.
fremennik/compliment: Hydra hide on your hands, outerlander. There's a saga in those gloves.
slayer_master/compliment: Hydra leather. Not many bring that back, and fewer wear it well.
kid/compliment: Hydra gloves! How many heads did it have, and did they argue?

compliment: Those vambraces are ancient. Older than the Wilderness, I'd say.
insult: Ancient vambraces. Did you earn them, or dig them out of a tomb?
remark: Those bracers have the look of the old empire about them, don't they?
wizard/compliment: Zaryte. One does not simply find those. Someone very old gave them up.
fremennik/compliment: Vambraces like those come off a god's own guard, outerlander.
kid/remark: Your arm things look really old. Older than my nan, and she's ancient.

compliment: Those gauntlets hum like a storm about to break, and that's fine work.
insult: Gauntlets that angry deserve an owner who could sit still a minute.
remark: There's a demon's cloth in those gauntlets, or I'm no judge of cloth.
vicar/remark: Those gauntlets are stitched with something unholy, so mind the font.
wizard/compliment: Confliction gauntlets. Torment and demon tears, and it holds together.
kid/remark: Your gloves are crackling! Is there a tiny storm in there, or a demon?
shady/compliment: Demon's cloth on your hands. Perhaps your sort isn't wasted after all.

compliment: Good honest leather boots, those. They'll see you a fair few miles.
Plain leather boots never let anyone down, in my experience.
insult: Those boots have been walked in more than they've been cleaned.
Leather boots and not a scrap of armour. Off to the sheep, are you?
remark: Hope she'd approve, the cow those boots were made of.
nan/remark: Mind you oil those boots, dear, or the wet gets in.
kid/remark: Which cow did your boots come from? Was it one of the brown ones?

compliment: Metal on your feet. Sensible, with all the dropped swords about.
insult: You clank when you walk, did you know? Every step, clank, clank.
Boots that heavy, I'd have thought you'd be shorter by now.
remark: Mind the puddles in those boots, they'll rust before you're home.
dwarf/remark: Plain smithing on those boots. Honest, though, I'll give it that.
guard/remark: Heavy boots. Keep them off the flowerbeds.

compliment: Black boots go with everything, even the rest of what you've got on.
insult: Black boots. Very serious. Are you off to a funeral or to cause one?
remark: Dark boots like those don't show the mud, which I'd call a mercy.
shady/remark: Black boots. Quiet ones, I hope, for your sake.
toff/insult: Black boots on a peasant. How very funereal of you.

compliment: Climbing boots! Been up the mountain past the trolls, have you?
insult: Climbing boots in a town with no hills? Expecting a steep staircase?
remark: Those boots have a grip on them. Icy up on the plateau, I hear.
rough/remark: Them's mountain boots. Dunstan's work, by the look of the nails.
kid/remark: Can you climb walls in those boots? Go on, climb that one there!

compliment: Barely a sound from those boots, you walk like a cat in them.
insult: Light boots, are they? Shame they couldn't lighten the rest of you.
remark: Odd, that. You don't leave footprints in those boots, do you?
wizard/remark: Enchanted footwear, I see. Somebody else's enchanting, no doubt.
nan/remark: Thin little boots like that, dear, you'll feel every pebble.

compliment: Those boots came up out of the pit by the barbarians, didn't they?
insult: Smart boots. Did somebody hand them out for minding your manners?
remark: There's a hole by the barbarian village where folk come out in those.
barkeep/remark: Free, were they? Everyone round here's got a pair of them boots.
kid/compliment: I want boots like those! Did you fight a thing for them?

compliment: Smart little boots, those. Properly wizardly, I'd call them.
insult: Pointy boots and no hat, so that's half a wizard, then.
remark: Wizards never run anywhere, so I wonder what they want boots for.
wizard/insult: How delightful. Wizard boots on someone who plainly cannot spell.
kid/remark: Do your boots do magic? Make them do some magic right now!

compliment: Sensible in this heat, sandals like those from Karamja.
insult: Sandals, in this mud. Your toes will never forgive you.
remark: You can hear those sandals slapping from the far end of the street.
nan/remark: Sandals, dear? You'll catch your death with your toes out.
kid/remark: Your toes are out! I can see all of your toes!

compliment: Flippers off a mogre, I'll bet. Rather you than me in that water.
insult: Flippers on dry land. Every step's a slap, isn't it?
Were you planning to swim here, or did the boat sink?
remark: Flippers on a road. Either you're lost or the sea is.
pirate/remark: Arr, flippers. Ye'll be wanting a tide to go with those.
kid/remark: Can you swim with those? Show me, there's a pond just there!

compliment: Bear slippers! Those look cosy enough to hibernate in.
insult: Big furry paws on your feet, and still no bite to you.
remark: Bear paws on a person. The real bears will want a word.
kid/remark: Are those real bear feet? Did you take them off a bear?
nan/compliment: Ooh, bear slippers. Keep those on, dear, the floors are freezing.

compliment: Demon slippers. Red, horned, and still the cosiest thing on you.
insult: Little demon feet. Is that a warning, or a confession?
remark: Those slippers have horns. Slippers shouldn't have horns.
vicar/remark: Demonic slippers, traveller? I shall pray for your feet.
kid/remark: Your feet are demons! Do they growl at night?

compliment: Frog slippers. Green, wide, and happy. Rather like a frog, in fact.
insult: Frog slippers. Do they ribbit when you step in something?
remark: Swamp's that way, if your feet are looking for company.
kid/remark: Froggy feet! Jump like a frog, go on, a big one!
nan/remark: Frog slippers, dear? Well, if they keep your toes warm.

compliment: Jester's boots with the curly toes! You'll have the Duke in stitches.
insult: Curly-toed boots. Are you the entertainment, or just dressed as it?
remark: Those boots have bells on. I can hear you coming round corners.
toff/insult: A fool's slippers. At last, some honesty in footwear.
kid/compliment: Your boots jingle! Walk again so they do it again!

compliment: Coloured boots! Somebody's been to a proper haberdasher.
insult: Boots that colour, and you still expect people to look at your face?
remark: Soft boots like those won't stop a sword, but they do match the hat.
gnome/compliment: Fine colour, human. Rometti's work, those boots, if I'm not mistaken.
nan/remark: Pity about the mud, dear, those boots are such a lovely colour.

compliment: Curly festive slippers! You're the jolliest thing on this street.
insult: Slippers with bells on. Hard to sneak up on anyone, I'd imagine.
remark: Was it a long winter? You're still wearing the festive slippers.
kid/compliment: Elf slippers! Are you one of the little helpers with the sack?
barkeep/remark: Those slippers again. Every winter they come out, and never go back.

compliment: Gravedigger's boots. Somebody has to do it, and you look the part.
insult: Those boots have been in a grave. I'd rather not ask whose.
remark: Mind where you stand in those boots. There's something on the sole.
vicar/remark: The boots of a gravedigger. Honest work, if a quiet sort.
kid/remark: Did you dig someone up in those boots? Did they wake up and complain?

compliment: Bedsheet boots. Nobody's ever haunted a place so cheerfully.
insult: Those boots are a cut-up bedsheet. Where does the rest of you sleep?
remark: Odd place to start, a ghost from the knees down.
nan/insult: That was a good sheet before you took the scissors to it, dear.
kid/remark: Ghost feet! Wooo! Are you a ghost from the bottom up?

compliment: Lovely pointed boots. Very witchy. The toads will be impressed.
insult: Pointy boots. You could open letters with those toes.
remark: Boots that curl at the toe. I keep expecting a broomstick.
nan/compliment: Ooh, proper witch boots. I had a pair like that till the cat ate them.
kid/remark: Are you a witch? Can you turn Tom into a frog for me, please?

compliment: Big paws on those boots! Who's a very good boy, then?
insult: Paws on your feet. Do you fetch, or just dig up the garden?
remark: You'll grow into them, those paws are bigger than the rest of you.
kid/remark: Doggy feet! Do they wag, and where have you hidden the tail?
rough/remark: Dog paws on a person. My hound's not sure what to make of you.

compliment: Cat slippers! Is that Bob from Burthorpe? He'd be ever so flattered.
insult: Slippers with a cat's face. Does it purr, or just judge?
remark: Cat slippers outdoors. Slippers are an indoor thing, surely.
kid/compliment: Kitty slippers! Can I stroke them, just the one, just a little?
nan/remark: Cat slippers, dear. Mind the real ones don't get jealous.

compliment: Cow slippers! Those look soft enough to milk.
insult: Slippers with horns. Even your feet are looking for a fight.
remark: Cow slippers. The cows in the field are giving you a very long look.
kid/remark: Moo! Your feet go moo! Make them do it, make them moo!
rough/remark: Cow slippers. Don't let the farmer see, he'll count them.

compliment: Gardening boots. Someone keeps a tidy allotment, I'll bet.
insult: Gardening boots and no spade. Were the weeds too much for you?
remark: Farmer, are you? Those boots have proper soil on them, not road mud.
nan/compliment: Gardening boots! You'll come and see to my roses, won't you, dear?
rough/remark: Them's my boots, or near enough. Where'd you get them, then?

compliment: Those desert boots have had a hard life. So have you, by the look.
remark: There's sand coming out of those boots with every step.
trader/remark: Nasty places, desert mines. Those boots came out of one, I'd wager.

compliment: Plain shoes, well kept. You can't say fairer than that.
insult: Only shoes? Not boots or sandals, just a pair of shoes on a road.
remark: Those shoes look like they belong in somebody's hallway.
nan/remark: Indoor shoes, dear. Your mother will be wondering where they went.
kid/remark: Those are house shoes! Did you walk out of your house in them?

compliment: Good boots, those, and the smith who shaped them knew their trade.
insult: Boots like those and you still walk like your feet hurt.
remark: You can tell a man by his boots, they say, and yours say 'heavy'.
dwarf/compliment: Decent metal on those boots. Somebody tempered it right.
guard/remark: Armoured boots. Don't go kicking any doors with them.

compliment: Rune boots. That blue-green shine is hard to miss, isn't it?
insult: Fine rune boots, and the rest of you looks borrowed.
remark: Those boots cost more than my roof, I shouldn't wonder.
dwarf/compliment: Rune, those. Hard stuff to work. Somebody earned their beer.
kid/remark: Your boots are shiny! Are they made of treasure?

compliment: White boots, kept white. The knights would approve of you.
insult: Give it an hour, white boots on a road like this.
remark: Falador make, those boots. The White Knights wear the same.
guard/remark: Falador issue, are they? Keep those white boots clean on my street.
vicar/compliment: White boots. A little purity goes a long way, traveller.

compliment: Snakeskin boots. Somebody got the better of a very big snake.
insult: Scaly boots. I'd check they haven't started hissing at you.
remark: Those boots are still shedding, I think. There's bits on the floor.
pirate/remark: Arr, snake boots. Karamja snakes, by the pattern.
kid/remark: Is that a real snake on your feet? Does it still bite people?

compliment: Clever stuff, that. Bark boots, like the wizards wear.
insult: Boots made of bark. Do they creak when you walk, or is that you?
remark: Those boots were a tree once. Woodcutters must find that funny.
wizard/remark: Splitbark, properly bound. Someone paid a wizard for that, I expect.
gnome/remark: Bark on your feet, human? The trees won't thank you.

compliment: Soft mystic boots. You've the look of someone who actually studies.
insult: Lovely wizard's boots. Have you read the books that go with them?
remark: Those boots are trimmed like the ones in the Wizards' Guild.
wizard/insult: Mystic boots. The first thing an apprentice buys, the last they earn.
kid/remark: Are those magic boots? Fly a bit for me, just a little bit!

compliment: Shell boots. That came off something nasty from the sea, didn't it?
insult: Boots made of shell. Mind the gulls, they'll think you're dinner.
remark: Heavy going, those. Dagannoth shell, unless I'm mistaken.
fremennik/compliment: Dagannoth shell on your feet, outerlander. You've been in the caves.
rough/remark: Can't say I mind it, them boots smelling of the sea.

compliment: Spined boots, with the spikes still on. Somebody tanned those well.
insult: Spikes on your boots. Are they for enemies or for stairs?
remark: Don't cross your legs, those boots have spines on them.
fremennik/remark: Spined hide, outerlander. Those came from the Waterbirth caves.
kid/remark: Your boots have spikes! Can you kick a wall with them?

compliment: Bone boots. Grim, but somebody fitted them beautifully.
insult: Boots made of bones. Whose, and did they mind?
remark: Bones on your feet. The gravediggers will think you're competition.
vicar/remark: Bones should be buried, traveller, not laced up.
kid/remark: Skeleton feet! Are you a skeleton all the way up underneath?

compliment: Granite boots. You must have legs like a troll's.
insult: Stone boots. Is that for stamping, or because you can't lift them?
remark: Every step you take in those boots shakes my teeth.
dwarf/compliment: Granite, cut for feet. That's a stonemason's work, that.
troll/remark: Rock feet. Good rock, heavy rock.
kid/remark: Are your boots made of rock? Can I stand on them and be taller?

compliment: Moonclan boots, aren't they? There's a lovely blue to them.
insult: Boots from the Moon Clan. Did you dream them, or buy them?
remark: Those boots look like Lunar Isle work. That's a long way from here.
wizard/remark: Lunar boots. Dream magic, that lot. Not quite my sort of thing.
fremennik/insult: Moon Clan boots, outerlander? Keep that nonsense off our isles.

compliment: Holy sandals. Blessed feet, blessed roads, I always say.
insult: Holy sandals, in this muck. Even faith has its limits.
remark: Monk's sandals. Did you walk all the way from the monastery in those?
vicar/compliment: Blessed sandals, traveller. Saradomin smile on where they carry you.
kid/remark: Are those holy? If I step on your foot do I get blessed?

compliment: Spiked manacles on your ankles. You look like you mean it.
insult: Spikes round your ankles. Did you escape, or get dressed?
remark: Those spikes on your ankles. Mind you don't cut your own leg off.
guard/remark: Manacles. Did you take those off a prisoner, or are you one?
shady/compliment: Spiked manacles. Someone's been in a dungeon, and not as a visitor.

compliment: Stone-soled boots. You've been down where the floor burns, I'd guess.
insult: Rocky soles. Walk softer, you're wearing a path into my floor.
remark: Those soles are stone. Hot ground wherever you've come from.
dwarf/remark: Stone soles. Clever, for walking where the rock runs hot.
kid/remark: Are those rock shoes? Do you sink if you swim?

compliment: Thick wellies. Dry feet in any weather, that's the dream.
insult: Wellies! Are you off to the fields, or just expecting rain?
remark: Rubber boots like those are for the puddles, or for the eels.
rough/compliment: Proper wellies, them. You've had wet feet before, I can tell.
nan/remark: Wellies, dear. Good. Nobody listens when I tell them about wet socks.

compliment: Been in the Rift, I see. Those boots have the great eye on them.
insult: Boots with an eye on them. Do they watch where you're going for you?
remark: The runecrafters' guardians wear that sort of thing, they say.
wizard/remark: Boots from the Rift guardians. Runecraft work, that, not real magic.
kid/remark: Your boots have an eye! Make it blink at me, go on!

compliment: Smith's boots, and worn in. You've stood at an anvil, I can tell.
insult: A smith's boots, but the hands of someone who's never held a hammer.
remark: Those boots are the Foundry sort. They look a size too small.
dwarf/compliment: Foundry boots. Good. Only a smith should wear a smith's boots.
rough/remark: Smith's boots, eh? Mind the sparks, they'll find the gap.

compliment: Forester's boots. You've been among the trees a while, haven't you?
insult: Woodsman's boots, and no splinters? Then you haven't been working.
remark: Those boots have bark on them. You've been in the woods.
gnome/compliment: A friend of the trees, human? Those boots rather say so.
rough/remark: Forester's boots. Good. The trees want looking after.

compliment: Soft-footed hunter's boots. Nothing hears you coming in those.
insult: Hunter's boots. What did you catch, besides a cold?
remark: Varlamore make, those boots. The hunters' guild sort, I think.
rough/remark: Hunter's boots. Keep off my chickens with those, that's all.
kid/remark: Are you a hunter? Go and catch a dragon so I can see it!

compliment: Been out past the storm? Those angler's wellies have a shine to them.
insult: Fancy wellies for a fisherman. Did the fish ask for a dress code?
remark: Angler's boots, those, but stranger than the usual sort.
pirate/remark: Arr, them boots have been through the big storm off the reef.
rough/compliment: Angler's wellies, and good ones. You've pulled some nets, I'd say.

compliment: Fine hunting, that. Hide boots stitched from three beasts at least.
insult: Boots made from several animals. Couldn't decide which one?
remark: Those boots are a patchwork of hides. Antelope in there, I think.
rough/remark: Mixed hides, them. Somebody's been busy with a spear.
kid/remark: How many animals are your boots? Count them for me, all of them!

compliment: Those shoes are the vyre style. You've walked in dark places.
insult: Vampyre shoes on someone that pale. Trying to blend in, were you?
remark: Meiyerditch shoes, those. Pointed, and not for dancing.
vicar/remark: Vyre finery, traveller? I hope it was worn for a good reason.
shady/compliment: Vyre shoes. Someone's been walking among the Drakans' kin.

compliment: Heavy war boots, those. Took them off one of Bandos's own, I'll bet.
insult: Who did you stamp? Those boots are made for stamping ogres.
remark: Those boots came out of the frozen temple in the north, didn't they?
goblin/compliment: Big High War God boots! You stamp good, you strong.
dwarf/remark: Heavy plate on those boots. Ogre work, not dwarf work.

compliment: Black stone set in your boots. You've been up the Slayer Tower roof.
insult: Yet here you are, in boots that heavy. I'd have thought you'd sink.
remark: Tourmaline, is it, that dark stone through your boots?
dwarf/compliment: Black tourmaline in a boot. Somebody knew what they were doing.
kid/remark: Your boots have a black rock in! Where did you get the rock?

compliment: A crystal that size in your boots. Varlamore's arena, was it?
insult: Crystal in your boots. Do they sing, or sulk when you kick things?
remark: Heavy as a gatepost, those stony boots with the crystal in.
wizard/remark: Crystal set in stone, worn on the feet. Such a waste of good crystal.
kid/remark: Crystal feet! Does it glow in the dark when you take them off?

compliment: Dragon boots with fire in them. You've been somewhere terrible.
insult: Burning boots. Shame the rest of you's a damp squib.
remark: Keep off the thatch, those boots glow at the seams.
dwarf/compliment: Dragon metal with a crystal worked in. By Guthix, that's smithing.
kid/remark: Your boots are on fire! Do they hurt, or are you used to it?

compliment: Winged boots! You walk like your feet barely touch the ground.
insult: Wings on your boots and you still took the long way round.
remark: Those boots have little wings. Do they help, or just flap?
toff/compliment: Winged boots, citizen. One hears they're rather dear these days.
kid/remark: Your boots have wings! So why aren't you flying about, then?

compliment: Those boots hum, faintly. Fine magic in them, I'd say.
insult: Enchanted boots. So the magic's in the feet, is it, and not the head?
remark: Dark boots with a glow to them. From the cold north, I'd guess.
wizard/compliment: Now those are properly enchanted boots. Rare to see them worn well.
kid/remark: Your boots are glowing! Is that allowed, or will the guards come?

compliment: Demon-forged boots. Those came from somewhere I'd not go.
insult: Fine demon boots. Pity they can't walk you out of trouble.
remark: Those boots were made somewhere a long way below, I'd say.
vicar/remark: Demon-made boots, traveller. I'd keep them off the chapel floor.
shady/compliment: Avernic work on your feet. You've been where the fires are.

compliment: Infinity boots. The mages at the arena wear those, don't they?
insult: Wizard's boots with the fancy pattern. Still just socks with ambition.
remark: Those boots have the old pattern on. From the mages' arena, I think.
wizard/insult: Infinity boots. Earned at the arena, or bought from someone who did?
kid/remark: Swirly boots! Are those magic swirls?

compliment: Drake claw worked into stone boots. You've been under the volcano.
insult: Boots with claws on. Do they scratch the floor, or just scare it?
remark: Karuulm, is it? Those boots smell of sulphur from here.
dwarf/remark: Stone soles with a drake's claw. Clever, if you like the heat.
kid/remark: Claws on your boots! Did a dragon give them to you?

compliment: Blessed sandals with a drake's tooth. Faith with teeth, that is.
insult: Does the monastery know about the tooth on your holy sandals?
remark: Strange pairing, that. Holy sandals with something clawed on them.
vicar/remark: A drake's tooth on blessed sandals. Unusual, but I'll not judge.
kid/remark: There's a tooth on your shoe! Whose tooth is it, and did they mind?

compliment: Rune boots set with dragonstones. That's a lot of purple to walk on.
insult: Jewelled boots. Are those for walking, or for keeping in a case?
remark: Those boots have gems in. You'll lose one in a drain, mark my words.
toff/compliment: Dragonstone on the feet. Finally, someone with taste in this town.
kid/remark: Purple stones in your boots! Can I have one, just a little one?

compliment: Spider-silk boots. Took those from the araxytes, I'd wager.
insult: Hairy boots. Did you make them, or did they make themselves?
remark: Little hairs on those boots. Spider, I think, so I'll stand over here.
kid/remark: Spider boots! Can they climb walls? Climb that wall over there!
nan/remark: Spidery boots, dear. I'll not have those in my kitchen.

compliment: Ranger boots. Half the archers in Gielinor want a pair of those.
insult: Ranger boots. All that fuss for a pair of green slippers.
remark: Those green boots are the archers' sort. Quiet on the grass, those.
toff/compliment: Ranger boots. Quite the little fortune on your feet, citizen.
kid/remark: Green boots! Are you a ranger? Shoot something for me, go on!

compliment: Wild, twisted-looking boots, those. Where did you earn them, then?
insult: Those boots look like they've been through a storm and lost.
remark: Odd boots, those. A relic hunter's, by the look of them.
pirate/remark: Arr, twisted boots. Seen a few come back with those from far off.
kid/remark: Your boots are all twisty! Did a wizard do that to them on purpose?

compliment: Those boots have flames up the sides. You've blazed a trail somewhere.
insult: Fiery boots. Shame the pace doesn't match the paintwork.
remark: Orange as a sunset, those relic hunter's boots.
kid/remark: Fire boots! Do they burn the grass when you stand still?
barkeep/remark: Blazing boots, eh? Seen a few of those come through, all in a hurry.

compliment: Crystal shards all over those boots. They catch the light beautifully.
insult: Broken crystal on your boots. Did you drop something, or step in it?
remark: Mind the children, with those shards all over your boots.
wizard/remark: Shattered relic work. Somebody's been poking at old things.
kid/remark: Your boots are all pointy bits! Are they as sharp as they look?

compliment: Dark blue and gold on those boots. Smart as a guard captain's.
insult: Gilded boots on a pair of feet that still trip on cobbles.
toff/compliment: Blue and gold boots, citizen. Almost regal, and I do mean almost.
kid/remark: Gold on your boots! Is it real gold, and can I scrape some off?

compliment: Those boots glow like coals. You've been somewhere loud.
insult: Smouldering boots and not a flicker of hurry about you.
remark: Keep them off the straw, those glowing red relic hunter's boots.
kid/remark: Your boots are angry! Why are your boots angry?
rough/remark: Them boots look hot. Don't bring them in the hay barn.

compliment: Gold on steel, those boots. You dug them up somewhere, didn't you?
insult: Ornate boots on an ordinary walk. The boots are doing all the work.
remark: Too fine for a road, those boots. Dug up, I'd guess, not bought.
toff/compliment: Ornate boots. At last, a peasant who's found some gold and worn it.
dwarf/remark: Pretty, but it'll chip, that gold inlay on your boots.

compliment: Blessed mole slippers. Now I've seen everything, and it's furry.
insult: A mole, with a halo, on your feet. The vicar will want a word.
remark: Mole fur on holy sandals. Somebody had a strange afternoon.
vicar/remark: Sanctified moles, traveller? I'm not sure the church has a view.
kid/compliment: Holy mole feet! Are the moles angels now?

compliment: Polished dress shoes. Somebody's off to a ball.
insult: Dress shoes on a muddy road. The ball's that way, I think.
remark: Shiny shoes. Where's the dinner, and am I invited?
toff/compliment: Proper dress shoes. There's hope for the peasantry yet.
barkeep/remark: Dress shoes. Not in here you're not, I've just done the floor.

alliance/compliment: Here, that's the Obligator. No, don't point, they'll see.
The Obligator, walking through the lobby. Didn't think I'd see it.
With that mace about the camp, I sleep easier in this cavern.
alliance/insult: All this guarding, and the big mace walks off with a passer-by.
Do mind the camp with that mace. We've only just put it up.
Shards and runes to keep it fed? That mace eats better than we do.
alliance/remark: Here, don't stare, but that's the mace everyone down here is after.
Mind that mace on the bridge. They've not finished it yet.
So that's an Obligator. Bigger than I'd pictured, I'll say that.
compliment: A mace on a vine! You'd get a fair old swing out of that.
I'd keep you between me and the goblins, with that mace about.
Ooh, that mace. I'd move my cart for you, and gladly.
insult: Is that a mace, or a marrow that's gone off on the vine?
Looks like a thistle that's got out of hand, that mace.
Mace on a vine. Next it'll be swords on bits of string.
remark: I've a vine like that out the back. Nothing on the end of it, mind.
Keep that mace away from the goats. They'll have the vine.
Looks like a seed pod, that mace. A very cross seed pod.

alliance/compliment: Both crossbows at once. I can barely manage a teacup in each hand.
Crystal crossbows out of our archive. You've earned your keep.
I've seen soldiers fumble with one crossbow, and you've two.
alliance/insult: Crossbows like those deserve a marksman. Still, here you are.
If one crossbow misses, I suppose the other's there to apologise.
You wave those crossbows about like a pair of spoons.
alliance/remark: Crystal crossbows, both of them. Must be like holding ice.
Do those crossbows take turns? They look like they take turns.
Mind where those crossbows point. I've only the one hat.
compliment: A crossbow in each hand. I can't manage one bucket.
Fair play, aiming two crossbows. I'd only shoot my own foot.
Two crossbows, and both of them lovely. Greedy, but lovely.
insult: Brought a spare crossbow, in case the first one sulks.
One crossbow's a weapon. Two's just showing off.
Shame they don't make a third crossbow. You've a foot spare.
remark: Green as the sea, those crossbows. Fished them up, did you?
Is it two crossbows, or one that's come in half?
Old crystal, those crossbows, or I'm a goblin.

alliance/compliment: Not many could carry that tome open all day and keep their temper.
Wise choice, that tome. A book never needs sharpening.
You hold that tome like a scholar and walk like a soldier.
alliance/insult: All the knowledge in that tome, and it ended up with you.
That ribbon in your tome marks a page you'll never get to, I expect.
That tome casts its own spells? Then what are you there for?
alliance/remark: Astral runes for every spell from that tome, I'm told. Costly reading.
Big book, that. Any good bits in it, or is it all footnotes?
Is that tome open at a good page, or just where it fell?
compliment: A book that size, carried open. You must read quick.
Big book, open in both arms... must be a good bit, that.
Never had the patience for a book that thick myself.
insult: Both arms full of book. What if somebody hands you a pie?
That book's bigger than your head. Hard to say which has more in it.
You carry that book like a maid with a tray of soup.
remark: Both arms round that book, like it might run off.
Can't read myself, but I know a big book when I see one.
What's in a book that size, I wonder? Recipes, I'd hope.

alliance/compliment: Even down here in the dark, that shield shines.
Old icyene work, that shield, and it's found the right arm.
That gold star on your shield catches every lamp in the cavern.
alliance/insult: Another shiny shield. Never once a shiny shovel, mind.
Some of us build the camp. Others polish round shields.
There goes a very fine shield, with somebody attached.
alliance/remark: Finely made, that round shield. Wonder whose arm it was made for.
Lean that shield by the bank if you like. Nobody'll touch it.
That shield's more silver than I've seen since I came down here.
compliment: A gold star on your shield! You'll not get lost at night.
I do like a round shield. Fits the arm, a round one.
That shield'd look well over a fireplace, if you ever retire.
insult: A star on your shield. Did you get it for good behaviour?
Not a scratch on that shield. Been keeping out of trouble, have we?
Very pretty shield. I'm sure the trolls will admire it.
remark: Funny, a star on a shield. I'd have gone for a dragon.
Round as a cheese, that shield. A very shiny cheese.
Seems a shame to let anything hit a shield like that.

alliance/compliment: An archivist's cape on a defender. That's how it ought to be.
Good, that cape again. We're in safe hands today.
Not a cape you buy, that. Only earned, and only down here.
alliance/insult: Archivists wore that cape with ink on their fingers. You've mud.
In that cape, the archive ought to be charging you rent.
Much longer down here and that cape of yours will put down roots.
alliance/remark: Archivists' cape, and not a quill in sight. Times change.
Back again in that cape? The kettle's barely cold from last time.
What does the engraving on your cape say? Can't read it from here.
compliment: Nice to see a green cape. Everyone's in red or black these days.
Ooh, a green cape. Cheers the street up no end.
You'd never lose that green cape in the snow, would you?
insult: Bold, that one, wearing a green cape so near the cabbages.
Lovely cape. The caterpillars will be very pleased.
Mind you don't stand still in that green cape. Someone'll water you.
remark: I had a cape near that green once. The moths had it.
My washing line's got a green sheet just like that cape.
That green cape'll not show the grass stains, at least.
